sessions.title: Making “Works on All Machines” Work for Agent Environments
sessions.description:
Agentic development environments need a lot of things - the project, agent harnesses, vector stores, compile tools, and more. And on top of that, it needs to be a trusted and safe environment in case an agent goes off-script. But, how?

This talk will dive deep on how to create and customize the sandbox environments for your agent, from the simple to the very complex. You'll also learn how to version control and share the environment through your codebase, ensuring everyone on your team has consistency in both environments and trust. The best part? It's not as hard as you think!

sessions.title: SBX 101: Hands-on with Docker Sandboxes
sessions.description: Modern AI agents are useful because they take real actions in the real world and on your machine: read files, run commands, hit the web, build containers, write and publish code. That capability is also where the risk lives. This hands-on workshop walks through the Docker AI primitives (sandboxes, network policy, MCP, hardened images, sbx kits, and multi-agent orchestration with Docker Agent) that make it practical to give an agent real capability without giving it unbounded reach. You'll spin up your first Docker Sandbox, prove its isolation guarantees with hands-on tests, govern its outbound network, attach real tools via MCP, harden the containers it ships, package the whole setup as a reusable kit, and finally compose a small multi-agent team where per-role tool scoping is enforced at the runtime. You'll leave with a working mental model of scoped autonomy and a running sandbox stack on your machine that you can keep experimenting with.

sessions.title: Local AI Workshop for Beginners: Private ChatGPT Experience on Your Own Computer
sessions.description:
Ever feel uncomfortable about sharing too much personal info with ChatGPT/Gemini/Claude but still want AI’s help? Against giving Big Tech your private life on a golden platter running on wasteful resource-sucking data centers? A bit confused about some of the jargon and words used in news articles about the next most powerful AI models coming out? This workshop is for you!

​Earlier this year there was a breakthrough - we can now run AI that are more than capable of being private and even completely offline assistants on personal computers and laptops!

​This is also a workshop for AI beginners who find setting up agents with OpenClaw too intimidating but still want a capable AI experience like ChatGPT that keeps all private information on their own computers - without writing any code or running any terminal/command line commands!

​What we'll cover:
​Setting up Unsloth Desktop (open source ChatGPT-like interface) and running powerful open source AI models of your choosing on your own computer.

​Learning important concepts about running AI on your own computer - from why open source AI exists to tokens, context, model quantization, MCP tool servers, and more.

​Answering your questions to make sure you're confident discussing AI model concepts and the major news developments that are shaking the world.

​System Requirements: The more RAM your computer has, the better. It’s now possible to run near-frontier-capable-AI on computers with just 16GB of RAM. That said, even if your computer has less than that (like 8GB), you can run less powerful AI that is still impressive and are welcome to attend!

​To be efficient, we encourage participants to download and install Unsloth Desktop (https://unsloth.ai/docs/desktop) as well as let it automatically download a suitable AI model it selects for you (if any) when first running the app in advance before coming to the event. During the event, you’ll learn how to find even better AI models to add to your Unsloth Desktop setup.

speakers.bio: Jason Stine is actually in no way related to Unsloth. He's just a passionate AI hobbyist who enjoys mentoring others and found that Unsloth Desktop was the most straightforward software for this workshop. He's a fullstack web developer (software engineer) who uses Cursor AI every day at work.

sessions.title: Agents That Own Their Inference: Building Production AI Agents on Dedicated GPUs
sessions.description:
Every production agent today is renting its intelligence. You're paying per token, sending your customer's data to someone else's servers, and hoping the provider doesn't rate-limit you during your launch. For most teams, that's fine. But for a growing number of teams in regulated industries, with high-volume products, latency-sensitive workloads, or rising token bills, it's starting to look like a liability.

In this 120-minute hands-on workshop you'll get a dedicated GPU and build an agent that runs on infrastructure you control. You'll stand up vLLM, point your agent at it, and drive concurrent load through the stack until you can see batching, KV cache pressure, and throughput limits in the metrics. Then you'll optimize the deployment to improve throughput while keeping per-request latency in line.

The focus isn't agent frameworks. It's the inference layer underneath them. You'll leave with working code and a real understanding of continuous batching under real concurrency, KV cache tradeoffs, vLLM's metrics, and the bottlenecks that only show up when you operate the inference server yourself.

speakers.bio: I’m a Software Engineer at Akamai working on managed Kubernetes platform infrastructure. I work on cloud-controller-manager, CSI drivers, Cluster API Provider Linode, and Karpenter-related autoscaling work. I’m interested in Kubernetes infrastructure for AI inference, especially GPU startup paths, model serving, and cost-aware scaling. Outside work, I experiment with inference on personal GPU hardware and Kubernetes clusters.

Sheilah is a software engineer–turned developer advocate focused on  AI infrastructure and inference engineering. She is passionate about helping developers understand the systems behind deploying AI applications, while continuously learning and exploring the rapidly evolving AI landscape herself.

sessions.title: Architecting Multi-Agent Teams: Mastering the Orchestration Patterns of ADK 2
sessions.description:
This hands-on workshop covers the primary orchestration patterns in ADK 2: graph workflows, collaborative agent teams, and dynamic (LLM-shaped) workflows. You will learn to construct architectures that combine parallel fan-out with join nodes, deterministic code-level routers that branch without extra model calls, collaborative supervisor-specialist teams executing dynamic parallel subsets, and recursive execution flows. You will conclude with a decision matrix for selecting and composing these patterns.

 - Identify the correct orchestration pattern based on structural problem constraints.
 - Construct graph-based, collaborative, and dynamic workflows using ADK 2 primitives.
 - Reduce latency and token consumption by offloading branching decisions from the model to code-level logic.

sessions.title: Docker does that? Five Docker capabilities you did not know about
sessions.description:
Most developers use Docker to package and ship an app, and that answer was complete five years ago. The toolchain has grown a lot. This talk walks through a normal working day and shows where the newer pieces fit.

- Docker Sandboxes provide a trust boundary around your agents, protecting your filesystem, network access, and credentials.
- Gordon, Docker's built-in AI agent, sits right in the CLI and Desktop, ask it questions about your images, containers, best practices, and let it run the actions for you.
- Testcontainers put a real database inside your test suite so you can stop maintaining mocks or using shared infrastructure.
- Your base images can arrive already patched with Docker Hardened Images.
- Docker Scout helps you know what's in your images and even run policy evaluations to ensure your images meet the mark.

Everything in the talk is free to use, and most of it is already installed as part of your existing Docker setup.

Attendees will leave with practical guidance for identifying opportunities for canvas extensions and designing experiences that make Copilot more useful, actionable, and connected to the tools customers already rely on.

sessions.title: The AI-Ready Developer Environment — Local Setup, Reproducibility, and Docker
sessions.description:
Modern AI development adds a new layer of complexity to the development environment: agent harnesses, agent-specific developer tooling, MCP servers, external services, credentials, and more. And every team has different requirements. How do you give developers and agents the tools they need while keeping environments consistent, reproducible, and secure?

In this hands-on session, you'll start with Docker Sandboxes and then go deeper into customizing and sharing sandbox-based development environments. You'll create sbx kits to tailor the tools and configuration available inside a sandbox, connect to external services—including those that require secure credential injection—and package those customizations for reuse.

You'll then use sbxenv, which brings a Docker Compose-like experience to sandboxes, to define an entire development environment as configuration. By the end, you'll have an environment that can be shared with your team and started with a single command—giving every developer and agent a consistent, ready-to-use workspace.

sessions.title: DeepAgents: Build Multi-Agent AI Systems That Actually Work
sessions.description:
We've taught LangChain and LangGraph multi-agent workshops at Grace Hopper two years running to 200+ developers each time. The number one question we get after every session: "This works in a demo — but how do I get past the walls when I try to scale it?"
We know those walls firsthand. We've built agentic AI systems across POCs and production in global banking — and between us, we've hit every failure mode: agents losing context mid-task, orchestration logic that doesn't survive real workloads, and delegation patterns that look clean on a whiteboard but collapse under pressure.
DeepAgents is a new LangChain framework built to solve exactly these problems — intelligent delegation, advanced planning, robust context preservation, and error recovery designed for production-grade workflows. In this 120-minute hands-on workshop, we'll build a real multi-agent system together in GitHub Codespaces — no setup, no installs, just code.
Through guided labs, you'll architect a coordinator that delegates research to one agent, analysis to another, and synthesis to a third. You'll implement human-in-the-loop approval gates, long-term memory, and the error recovery patterns that separate prototypes from systems that survive production. We'll be honest about what's battle-tested and what's cutting-edge — because that's the conversation practitioners actually need.
What you'll walk away with: a portfolio-ready multi-agent system you built yourself, production skills across backends, subagents, coordinators, memory, and debugging, a complete code repository with reusable templates and documentation you can extend immediately, and the framework decision-making to know when LangChain chains, LangGraph, or DeepAgents is the right tool for your problem.
Bring a GitHub account and a browser. Leave with production-tested patterns.

sessions.title: Build a Human + AI Agent Team in tools like Slack, Teams and Discord.
sessions.description:
AI agents are getting better at doing work, but most still work alone, separated from the people and other agents they need to collaborate with.

In this hands-on workshop, you’ll use Switch to bring AI agents from Claude Code, OpenAI, Google ADK, LangChain and other frameworks into Slack, Microsoft Teams, Discord and other collaboration platforms, where humans and agents can work together with shared context, history and resources.

You’ll build a working human + agent team, assign specialized agents to real tasks, hand work between people and agents, and see how context stays with the work even as agents, models and teammates change.

Switch is free, open source and vendor agnostic, so you can use the agents and tools you already have without migrating your team to a new platform or committing to a single model or framework.

By the end of the workshop, you’ll have a working human + agent workspace you can continue using and adapting to your own projects.

sessions.title: Building an AI-Native Development Workflow
sessions.description:
AI is changing more than how we write code. It’s changing how we build software. As GitHub Copilot evolves beyond code completion into an intelligent collaborator, developers and organizations have an opportunity to rethink how they work. 

In this session, we’ll explore how AI can support the software development lifecycle, from planning and implementation to testing, documentation, and code reviews. We’ll discuss context engineering, intentional AI adoption, and how teams can create effective collaboration between developers and AI while maintaining the right balance of automation and human judgment.

speakers.bio:

She works with enterprise engineering teams to develop AI adoption strategies, deliver technical enablement, and build practical guidance that helps organizations integrate AI into their software development lifecycle.
Vanessa specializes in AI collaboration, agentic workflows, and context engineering, helping teams move beyond using AI as a coding assistant to building sustainable, AI-native engineering practices. Her work focuses on enabling developers and organizations to effectively combine human expertise with AI while maintaining governance, code quality, and engineering best practices.
Drawing from real-world enterprise experience, Vanessa has designed and delivered workshops, technical trainings, and enablement programs for organizations adopting GitHub Copilot. She is passionate about making emerging AI capabilities approachable and actionable, giving teams practical strategies they can immediately apply to improve developer productivity and software delivery.

sessions.description: When an agent chooses your dependencies and assembles your build, answering what you are actually shipping gets genuinely hard. sessions.description: Learn to Cloud is a free, open-source alternative to paid cloud bootcamps. In this talk, we'll open up our repos and show what's actually in them: agent skills that encode our production runbooks, custom agents that review security and drive browser QA, agentic workflows that keep content current, and more. sessions.title: Lean Intelligence: Lessons from GitHub Copilot Data Science Efforts

Behind every suggestion, chat response, and agentic action are countless decisions about which model or subagent to invoke, how long to let it run, and when the answer is already good enough. This talk shares lessons from the Code|AI research team's work on making the Copilot harness leaner without sacrificing quality. We'll dig into the experimentation, evaluation, and data science that helped us find and validate meaningful efficiency gains at scale.

If evals, experimentation, and data science are your jam, this one's for you.

sessions.title: Docker's Agentic Platform: Sandboxes, MCP, and the Infrastructure of Autonomous Development
sessions.description: AI agents are only as capable as the environment they're allowed to act in. This session introduces Docker's purpose-built platform tools for agentic development — the infrastructure layer that lets autonomous systems do real work, safely and reliably. We'll dive into Docker Sandboxes, which give agents secure, isolated execution environments where they can write and run code, interact with filesystems, and test outcomes without risk to your host system or production infrastructure. We'll also explore Docker's MCP toolkit, which provides agents with a standardized way to discover and invoke trusted tools. Together, these tools form the foundation of a trustworthy agentic platform: one where autonomous processes have exactly the access they need, and every action is contained, observable, and repeatable. Leave this session ready to wire Docker into your AI agent stack as the execution layer your agents can depend on.

sessions.title: Doors open - Day 1
Official Opening of WeAreDevelopers World Congress: North America
Manufacturing trust: speed and safety in the age of agents
sessions.description:
Agents have made building software faster, but infrastructure has to catch up.
In the world we now live in, developers review code they did not write, or don’t review it at all. An agent can generate and execute changes faster than any person or team can inspect them. And while prompts and skills can steer an agent, they cannot guarantee trust.
For decades, we established trust in software through people and process: shared context, code review, CI, and ownership, all of which run at human speed. Agents do not. If a person has to watch every step, the agent is not autonomous, and most of the promised speed disappears. Trust has to move into the system itself.
Mark Cavage, President and COO of Docker, makes the case for enforceable boundaries around nondeterministic agents. When you can’t inherit trust, you have to manufacture it. That means isolating where agents run, limiting what they can reach, recording what they do, and making failures reproducible. These controls are not the price of moving fast. They are what let you move fast without losing control.
The test for an agent platform is simple: Does security hold when the prompt does not? Can you audit what happened? Can you switch models and tools without rebuilding the trust layer? The goal is not to trust the agent. It is to trust the system around it enough to close your laptop, while the work continues.

speakers.bio: Mark Cavage is President of Docker. Over a 25-year career spanning AWS, Oracle, Heroku, Stripe, and Docker, he has moved from senior and principal engineer to engineering leader to business leader. That arc gives him a perspective few executives have: he has written the systems, led the teams building them, and run the businesses that depend on them. Today, Mark is leading Docker through the shift to agentic software development, helping more than 20 million developers give AI agents real autonomy while keeping control of their code, credentials, and infrastructure.

Each component shapes the final experience: how quickly a system responds, how reliably it performs, where data lives, and how easily developers can build with it. sessions.title: From Static Rules to Reasoning Platforms: Scaling Intelligent Canary Delivery in 2026
sessions.description:
As organizations scale their Kubernetes footprint, the "Day 2" reality of GitOps becomes clear: static thresholds are brittle. Standard Canary rollouts rely on fixed Prometheus queries (e.g., Error Rate < 1%), but these rules lack the context to distinguish between a minor transient blip and a systemic failure. For Platform Engineers, this results in "Alert Fatigue" and manual "promotion" gates that slow down the delivery pipeline.
In 2026, we are moving from Static Automation to Reasoning Platforms.
This session explores how to evolve your delivery infrastructure into an intelligent system that doesn't just follow rules, but reasons through data. We will demonstrate how to wrap ArgoCD Rollouts with an Agentic Reasoning Layer capable of cross-referencing metrics, logs, and distributed traces to make autonomous "Go/No-Go" decisions.

We will trigger a Canary deployment that passes basic health checks but introduces a "silent failure" (e.g., a cache hit-rate drop causing downstream latency). You will see the Reasoning Platform detect the anomaly, pause the rollout, "investigate" the root cause, and present a natural-language justification for the automated rollback.

As a CNCF Ambassador and TAG DevEx co-chair, Daniel actively shapes the cloud native ecosystem, fostering partnerships between enterprise developers, AI engineers, and platform engineering teams to accelerate hybrid cloud adoption. sessions.title: Reading the Mind of Your NGINX Fleet: A Hybrid Rule + ML Pipeline for NGINX Config Intelligence
sessions.description:
Every NGINX config encodes intent — is this a reverse proxy? an API gateway? an SSL terminator? — but that intent is never written down. At fleet scale, nobody can tell you what your configs actually do. This session shows how we taught a machine to read them.
We classify NGINX server configs into eight canonical roles using a three-stage pipeline: parse the raw config into a structured directive tree with CrossPlane, then run two complementary classifiers against it — a precision-tuned rule engine that abstains when signatures are ambiguous, and an ML model that generalizes to configs the rules don't cover. A confidence-fusion layer blends them, auto-accepting confident calls and routing borderline ones to expert review.
The counterintuitive lesson: we deliberately didn't just throw an LLM at this. The hybrid beats either approach alone — keeping rule-level precision while recovering the coverage rules lack. You'll see why "negative evidence" (the absence of a directive) is often the strongest signal, how an LLM-as-judge eval validated the design, and how a closed expert-feedback loop turns review hours into measurable accuracy gains. Live, against real configs — including yours, if you bring one.

sessions.title: AI Decision Observability: Enabling Transparency and Trust in Intelligent Systems
sessions.description:
Artificial Intelligence (AI) now drives decisions across enterprise operations, for autonomous systems—yet much of this decision-making remains a “black box.” AI Decision Observability is an emerging paradigm that transforms opaque model behavior into traceable, explainable, and auditable decision pathways. This session introduces a unified framework that combines AI Decision Observability with Decision Intelligence—linking how decisions are made, measured, and improved across human-AI systems.

Building on our AI Decision Automation Framework, we explore the technical and organizational capabilities required to move from decision outputs to decision systems: continuous, observable pipelines where every inference, rule, and outcome can be traced back to its origin. We discuss key methodologies—comprehensive logging, data and model lineage tracing, model introspection, counterfactual and causal analysis—and how these integrate into enterprise observability stacks.

The session also showcases tools and architectures that operationalize observability, alongside real-world case studies from regulated domains like finance, healthcare, and autonomous mobility.

We’ll conclude with a forward-looking view on how Decision Observability fuels Decision Intelligence—enabling enterprises to build trusted, adaptive, and compliant AI ecosystems where decisions are not just made but understood, improved, and governed.

Key Takeaways:

How to architect AI systems for full decision traceability and governance

Integrating Decision Intelligence with AI Decision Observability for continuous learning

Practical frameworks for scaling decision transparency and automation across the enterprise

speakers.bio:

My focus has always been at the intersection of technology architecture, organizational design, and human potential — building systems where humans and AI agents co-create outcomes.

I’ve driven multiple enterprise-scale implementations, from AgentX (AI Agents that creates AI Agents) and AI Decision Observability to Knowledge and Workflow Data Fabric integration with Snowflake — directly improving self-service rates, decision transparency, and productivity across tens of thousands of employees.

sessions.title: Vector, Graph, or Key Value? Choosing Your Agent's Memory
sessions.description:
Your agent works in the demo, then forgets everything the next day. The model is not broken: models are stateless by design, and memory belongs to the harness you build around them. Bigger context windows do not fix it. Re sending full history burns tokens every turn and still vanishes between sessions.

This talk maps the agent memory landscape through one question asked four ways: retrieval by key, by meaning, and by relationship. You will learn when key value, vector, graph, and hybrid memory each win, plus the capabilities layer on top: selective memory, hygiene against dirty and poisoned entries, and reasoning memory for auditable decisions.

speakers.bio: Elizabeth Fuentes is a Developer Advocate and AI engineer specializing in agent harness architecture. Through hands-on demos she breaks complex concepts into simple, understandable pieces of code, helping developers build more efficient agents and democratizing the adoption of advanced AI for everyone

In this technical session, we will take a repository from a generic Copilot experience to an AI-ready development environment. We will encode the project knowledge and validation developers need, then package recurring workflows as reusable prompts, skills, plugins, and custom agents. Next, we will version and govern those resources, and publish them through a centralized internal marketplace. We will close by connecting these developer practices to GitHub Copilot enterprise managed settings and how you can configure these at scale. You will leave with a practical guidance for making Agentic workflows useful beyond a single developer while providing engineering velocity and keeping people responsible for what ships.

speakers.bio: Luis Pujols is a Staff Customer Success Architect at GitHub, where he serves as a trusted technical advisor to some of GitHub's largest strategic customers, helping them turn AI-assisted, agentic development into a scaled team capability rather than a series of individual wins. Luis partners with technical leaders to drive adoption across the full software development lifecycle from CI/CD to security and GitHub Copilot, helping them define the governance guardrails that make agentic development safe and accountable at scale.

Through real-world deployment examples, we'll demonstrate how these zero-trust foundations solve critical security challenges at the intersection of AI, cloud infrastructure, and regulatory compliance.

Roboflow is supported by thousands of customers and investors like Y Combinator, Craft Ventures, GV (fmr Google Ventures), the founders of OpenAI, Jeff Dean, amongst others. sessions.title: Application-Defined Compute: Rethinking Infrastructure for AI Applications
sessions.description:
AI applications don't have fixed infrastructure requirements. A single request can fan out into hundreds of long-running tasks with different runtimes, memory requirements, and execution times. The application is no longer just consuming infrastructure. It defines the infrastructure it needs at runtime.

In this talk, Render CEO Anurag Goel introduces Application-Defined Compute, a new infrastructure model built for AI-native applications. You'll learn why traditional serverless platforms and self-managed orchestration both break down at scale, and how developers can provision compute just in time, run long-lived stateful workloads, and execute tasks with the flexibility of real servers, without managing queues, worker pools, retries, or orchestration themselves.

Using Render Workflows as an example, the session explores the new infrastructure primitives emerging for AI-native applications and how cloud platforms are evolving to support them.

speakers.bio: Anurag Goel is the founder and CEO of Render, the modern cloud platform helping millions of application developers and teams innovate and scale faster. The company has raised over $250M from top investors and was recently valued at $1.5B. He previously founded and exited Crestle, a GPU-powered notebook platform for data scientists. Earlier, he was the eighth employee at Stripe, where he led the Risk organization and played a key role in scaling the company through its hypergrowth phase. Anurag holds a B.Tech in Computer Science from IIT Delhi.

sessions.title: From Stateless to Stateful: Real-Time Voice & Messaging Agents with Twilio   and AWS
sessions.description:
We have all had that maddening customer service experience: you text a support line about a delayed flight, receive a confirmation, but when you call in a minute later, the voice agent asks, "How can I help you today?" completely blind to the SMS you just sent. This is the "Channel Amnesia" problem.

While businesses are pouring billions into generative AI, most agents are still built on stateless architectures that forget customer context the second a session ends.

In this session, we will cure AI amnesia. You will learn how to orchestrate stateful, production-grade AI agents across SMS and Voice using Twilio Agent Connect and Amazon Bedrock. We will dive into why traditional serverless compute fails stateful agents, how to leverage AWS Fargate for isolated, long-lived sessions, and how to configure Bedrock AgentCore over WebSockets to hit sub-50ms streaming voice latency. No slide-ware here — expect a live, cross-channel demo and open-source code you can deploy tomorrow.

speakers.bio: Rishab is a Staff Developer Evangelist at Twilio, part-time cloud professor at St. Lawrence College, co-author of Learn to Cloud, AWS Community Builder, and a Microsoft MVP. He is passionate about helping people get into cloud and sharing his learnings from his time in cloud, DevOps and now DevRel.

sessions.title: Making Science Larger, not just Faster
sessions.description: The dominant framing of enterprise AI is speed: faster code, faster decisions, faster discovery. That framing misses the larger story. When AI is anchored to the equations of physics, chemistry and biology rather than to the corpus of the open web, it does not just compress timelines — it expands the space of what can be explored. A bigger biochemical landscape for drug discovery. A bigger materials landscape for batteries and alloys. A bigger design landscape for everything humans build. Drawing on SandboxAQ's deployments across pharma, energy and navigation, Yuval shows why Large Quantitative Models are the first AI architecture capable of growing the pie rather than slicing it thinner, and what that means for any enterprise still measuring AI value in cost reduction.

speakers.bio:
Yuval Dvir has operated through two of the largest technology shifts of the modern era from the inside - Microsoft's digital transformation, and the AI transformation that Google, DeepMind, and SandboxAQ are leading. This makes him a rare translator between the old world and the new.
Across twenty years he has turned frontier science into real-world applications at Skype, Microsoft, Google, DeepMind, and now SandboxAQ, the Alphabet spinoff. At Google he built and led the global partner ecosystem behind Gemini and Workspace, cementing Google's distribution advantage and launching Gemini's first-ever global partnerships. He worked with DeepMind and Google Brain on moving science from research to revenue, through partnerships ranging from AI pathology to the connectomics project mapping the neural network of the fruit fly brain.
As a founding member of SandboxAQ, he drove the company’s first commercial engagements. He was also behind one of the largest pharma drug discovery deals in partnership with Google Cloud and the DeepMind co-scientist team. He holds an MSc in Applied Neuroscience from King’s College London and an MBA from INSEAD. He is the author of AI-Political (September 2026), which argues that AI is most powerful when it remains apolitical - innately unbiased and truth-seeking, the guardrail humans are not wired to be.

sessions.title: From Voice Demo to Enterprise Production
sessions.description:
Building a Voice AI demo takes a weekend; production engineering is a different beast. This session delivers the architectural playbook for scaling resilient, enterprise-grade voice agents.
We will evaluate speech-to-speech versus modular (STT → LLM → TTS) pipelines, WebRTC stacks, and hybrid topographies for strict data residency. You will learn fast-brain/slow-brain UX patterns to keep turn-taking responsive while backends process tool calls, alongside strategies for runtime model switching and custom vocabulary.
Walk away with the exact trade-offs, patterns, and metrics needed to operate low-latency voice pipelines at scale.

speakers.bio: Anahita Havewala is a Development Architect in the Office of the CTO at SAP, where she defines technical strategy and hands-on execution for enterprise AI runtimes, multi-agent orchestration, and real-time streaming voice systems. A holder of multiple AI/ML patents, she specializes in taking frontier AI models and grounding them in resilient, cloud-native enterprise platforms. With over a decade of software architecture experience, Anahita bridges high-level executive strategy with low-level engineering execution to ship low-latency, production-grade AI infrastructure at global scale.
speakers.company_position: Expert Development Architect Office of the CTO

speakers.bio: Anuj Gupta has been working on Applied AI, Distributed Systems and Low Latency applications for more than 15 years. He loves solving the most challenging problems. In this his current role, he focuses on Agentic platforms, context engineering, agentic orchestration, agents framework, enterprise agents, A2A, MCP strategy and other company-wide strategic goals.

sessions.title: The Missing Infrastructure for AI Agents
sessions.description:
Everyone can build an AI agent. Almost nobody knows how to run thousands of them safely in production.

Over the past two years, we've watched AI agents evolve from demos into software that writes code, answers customers, automates workflows, and makes decisions. The challenge has shifted from building smarter agents to operating them reliably at scale.

Having spent time at Meta and Google and now helping lead Guild.ai, CTO and co-founder Chris Waterson has seen firsthand where production systems fail. It's rarely the model. It's the surrounding infrastructure: context management, permissions, observability, cost controls, versioning, evaluation, and governance.

This session explores what changes when AI agents become real production systems instead of prototypes. He'll draw on lessons from building Guild Software Factory, a system of specialized agents that plans, implements, reviews, and maintains work across a codebase, and Guild Optimizer, which automatically tests cheaper agent configurations against production history to cut costs without sacrificing quality.

Attendees will leave with practical frameworks for designing AI agent systems that are observable, secure, reusable, and capable of evolving over time, not just impressive during a demo.

Whether you're building your first agent or managing hundreds across an organization, this talk offers lessons from operating AI where reliability matters.

speakers.bio:
Chris Waterson has spent three decades working toward a single goal: building systems that can reason, plan, and act on their own. He started chasing that vision in the ‘90s, long before the tools to realize it existed. Since then, he's helped build many of those tools himself, contributing to foundational embedding research and deep learning ranking models at Google, and later leading the team behind DevMate, Meta's internal agentic coding framework.

That work convinced him that building agents is no longer the hard part – managing them reliably in production is. It's why he co-founded Guild.ai, the control plane for AI agents, giving engineering teams the access controls, observability, versioning, and sharing infrastructure needed to run agents at scale with confidence.

sessions.title: Accelerating development and managing agents with the GitHub Copilot app
sessions.description: Built from the ground up as a native AI coding tool, the GitHub Copilot app integrates with your work and workflow. From triaging issues, managing agents, and creating interactive canvases, you can build, review, and deploy all from one location! Let's explore how to accelerate your dev flow and get the most out of the tool.

speakers.bio: Christopher is a longtime geek and developer at heart. He's spent the better part of the last couple of decades enabling and upskilling developers on a variety of languages and platforms. At present he's at GitHub focusing on aiding organizations in improving their DevOps processes. When not in front of a monitor he can be found running many miles or spending time with his partner and their adopted fur-baby.

sessions.title: Alexander Varro and Alija Nuredini - Founders OS for replacing operational fragmentation
sessions.description: Every tool solves a problem until it creates another one. What started as a simple search for better software turned into years of frustration, dozens of disconnected tools and one simple realization: managing software had become harder than managing the business itself. In this founder story, you'll discover how that frustration led to building Pistacio, a Founders OS platform designed to simplify operations for modern service companies and why reducing complexity could become the next major opportunity in B2B SaaS.

speakers.bio:
I am the Founder and CEO of 8reasons Digital GmbH, a UX agency specialized in complex B2B and enterprise applications. Together with my 15-person team, I design digital products for internal platforms, data-driven tools and sophisticated software systems where UX needs to create real business impact.

My mindset is simple: UX is not decoration, it’s a strategic lever for efficiency, adoption and growth.

8reasons Digital is part of the iits Group with more than 160 experts combining UX excellence with deep technological expertise.

I lead my company fully remote between Germany and Peru and stand for modern leadership built on clarity, trust and responsibility.

Alija Nuredini is the Founder and CEO of Pistacio and DesignOps Lead at 8reasons Digital, a design agency. He built Pistacio to solve a problem he saw firsthand: service businesses juggling too many disconnected tools for time tracking, task management, expenses, and team coordination. Combining a founder's instinct with a builder's hands-on approach, he shipped a full operations platform serving real service teams. He has the scope decisions, dead ends, and lessons to prove it.

sessions.title: Build and deploy a personal agent on a Cloud Run instance
sessions.description:
How do you run an autonomous AI agent in the cloud 24/7 without wasting a fortune or managing servers?

If you are building long-running agents, you know the hosting dilemma: standard serverless platforms scale to zero, which instantly kills your background loops and wipes your agent's active memory. Dedicated VMs keep the agent awake, but they cost more and leave you stuck managing the infrastructure.

The fix is a new compute primitive: Cloud Run instances.

In this hands-on workshop, you will learn how to deploy a single, always-on container to host a continuous background agent. Stepping into the role of a coffee shop manager, you will build an AI assistant using the Agent Development Kit (ADK) that continuously analyzes business data. You will also leverage Cloud Run sandboxes, enabling your agent to dynamically write, execute, and test code on the fly to solve complex problems safely.

Stop managing infrastructure and start building agents that never sleep!
sessions.workshop_requirements: Laptop & charger

speakers.bio: Shir Meir Lador leads an Applied AI Engineering team at Google Cloud with the mission to accelerate the developer journey from code to secure AI workloads in production. She is also the co-host of  "The agent factory"  podcast that dives into building production-ready AI agents. Previously, she worked as the AI group Manager of the Document Understanding Group at Intuit, where she led teams in developing AI services that helps consumers and small businesses prosper. Prior to intuit, Shir worked at 2 Israeli startups as a data scientist and researcher. A recognized leader in AI and data science, Shir has served as WiDS Tel Aviv Ambassador, KDD workshop organizer, co-founder and organizer of PyData Tel Aviv, and the co-host of "Unsupervised" a podcast exploring the latest in data science in Israel. She frequently speaks at international AI and data science conferences, sharing insights on applied machine learning and AI innovation. Shir holds an M.Sc. in Electrical Engineering and Computers from Ben-Gurion University, specializing in machine learning.

sessions.title: Creating and Sustaining Positive Communities
sessions.description:
Maezza Romero, Community Developer for Romero Games, has been shaping communities from the ground up for 6+ years. She started her journey in 2018 with Cyber Squad for Hewlett Packard Enterprises and the Girl Scouts, and now manages social media and a 6,000+ member Discord for Romero Games, one of the friendliest shooter communities in the industry. Her passion? Ensuring everyone feels valued and welcome.

Join Maezza to discover the strategies behind building inclusive, engaged communities. She’ll share tips on authentic engagement, moderation best practices, and laying the groundwork for communities that stand the test of time. This workshop is suitable for those working in both game development and general business, with practical insights that can be applied across a range of industries.

speakers.bio: Maezza Romero, Community Manager at Romero Games, has 6 years of industry experience, managing large community spaces like the Romero Games Discord, now with 7,000 members. The company's Twitter, with over 10,000 followers, engages fans of legacy titles like DOOM and Quake through polls and Q&As. In 2024, Maezza adapts to the evolving social media landscape by using TikTok, Discord and Instagram, alongside Facebook and Twitter, to create content for dedicated Millennial and Gen-X fans.

sessions.title: The AI-Native Engineer: From Business Problem to Prototype
sessions.description:
How well you scope a problem determines how well AI can help you solve it. This workshop makes that claim testable, not just believable. 

Bring your laptop and the AI tools you already use. Teams take on a real, messy business challenge — a live-service gaming company caught between an AI feature its CEO already announced and the fragile data foundation that feature would actually run on. Before building anything, each team is randomly assigned exactly one stakeholder to interview. What they hear — and how well they turn it into a scoped, defensible approach — is the variable we're testing. 

From there, teams use their own tools and AI to build a working solution slice with AI as a genuine collaborator throughout. We instrument the build: prompts submitted, iterations to a working version, time to first pass. At the reveal, we show the correlation directly: teams that scoped tightly from partial information moved faster and cleaner with AI than teams that tried to build before they'd committed to an approach. 

Every participant leaves with a personal build card — their own scoping-to-efficiency numbers next to the room's benchmark — and a sharper instinct for a skill AI hasn't replaced: knowing what problem you're actually solving, from an incomplete picture, before you start.

speakers.bio: Srishti has eight years of industry experience spanning product management, business process automation, data science and digital strategy. Known for her collaborative and solutions-oriented approach, she specializes in bringing practical solutions to complex challenges. Most recently, her work has focused on delivering meaningful fan experiences within the sports industry.
Sidarth Aurora

sessions.title: RoboCoders: Judgment Day: AI-Assisted Engineering Applied - The Battle of Agents
sessions.description:
Agentic AI-assisted engineering tools promise cleaner code, faster development, and fewer late-night debugging sessions. But do they truly deliver?

In this live showdown, Viktor and Baruch will each use a different set of cutting-edge AI coding tools, like an IDEs and CLI agents (we'd name them, but honestly, things move too fast in this space), to develop a non-trivial IoT application, from initial setup to testing and debugging, all live on stage.

Will the IoT bulb turn on by the end of the session, and which tool will make it happen? You don't know, we don't know, but we'll find out together—live on stage.

You, the audience, decide which tool actually improves quality and productivity and which just adds noise instead of useful code. Bring your skepticism, cast your vote, and get ready for surprises.

speakers.bio:
Baruch Sadogursky (@jbaruch) did Java before it had generics, DevOps before there was Docker, and DevRel before it had a name. He built DevRel at JFrog from a ten-person company through IPO, co-authored "Liquid Software" and "DevOps Tools for Java Developers," and is a Java Champion, Microsoft MVP, and CNCF Ambassador alumni.

Today, he's obsessed with how AI agents actually write code. At Tessl, an AI agent enablement platform, Baruch focuses on context engineering, management, and sharing. On top of sharing context with AI agents, Baruch also shares knowledge with developers through blog posts, meetups, and conferences like DevNexus, QCon, Kubecon, and Devoxx, mostly about why vibecoding doesn't scale.

Viktor Gamov is a Principal Developer Advocate at Confluent, founded by the original creators of Apache Kafka®. With a rich background in implementing and advocating for distributed systems and cloud-native architectures, Viktor excels in open-source technologies. He is passionate about assisting architects, developers, and operators in crafting systems that are not only low in latency and scalable but also highly available.
As a Java Champion and an esteemed speaker, Viktor is known for his insightful presentations at top industry events like JavaOne, Devoxx, Kafka Summit, and QCon. His expertise spans distributed systems, real-time data streaming, JVM, and DevOps.
Viktor has co-authored "Enterprise Web Development" from O'Reilly and "Apache Kafka® in Action" from Manning. 
Follow Viktor on X—@gamussa to stay updated with his latest thoughts on technology, his gym and food adventures, and insights into open-source and developer advocacy.

sessions.title: Exploring MCP Servers with GitHub Copilot
sessions.description: Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard that lets AI agents like GitHub Copilot tap into external tools, services, and your own account data. In this hands-on workshop, you'll connect GitHub Copilot to both public and authenticated MCP servers, explore the tools they expose, and put them to work—researching topics, troubleshooting issues, and making real contributions to a codebase. You'll also discover how combining MCP servers with agent skills unlocks more powerful, personalized developer workflows.
sessions.workshop_requirements: Attendees should bring a fully charged laptop, and already have a GitHub account. Attendees will all have the option to complete the workshop using GitHub Codespaces, a browser-based VS Code environment, but they may also want to download the GitHub Copilot CLI and GitHub Copilot App on their machine beforehand, so that they can try all forms of Copilot.

speakers.bio: Pamela Fox is a developer advocate at Microsoft, where she helps developers use Python with Azure, Microsoft Foundry, VS Code, and GitHub. Before Microsoft, she was one of the first engineers at Coursera, early DevRel at Google, lecturer at UC Berkeley of the largest CS class, and the creator of the Khan Academy programming courses.

sessions.title: Ducks, Sensors, and Agents
sessions.workshop_requirements:
What to bring:

A laptop with a USB-C port.
A smartphone with a camera.
A USB-C cable to connect the Arduino UNO Q to your laptop.

speakers.bio:
Brian McFadden is a Staff Engineer in Developer Relations at Edge Impulse, a Qualcomm company, where he helps developers build AI applications that run on edge devices. His work spans machine learning, agentic systems, developer tooling, technical content, and community building.

A self-described professional explorer, Brian is drawn to ambiguous problems and turning ambitious ideas into reality. That mindset has taken him across industries ranging from robotics and biotechnology to edge AI, and beyond technology into ultramarathons, world travel, and adventures in the mountains.

sessions.title: Responsible AI Architecture with Zero Trust Agents
sessions.description:
As we shift from simple chatbots to long-running agents, we face a critical engineering challenge. The risk is no longer just bad output. It is memory poisoning. This occurs when malicious data permanently corrupts your vector database, causing agents to hallucinate or leak private information indefinitely.

This session will present a Zero Trust architecture for Responsible AI starting prompt injection until agent isolation. We will dissect a reference stack built entirely on open source standards that treats your vector storage as a high-security vault.

Attendees will walk away with practical techniques to: Replace risky API keys with cryptographic verification using SPIFFE and SPIRE, ensuring only valid code can access long-term memory.

Use policies to write security rules as code, separating your safety logic from your application logic. Block sensitive data and malicious prompts before they are ever stored using tools like Microsoft Presidio.

Join me to learn how to build agents that are resilient, audit-ready, and secure by design.

speakers.bio:
Ashok Prakash is a Staff Engineer at Apple, where he leads engineering initiatives for Responsible AI and safety infrastructure. He specializes in designing high-performance cloud platforms that make complex GPU-accelerated workloads reliable and easy to use. His work focuses on turning difficult infrastructure problems into predictable, self-service systems that allow engineering teams to move faster without breaking things.

Before joining Apple, Ashok spent six years at Oracle Cloud as a Senior Principal Engineer. There, he led the platform engineering efforts to build a Kubernetes-based GPU platform that abstracted bare-metal clusters behind simple APIs. His work allowed product teams to launch AI workloads in minutes instead of days, providing consistent provisioning, quota controls, and clear cost visibility. He has extensive experience building multi-tenant schedulers, automating cluster lifecycles, and creating developer tools that enforce good defaults for security and observability.

Ashok is a regular speaker at engineering and data conferences, including the Airflow Summit, AI Risk Summit and Linux Foundation Workshops, where he shares practical, vendor-neutral patterns for using AI safely. His talks often cover topics like automating documentation, generating unit tests, and establishing human-in-the-loop review processes for AI-generated code.

Ashok holds three published U.S. patent applications and has authored multiple international publications in AI and NLP, which have been cited by both academic researchers and industry practitioners. His core philosophy is simple: pave the path so the right thing is the easy thing to do.

Based in Seattle, Ashok also contributes practical guidance on AI adoption for non-specialists. He is the author of Human Reimagined: Thriving in the Age of AI, a guide for professionals looking to use AI as a helpful assistant rather than a source of anxiety.

sessions.title: Architecting the 100X SDLC: Building Production Trust into AI-Assisted Delivery
sessions.description:
AI-assisted development has made it astonishingly easy to produce software — and astonishingly hard to trust it. Demos ship in hours, but production demands more: auditability, verifiability, cost control, and the delivery discipline enterprises have spent decades refining.

This session begins by clarifying the terminology now shaping the industry — SDLC, AI-Assisted SDLC, and ADLC— and what actually changes when AI agents become first-class participants in software delivery rather than autocomplete on the side.

We then share hard-won lessons from building the VibeFlow, a 9 persona AI team for producing production-quality software through AI-assisted development. VibeFlow structures specialized agents into a governed team that operates inside familiar Scrum and Kanban constructs: backlogs, sprints, reviews, and definitions of done. The result is AI velocity that remains observable, auditable, and verifiable at every stage.

Attendees will learn the design principles that made this work in practice: why governance must be architected in rather than bolted on; how work-item traceability makes AI output verifiable instead of merely plausible; how cost controls and guardrails keep agent teams economically predictable; and how marrying agents to agile ceremonies turns impressive demos into dependable delivery.

Whether you're an engineering leader evaluating AI adoption, an architect designing for it, or a practitioner already shipping with AI, you'll leave with a concrete blueprint for moving from vibes to verifiable — and from X to 100X — without sacrificing the trust production demands.

speakers.bio: Ranjan Parthasarathy is CEO and co-founder of Axiomstudio.ai, where he is building enterprise-grade AI platforms for governed software development, agent orchestration, and AI adoption at scale. He previously served as Chief Product and Technology Officer at Apica and was founder and CEO of LOGIQ.AI, his second technology company to be acquired. Ranjan’s work spans AI, DevOps, ITOps, observability, data platforms, and enterprise automation, with a focus on helping engineering and operations teams build faster without compromising governance, security, or reliability. He holds an  MS degree from Stanford University and is based in the San Francisco Bay Area.

sessions.title: Finding the Edges: Testing, Evaluating, and Monitoring Voice AI Agents Before Your Users Do
sessions.description:
Every demo of a voice AI agent looks great — until real users start talking. They interrupt, mumble, switch languages mid-sentence, and ask the one question that sends the agent off the rails. Traditional scripted QA only verifies the behaviors you already thought of, which is exactly why so many voice agents fail in production in ways their teams never saw coming.

This session walks through a practical, engineering-grade approach to shipping Voice AI agents you can trust, built on three pillars: simulation, evaluation, and monitoring. You'll see how synthetic "drivers" — AI-powered simulated users with distinct personalities, goals, and contexts — hold realistic multi-turn conversations with your agent across 30+ languages and real-world audio conditions (noise, crosstalk, clipping), actively exploring the edges scripted tests miss. We'll then look at how judge-based, symbolic, and audio evaluations turn those discoveries into CI/CD release gates, so a change that degrades conversation quality fails the build before it reaches users. Finally, we'll close the loop with production monitoring that captures real failures and automatically converts them into regression tests — so the same mistake never ships twice.

You'll leave with a concrete blueprint for finding the edges of your Voice AI agent before your customers do.

speakers.bio: Matt Wyman is the CEO and co-founder of Okareo, the platform for testing, evaluating, and monitoring Voice AI agents — using synthetic user simulation to find the edges of agent behavior before customers do. A career-long builder of developer and testing tools, Matt was previously Chief Product Officer and Chief Customer Officer at Sauce Labs, the leader in continuous web and mobile app testing, and VP of Product at CircleCI, where he helped define modern CI/CD practices. His earlier roles include product leadership at Xtime and CoreLogic, and he founded two startups, RealiD and ConnectingVoices. That blend of shipping developer platforms and obsessing over quality at scale led him to co-found Okareo in 2023, tackling the hardest reliability problem in AI today: real-time voice agents facing real human behavior. Matt holds degrees in Computer Science and Cultural Anthropology from UC Berkeley — a pairing that turns out to be exactly right for teaching machines to talk to people.

sessions.title: Loominus Studio: The AI Workbench for Labs and Factories
sessions.description:
Most AI agents move files. Ours run machines.

Loominus Studio is an AI workbench. You use it to build agents that work alongside people to design and make real things: materials, formulations, devices. The jargon for this is collaborative cyber-physical agents. The plain version is agents with hands.

What you build is a harness. A harness is everything an agent needs to do real work: the tools it can reach, the steps it follows, what it remembers, what it is allowed to touch. Coding agents have harnesses. That is why they work. Labs and factories have none.

You build one by wiring nodes into a graph. Each node is a step or a tool: run this machine, mix this batch, ask a person to check, measure the result, pick what to try next. Wire them together and the agent runs the loop.

Two things matter about these harnesses.

Configurable: no two labs work the same way, so you build yours instead of buying someone else's.

Portable: build it once, run it on someone else's machines. Your process should not be locked to one vendor's box.

We use it ourselves. MetaLab is a harness for making formulations. BioLoom is a harness for printing parts. Same workbench, different graph.

Five minutes on why the loop that made coding agents work is the same loop every lab runs, why nobody built the workbench for it, and what that changes for the bioeconomy age, when the things ahead of us have to be made, not just written.

speakers.bio:
Filippos Tourlomousis is the founder of Biological Lattice Industries (BLI), a company building a new way to advance the bioeconomy through collaborative cyber-physical AI agents for innovators who design and make advanced formulations and devices serving human health and the environment.

His work bridges entrepreneurship, autonomous laboratories, biofabrication, materials engineering, and open-source scientific instrumentation. He also leads the Autonomous Science Lab at NCSR Demokritos in Athens and previously conducted postdoctoral research at MIT's Center for Bits and Atoms. His mission is to make AI-powered experimental platforms and self-driving labs more accessible, scalable, and impactful for materials discovery and bioengineering.

sessions.title: I Don't Trust AI Agents (And Neither Should You): Building Production-Ready Architectures
sessions.description: Your AI agent works great in the demo. Then you deploy it and it hallucinates a refund policy, exposes customer data, or just loops endlessly burning tokens. This session walks through a layered approach to agent safety using tools like Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and the Strands Agents SDK: guardrails, observability, multi-agent safety patterns, and reference architectures you can adapt immediately.

speakers.bio:
I am a computer person who writes Rust, breaks things on AWS, and collects computers older than most of my audience. By title I'm a Distinguished Developer Advocate, by practice I'm live-coding on Twitch or convincing a 1974 minicomputer to do something useful. I build CLI tools nobody asked for but everyone ends up using, blog about Rust and cloud development right here, and firmly believe the terminal is the best UI ever made. I'm happiest when a demo works on the first try, which almost never happens.
I also care deeply about developer productivity and coding assistants. I spend an unreasonable amount of time teaching AI agents to be better coding companions, building MCP servers, and automating everything that stands still long enough. If there's a way to make developers faster and happier, I'm probably already tinkering with it.

sessions.title: Rethinking Developer Tools for the Agent Era
sessions.description: AI agents are becoming heavy users of developer tools: reading documentation, operating platforms, writing and shipping code. Tools designed around human attention - interfaces, docs, onboarding - behave differently when the one using them is software. Companies across the stack now serve humans and machines at once, and the choices go to the core of the product. What changes when agents become users, and what it means for the people building with them.

speakers.bio: Han Wang is co-founder and CEO of Mintlify, the knowledge infrastructure layer that makes technical knowledge accessible to humans and AI agents. He started Mintlify with Hahnbee Lee in 2022, their senior year at Cornell. Mintlify now powers documentation for more than 20,000 companies including Anthropic, Microsoft, Coinbase, PayPal, and Amazon.

Sam Bhagwat is the Co-founder and CEO of Mastra, the leading open-source TypeScript framework for building AI agents (YC W25). Previously, he co-founded Gatsby, used by hundreds of thousands of developers, and is the author of Principles of Building AI Agents.

Ben Haefele is Chief Product Officer at Webflow, where he oversees the company's product and design teams and sets the direction for the Webflow platform. Ben joined Webflow in 2022 and helped lead Webflow's transformation into a multi-product enterprise platform before stepping into the Chief Product Officer role. He brings more than 15 years of experience leading teams across product, engineering, and design, and previously co-founded the app-building platform Adalo.

As CPO, Ben is focused on Webflow's vision of a living web, where every digital experience can come alive. He pairs AI with the craft, control, and trust that teams need to build trusted brand experiences and drive compounding growth.

Ignacio Riesgo is Senior Director, Developer Advocacy, for IBM & Red Hat Runtimes. In his role, he leads all Developer Outreach Programs, Content and Advocacy initiatives for the IBM and Red Hat Java portfolio, adopted by tens of thousands of enterprise customers, and millions of developers.

sessions.title: The Next Wave of Agents: What’s Real, What’s Next, and What Matters
sessions.description: Artificial intelligence is undergoing a foundational shift from passive, generative model outputs toward goal-oriented, autonomous operational execution. Agentic AI represents an architectural evolution beyond static prompt-response systems, combining reasoning, memory, planning, and external tool execution to act independently within complex environments. Further, organizations face real-world challenges in reliability, safety, governance, and system orchestration. In this panel, we will discuss what the current capabilities of agentic systems and how its impact is measured. We will also discuss architectural breakthroughs driving next wave of agents which consists of multi-agent collaboration, tool integration and persistent memory how to move agents from pilots to production. sessions.title: Stop Running Mystery Meat in Production
sessions.description:
We have all been there. You need a database or a quick node environment, so you throw "FROM node:latest" into your Dockerfile and deploy. It works, but you have just introduced a black box into your Kubernetes cluster.

For the Developer, it’s a quick fix. For the Platform Engineer, it’s a nightmare.

Most upstream images from public registries are a roll of the dice. They come pre-packed with critical vulnerabilities, unknown binaries, and bloated libraries that you didn’t ask for and definitely don’t want running in your secure environment. In a world of Zero Trust, why are we trusting random upstream maintainers with the keys to our infrastructure?

In this session, we will dismantle the myth that "open source means secure" when it comes to container images. We will walk through the architecture of a truly Secure Software Delivery pipeline—one that establishes trust before a single line of code is committed. We will discuss:

- The hidden dangers inside popular "official" images.
- Moving beyond basic scanning: Why you need SLSA L3 provenance, SBOMs, and cryptographic attestation.
- The "Build vs. Buy" dilemma: Should you curate your own base images or rely on a hardened upstream provider?

Join us to learn how to bridge the gap between developer velocity and platform security, ensuring that the only thing running in your cluster is code you actually trust.

sessions.title: Taming Rogue Agents: Observability-Driven Evaluation for Production Reliability
sessions.description:
Moving from a viral demo to reliable enterprise AI is the hardest hurdle in modern software engineering. Because agents are inherently non-deterministic, validating performance requires a granular look at the "why" and "how" behind every action. 

This session explores how observability redefines agentic evaluation beyond binary pass/fail testing, shifting the focus from the result to the entire reasoning chain. Featuring a live demo using Arize Phoenix and LangGraph, we’ll showcase how to trace complex loops and automate evaluations in real-time. 

What you’ll learn: 

Beyond Output: Why judging final answers alone is a recipe for silent failure. 

Live Implementation: Using Arize Phoenix with LangGraph to visualize traces and debug agentic "thought processes". 

The Playbook: An incremental framework for evaluation-first development. 

Are you ready to stop guessing and start measuring? Join us to master the art of agent evaluation.

sessions.title: Your Agents Need Observability Before They Need Better Models
sessions.description:
Everyone's chasing faster models, better reasoning, shinier inference endpoints. But here's the truth: your agent will fail in production long before model quality becomes your bottleneck.

The problem isn't the model. It's that you can't see what your agent is actually doing.

In this session we cover why traditional observability breaks for agent workloads, how OpenTelemetry and GenAI semantic conventions give you the vocabulary to instrument agents correctly, and how observability becomes the thing that lets you gradually trust your agents with more autonomy. You'll walk away knowing what to instrument, why it matters, and how to stop guessing when your agent does something unexpected in production.

sessions.title: AI ROI: The Hard Unit Economics of AI-Native Engineering
sessions.description:
The honeymoon phase of AI is over.

Organizations across all industries have spent the last two years buying licenses and experimenting, but boards and CFOs in the 2026 fiscal year are demanding proof of value. For CTOs and VPs of Engineering, the challenge has shifted from "how do we build this?" to a critical fiscal responsibility: showing a measurable return on AI investment.

The bottleneck isn't the model; it’s the middleware of the human process. Too many organizations are automating tasks (AI-Augmented) while leaving the topology of their engineering organizations untouched. To capture true ROI, we must shift to AI-Native Engineering, where the SDLC is architected around probabilistic capabilities rather than deterministic checklists.

In this session, Manu will help teams learn how to move past "productivity vibes" and into measurable ROI. Manu will break down the “Efficiency Trap”: the phenomenon where AI generates code faster, but testing, security, and deployment bottlenecks remain static, resulting in zero net gain in system throughput. 

Additionally, Manu will present a framework for evaluating ROI at every stage of the product lifecycle and show attendees how they can move their metrics from "PRs per day" to "Outcome Velocity", in short, reduce the “Lead Time to Value.”

The 4-Stage ROI Lifecycle

- Discovery (The Intent Stage): ROI of using AI to bridge the "Context Gap" between Product, Design and Engineering.

- Development (The Build/Composition Stage): Measuring "Unit Cost of Code" to ensure high-velocity output doesn't increase downstream maintenance costs.

- Verification (The Quality Stage): ROI of shifting from manual QA to "Automated Eval" stacks.

- Operations (The Resilience Stage): The financial impact of AI-driven observability, self-healing systems, and the automation of the Support-to-Engineering feedback loop.

sessions.title: Clean Rooms Demystified: Architecture and Patterns for Privacy-Safe Data Collaboration
sessions.description:
As enterprises increasingly look to combine data with partners, suppliers, and platforms to power AI, analytics, and personalization — without exposing raw records or violating privacy regulations — Clean Rooms have moved from an emerging concept to a serious architectural option. But most teams encounter them first through vendor documentation and demos that skip the hard parts.

This session starts from first principles. It explains the core problem Clean Rooms solve: enabling joint computation across datasets from multiple parties without any party accessing the other's raw data. It then walks through the architectural building blocks — controlled computation environments, output restrictions, access control policies, and the cryptographic boundaries that make privacy guarantees enforceable — and shows how these concepts translate into real design decisions.

From there, the session takes an honest look at the implementation landscape. Attendees will understand how Clean Rooms compare to alternative privacy-enhancing approaches — federated learning, differential privacy, synthetic data, and contractual anonymization — and the trade-offs each involves across privacy strength, latency, operational complexity, and regulatory defensibility. The session also covers where production complexity tends to concentrate: access control configuration, output data governance, deployment automation, and integration with AI and ML workloads.

Attendees leave with a clear mental model for evaluating Clean Rooms against their own organization's data collaboration challenges, a practical understanding of the architectural patterns involved, and an honest view of what separates a well-designed Clean Rooms implementation from one that looks good in a proof of concept but struggles in production.

speakers.bio:

He specializes in real-time distributed data systems, ML-driven credit decisioning, and large-scale Apache Spark and Databricks pipelines in production FinTech environments.

His work includes reducing ML scoring latency from 24 hours to under 10 minutes, migrating 400+ legacy pipelines to optimized PySpark, and architecting Intuit's privacy-safe lending data collaboration platform using Databricks Clean Rooms — a first-of-its-kind implementation in financial services that he presented at the Databricks Data + AI Summit 2025.

Anurag writes for HackerNoon, DZone, and Medium's Towards Data Engineering publication, and has served as a peer reviewer for ICML, ICCV, and NeurIPS workshops. He holds an M.S. in Computer Science (Distributed Systems & Big Data Analytics) from Rochester Institute of Technology.

sessions.title: One Environment, N Machines: Deterministic Builds for Humans and Agents
sessions.description: Software used to be built in a handful of places you controlled. Now it's built everywhere: a laptop, a fleet of CI runners, a local sandbox, a remote sandbox with an agent driving it. Increasingly, nobody sets those machines up by hand. Two hard problems fall out of this: making the build produce the same result on every machine, and making the output of that build reproducible wherever it runs next. This talk looks at how deterministic, declarative environments (built on Nix) solve both: one definition that pins packages, toolchains, and even agent skills, reproduced bit-for-bit across the lifecycle, with a verifiable record of everything that went in. We'll show how Flox makes this practical without requiring your team to learn Nix.

speakers.bio: James has spent his career working closely with engineering, design, and cross-functional teams to build products customers love. Most recently, he led product at FluidCloud, and before that spent over five years at HashiCorp. His background also includes time at Pivotal Software.

sessions.title: The Private AI Platform: Why Agentic Apps Need a Private Application Platform
sessions.description: As AI moves from chat demos to “do-things” software, the platform requirements change: identity, policy, network controls, data governance, audit, and safe tool execution become mandatory. This session explains why a private application platform on private cloud is the most reliable foundation for enterprise AI—especially for agentic workflows and development assistants that touch sensitive systems. We’ll map the core platform capabilities (runtime, workload identity, secrets, supply chain, service brokering, observability, guardrails) to real AI components: model endpoints, vector stores, tool APIs, MCP servers, and skills routing. You’ll leave with a reference architecture and a pragmatic checklist to evaluate whether your current platform can safely run “full-blown” AI experiences.

sessions.title: Can AI Agents Actually Discover and Use Your Product? Agent-Led Growth and Agent Experience.
sessions.description:

Yet most teams only test their product journey for humans, leaving agent failures, such as unclear docs, missing setup context, broken authentication flows, and unreliable tool calls, largely invisible.

In this five-minute pitch, Lightsage shows how teams can test real agent journeys end to end, identify where an agent fails, and convert that evidence into improvements across APIs, SDKs, CLIs, MCP servers, and documentation. The outcome is a new discipline for developer platforms: Agent Experience.

sessions.title: AI vs. AI: Defending the open source supply chain with agentic workflows
sessions.description: With the arrival of Mythos and other frontier models we enter a new world. They can find security issues in libraries, create individual exploits, and successfully chain them to real-world attack campaigns in 2026. The open source ecosystem is on the verge of something new. What happens next is terrifying and exciting at the same time. At Chainguard we started a coalition with many partners across governments, banks and other large corporations, foundations, and open source communities to use the tools to strengthen our defenses against attackers. We established trust and infrastructure to share exploits, create patches, and bring them to use as binaries. Just in our first weeks we processed over thousands of findings, created well over 1k patches, and touched the code base of hundreds of open source projects. Now it is a few months later, and Manfred will share our experience from working within and outside the project. We will talk about good findings, bad patches, and ugly consequences alike, and dive into the details of examples and our collaboration with open source projects, communities, and their users. Manfred will also talk about the machinery behind the scenes that enables patching at the necessary scale - Chainguard Factory, powered by our open source agentic framework DriftlessAF, and expert engineers assisted by powerful AI models.

sessions.title: Software change is outpacing the platforms built to understand it.
sessions.description:
Atomic makes software changes queryable.

Atomic is source code management at the primitive level: a distributed, agent-native Git alternative. A single CLI brings semantic call graphs, enhanced code search, intents, attestations and provenance to every agent you already use, so every change keeps its origin, its reasoning, and its evidence

speakers.bio:
Lee Faus Founder & CEO, Atomic Software, Co.
https://atomic.dev
Lee is the Founder and CEO of Atomic, a code intelligence platform rebuilding version control from the ground up for the software factory era. He bootstrapped Atomic through pre-seed, assembled the founding team, and led the company to v1, drawing on two decades of experience inside the infrastructure of how software gets built.
That experience includes engineering and go-to-market roles at Borland, Compuware, Red Hat, GitHub, and GitLab, as well as direct advisory work with engineering leaders at Fortune 100 and Global 2000 companies including State Farm, Pfizer, Wells Fargo, Travelport, and Nokia. Those tools and those organizations were the right answer for their era. But after years of watching enterprises strain under the weight of agent-driven development, the architectural gap became impossible to ignore. Git was designed in 2005 for humans editing text files one commit at a time. It was never built for what is coming next.
Atomic was built to replace it. Where legacy platforms bolt AI onto infrastructure designed for human-rate commits, Atomic starts from a different foundation: immutable changes, Merkle-bound policy, cryptographic attestation, and a decision ledger that tracks every input and output from intent to integrated code. The inner loop, where agents actually work, has no serious tooling today. That is the white space Atomic was built to own.
Lee speaks at international conferences on AI-native engineering, software supply chain integrity, and the architectural consequences of machine-rate development. His focus is practical: what engineering organizations actually need to govern, audit, and scale a software factory where agents generate the majority of code.

sessions.title: each::labs: Close the Imagination Gap
sessions.description: The gap between what people imagine and what AI creates is a production problem. How each::labs closes it: one API, 600+ media models, routing and failover built in, frontier quality with production economics.

speakers.bio:

sessions.title: Fault Tolerance and Consistency at Scale: Harnessing the Power of Distributed SQL Databases
sessions.description:
Distributed SQL Databases are a powerful new data management technology that addresses modern applications’ need for scalability, availability, geographic distribution, and low response time – with the power of SQL and strong consistency. 

However, distributed databases bring their own challenges. For example, the familiar trade-offs between consistency, high availability, and partition tolerance still exist. Remote data access will still incur speed-of-light network delays.

This talk will describe the inner workings of distributed databases and how to design applications to best exploit their power. Using Oracle and other distributed databases as examples, we will explore the capabilities and unique application challenges posed by distributed databases. This talk will address design patterns that empower applications to handle network latency and consistency in the presence of real-world networks that can and do fail.
