My technical journey has focused on high-stakes environments, including migrating 192M+ sellers to next-generation billing platforms and designing APIs that handle 80M+ daily requests. I specialize in the intersection of Java, Spring Boot, and Azure.

After more than a decade of focusing on execution and architecture, I am now dedicated to sharing my "war stories" and technical insights with the broader developer community. My goal is to help other engineers navigate the complexities of modernizing legacy systems and building at scale.

sessions.title: Autonomous Infrastructure: Building AI Agents for Global-Scale Capacity Efficiency
sessions.description:
Efficiently managing compute capacity is a multi-dimensional optimization problem that has outpaced human-in-the-loop systems. 
This presentation details the development of an agentic ecosystem used to optimize Meta’s global infrastructure. 
We delve into the design of tooling that identifies inefficiencies in workload placement and resource allocation, utilizing AI agents to execute complex rebalancing tasks autonomously. 
We will share the results of these implementations, specifically how we recouped tens of megawatts of power and the lessons learned in building trust in autonomous infrastructure tools.

speakers.bio:
Tommy Tran is a software engineer at Meta, where he leads work on automated capacity efficiency, building the AI-agent systems that keep Meta's large-scale AI infrastructure running efficiently.
He authored Meta's Engineering Blog publication on that work, which was covered by the technical press, and he has been profiled by international media, including a feature interview on the French technology program Monde Numérique.
Earlier, he built machine-learning systems for ads and monetization at Meta and for sales automation at Ramp.
He holds an MSc in Data Science from École Polytechnique (X) and HEC Paris, and is a selected speaker at leading AI and developer conferences.
His work spans applied generative AI and AI-agent systems, including their application to large-scale AI infrastructure.

sessions.title: Your Thread Pool Is Lying to You — Sizing Concurrency from Rate Limits and Latency, Not Guesswork
sessions.description:
Here's a scenario most API teams have lived through: you set a rate limit of 40 TPS, your downstream averages 2.3 seconds per call, and your executor tops out at 25 threads. The limiter is happily approving work. The pool can't actually run it. Throughput collapses and nobody can explain why, because every component looks correctly configured in isolation.
The root cause is that teams size thread pools, HTTP connection pools, and database pools independently — usually from defaults or past incidents — instead of from the relationship between them. The math isn't complicated. It's just rarely done.
This talk covers one formula and its consequences: in-flight work equals throughput times latency. We'll apply it to executor pools, HTTP client pools, database connection pools, and distributed limiter client pools. I'll show the configuration mistakes that create each mismatch, what the symptoms look like in production, and the sizing cascade that keeps the gates consistent with each other.
If you've ever stared at a dashboard where the rate limiter says everything is fine but p99 latency is through the roof, this talk is for you.

speakers.bio: Ratul Ghosh is the Tech Lead and Architect for the Intuit Accountant Suite, an AI-native platform powered by Intuit Intelligence. Previously, he designed and led the development of GenOrchestrator, the core engine of Intuit’s GenOS platform, and successfully launched Intuit's Prompt Management and Agentic Starter Kit. Prior to GenOS, Ratul architected CoreAI and built the Feature Management Platform from the ground up. He brings extensive end-to-end experience across data engineering, MLE, platform engineering, and product engineering.
speakers.company_position: Tech lead and architect for GenOS platform

sessions.title: Don’t kill my Vibes - Simple Steps to Stay Secure when Vibe Coding
sessions.description:
The rise of vibe coding, AI-generated code, and low-/no-code tools is changing how software is built. Traditional DevSecOps assumptions (full code review, manual security gates, “shift left”) no longer cleanly apply yet prompting an LLM for “secure code” does not guarantee safe handling of data, correct auth logic, or secure outcomes in general.

This session will provide examples of how successful teams have addressed this issue and highlight the concept of using secure guardrails that notify (but don’t block) developers in their native workflow and promote the generation of secure code. Find out how to replace brittle security gates with automated guardrails, continuous checks and feedback loops that don’t slow developers. Attend to understand why security is becoming a question of intent and outcomes, not line-by-line code inspection.

speakers.bio: Isaac Evans is co-founder and CEO of Semgrep, a company dedicated to improving software security and reliability. Previously, he served as a researcher at the US Defense Department under a SFS program and at MIT Lincoln Laboratory, conducting research into binary exploitation bypasses for techniques like control-flow integrity and novel hardware defenses on new architectures like RISC-V. Isaac received his BS/MS degrees in EECS from MIT. Other interests include next-generation programming languages, secure-by-design frameworks, software-defined radio, and the intersection of cryptography and public policy.

sessions.title: Reinventing Incident Response with AI Agents and MCP
sessions.description:
When a critical service goes down at 2 AM, every second counts. But traditional incident response is a maze of manual steps: hunting through logs, correlating GitHub commits, pinging teams on Slack, and piecing together timelines while customers are impacted.
At Slack, we solved this by building AI agents that think like our best senior engineers, but work at machine speed. Using custom MCP tools integrated directly into Cursor, our system transforms a simple incident alert into a complete investigation: automatically surfacing relevant logs, identifying suspect commits, mapping blast radius, and even drafting incident communications. This production-grade automation is already saving our team multiple hours per week and dramatically improving our escal response. This session will be useful for anyone building developer productivity tools who wants to see AI deliver measurable operational impact.

speakers.bio:
Jayant Tyagi is a seasoned full-stack engineer with 13 years of experience in designing and developing high-scale applications. As a Lead Member of Technical Staff at Salesforce, he has played a pivotal role in building and optimizing enterprise applications, spearheading innovations in Salesforce, Slack, Quip, developer productivity, AI-driven financial services, and cloud-based automation. 

Jayant led the Salesforce Financial Services Cloud mortgage lending team, successfully delivering mission-critical functionality that transformed lending workflows for financial institutions. As the technical lead for Slack Sales Elevate, he architected seamless integration between Slack and Salesforce's system of record, driving significant productivity improvements for sales teams worldwide. He is a polyglot software engineer and has deep expertise in cloud platform, CI/CD, performance engineering, and system architecture. Jayant is also an inventor with multiple U.S. patents:
"Method and system for generating insights regarding a party in response to a call" [US11170381B2]
"Method and system for intelligent priming of an application with relevant priming data [US20190163664A1]
"Embedded view of third-party data and template generation for a communication platform" [US20250086591A1]

Passionate about scalable software solutions, AI-driven enterprise applications, and developer tooling, he is dedicated to enhancing productivity and performance in modern cloud ecosystems.

sessions.title: Red Teaming Your LLM App -- A Hands-On Threat Model You Can Reuse
sessions.description:
This session focuses on spotting those risks early by thinking through how an LLM app can be misused or broken.

We’ll discuss common attack patterns like prompt injection, data leakage, tool abuse, and jailbreaks, using familiar setups such as RAG pipelines, agents, and function calling. We’ll also talk about how teams intentionally test these scenarios, what usually gets missed, and which defenses actually help in production.

Attendees will have a simple, reusable threat-modeling approach and a practical checklist they can apply to their own LLM applications, without slowing down development or overcomplicating security.

speakers.bio: Saloni Garg is a Senior Machine Learning Engineer at Adobe, where she specializes in AI and machine learning. She is also a recognized author in the field, with a forthcoming book on Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to be published by De Gruyter later this year. Saloni has made significant contributions to the academic community, evidenced by her multiple IEEE publications and a published patent.

sessions.title: AI Agents are Only as Smart as their Context: Building a Real-Time Context Engine
sessions.description:
The industry has poured billions into LLMs and AI agents, yet many deployments stall in pilot because they lack one thing: fresh context. 
If your AI agent is reasoning over stale batch data or fragmented profiles, it cannot deliver real enterprise value. The missing piece isn't a bigger model, it's a real-time context engine: a streaming feature store that supplies an up-to-the-second 360° view of the customer, and that actively notifies agents when something they care about changes.
This session walks through how we built exactly that at Intuit. The Customer Data Cloud platform ingests data from hundreds of sources, processes data through config-driven Apache Flink pipelines, maintains unified profiles in a low-latency NoSQL store, and serves them via a GraphQL Read API. But the story doesn't end with the read path, every profile update publishes a real-time change notification on Kafka, which forms the backbone of an event-driven AI loop: agents and automation systems subscribe, react to changes the moment they happen, and drive in-product personalization and marketing workflows in real time.
We'll cover three ideas developers can take home:

* Context over Models: Why a streaming 360° view of the customer matters more than the specific LLM you pick — and how to architect for it.
* The Event-Driven AI Loop: Using Kafka change notifications as triggers for autonomous agentic workflows.
* Privacy-by-Design in the Stream. Enforcing user consent and asset-based access inside the streaming fabric itself, so compliance is a property of the data, not a layer bolted on top.

Expect architecture diagrams, concrete Flink-pipeline patterns, a live walkthrough of a change notification firing an agent, and the honest lessons from operating this in production.

speakers.bio: Bharat is a Lead Software Engineer at Intuit with extensive experience in building high-scale Data streaming platforms. He currently leads the development of a Customer Data Cloud, managing a high-throughput environment of 8 billion events per day, which empowers various Data driven use case and AI workflows. Bharat specializes in leveraging various Data Processing technologies to build scalable, config-driven pipelines across various enterprise data sources. He is an expert in AI, Data, Cloud technologies and enterprise platform design, passionate about solving the engineering challenges of high-cardinality data and real-time state management.

sessions.title: Where Judgment Went — and How to Put It Back
sessions.description:
What the product job becomes when you can't see inside your own product.

When AI writes the spec and runs the product, thousands of decisions get made that you never see and never signed off on — and your judgment quietly leaks out of the job. This talk traces where it goes, and lays out four concrete places to put it back: governing through rules instead of reviewing decisions, building on ground that survives the next model update, designing away the blank chat box, and treating a graceful handoff as a feature.

 The session will cover actionable strategies to keep the judgement where it matters the most, aimed at people who own or shape AI products in production including AI product managers, product operations leaders, and engineering leaders.

speakers.bio: Shruti Tiwari leads AI product development at Dell Technologies, where she builds enterprise AI systems for global customer support operations at scale. With 15 years across engineering, strategy, and product, including AI strategy at Dell and advising Fortune 500s at EY-Parthenon, she brings a practitioner's lens to the hard problems of making AI work in production. Her frameworks have been published in VentureBeat, CMSWire, Mind the Product, and The Guardian. She mentors AI founders at various accelerators and serves as Lead Mentor for mission -driven startups under GPAI/OECD program.

sessions.title: Why Infrastructure Forecasting Fails – Building a Self-Serve Forecasting Platform
sessions.description:
Most large organizations still plan infrastructure capacity using spreadsheets, manual reconciliations, and tribal knowledge. It works at small scale. It collapses at hyperscale.

As systems grow more interdependent, one team’s workload change silently creates induced demand across shared compute, storage, and platform layers. Forecasts get revised late in the cycle. Finance loses confidence. Engineering overprovisions to stay safe. Toil increases while accuracy decreases.

In this talk, I’ll walk through how to replace spreadsheet-driven capacity planning with a self-serve forecasting platform built using control plane design principles. Instead of static files and ad-hoc meetings, forecasting becomes an operational system with explicit dependency modeling, automated recomputation, validation gates, audit trails, and clear ownership boundaries.

speakers.bio: Ankur Gupta is a senior staff technical program manager in AI infrastructure at LinkedIn in San Jose, California, USA. His research interests include large-scale AI inference platforms, GPU capacity planning, and production reliability engineering. Gupta received his master’s degree in information management from Syracuse University. He is a member of IEEE.

sessions.title: From Possibility to Production: Why AI Raises the Bar for Engineering
sessions.description: AI is increasing the role of engineers to shaping systems, controls, evaluation, and trust in production. Using examples from BNY’s enterprise AI journey, including Eliza and digital employees, Leigh-Ann Russell shows that successful AI adoption depends less on model capability and more on coherence across data, architecture, governance, and human accountability. The central message is that the teams that win with AI will be the ones that build strong foundations, reuse what works, evaluate rigorously, and apply sound engineering judgment to turn possibility into durable production value.

speakers.bio:
Leigh-Ann Russell serves as the Chief Information Officer and Global Head of Engineering. In this role, she oversees a high-performing global team of technologists who are driving the development of cutting-edge digital solutions that enhance client experience, ensure security and resilience, and drive our platforms forward with innovative software, infrastructure, and technologies. She is also a member of the BNY Executive Committee.

Before joining BNY, Leigh-Ann held prominent roles at BP, including membership on BP's Executive Committee, reporting directly to the CEO. As Executive Vice President of Innovation & Engineering at BP, her responsibilities encompassed being the Chief Scientist, Chief Technology Officer, and Chief Digital Officer. She directed BP's clean technology advancements, led the expert engineering organization, managed enterprise IT infrastructure, and oversaw digital engineering, product development, data science, and design teams. Additionally, she served as BP's Chief Risk Officer.

Prior to these roles, Leigh-Ann was BP's Chief Procurement Officer, where she modernized and digitalized BP's supply chain operations and significantly enhanced supply efficiency while reducing costs during the high inflationary period of COVID. Her career has consistently focused on engineering and operations, leading large teams at executive levels.

Leigh-Ann holds a Bachelor of Science in Engineering from the University of Aberdeen, is a chartered engineer, and has earned Fellowships with the Royal Academy of Engineering, the Royal Society of Edinburgh, and the Energy Institute. She was also bestowed the honorary title of Professor of Practice by Queen’s University Belfast in 2022.

Leigh-Ann previously served as a non-executive director for Hill & Smith PLC, a FTSE 250 infrastructure company, participating in audit, nomination, and remuneration committees.

sessions.title: Inside the AI-Native Engineering Org
sessions.description: AI is changing how software gets built, and engineering organizations are changing with it: tools, workflows, and team structures are all in motion. What AI-native engineering looks like in practice - what's changing, what's working, and where it's heading.

speakers.bio: Hari Lingamagunta is the Head of Engineering for Developer Infrastructure at Atlassian, where he’s currently leading the company’s AI-first engineering transformation. Hari leads a global team building the platform, developer loop, and tooling behind Jira, Confluence, and Trello. With 18+ years across Amazon, Concur, and SAP, Hari is known for building high-performance teams and obsessing over reliability, scalability, and performance at scale.

Siwei Shen is a seasoned engineering leader currently serving as Vice President of Engineering at Coinbase where he oversees technical infrastructure, AI implementation, and blockchain platforms. 

With a career defined by scaling complex systems and leading high-performing global teams, Siwei plays a pivotal role in Coinbase’s mission to increase economic freedom in the world. His work focuses on ensuring the security, reliability, and scalability of Coinbase's core services.

Amy leads developer productivity, AI transformation and Technical Program Manager for engineering at Snowflake. Snowflake developer productivity has gone through a complete turnaround in 2024 and 2025, boosting both productivity and developer sentiment. With the advent of agentic coding, we have seen productivity more than double in 2026.

Before Snowflake, Amy led the infrastructure team of Azure SQL at Microsoft, which includes observability, supportability, deployment and release infrastructure, data science and business analytics. 

She is passionate about building the team culture where everyone feels a sense of belonging. Amy is known as the “Carrie Bradshaw of Snowflake” for her enviable shoe collection.  

Amy grew up in China, and got her BS and MS in CS from University of Maryland. In her infinite free time, she enjoys baking 🍰, traveling ✈, reading 📖 and being tiger mom 🐯 to her two tiger cubs.

Gene Kim has been studying high-performing technology organizations since 1999. He was the founder and CTO of Tripwire, Inc., an enterprise security software company, where he served for 13 years. His books have sold over 1 million copies—he is the WSJ bestselling author of The Unicorn Project, and coauthor of Wiring the Winning Organization, The Phoenix Project, The DevOps Handbook, and the Shingo Publication Award-winning Accelerate. His latest book, Vibe Coding, was released in October 2025.

In 2025, he won the Philip Crosby Medal from the American Society for Quality (ASQ) for his work in the 2023 book Wiring the Winning Organization. Since 2014, he has been the organizer of DevOps Enterprise Summit (now Enterprise AI Summit), studying the technology transformations of large, complex organizations.

sessions.title: Still on 4.8 or lower? A Practical Guide to Moving Your "Un-Migratable" .NET Apps
sessions.description:
Let’s be honest: if your .NET Framework app was easy to migrate, you would have done it three years ago. You’re likely stuck with legacy WCF services, deep dependencies on System.Web, or a NuGet graph that looks like a bowl of yarn. The .NET Upgrade Assistant is a great start, but it’s the last 20% of the migration—the part that the tools can’t automate—that actually keeps us up at night.

In this session, we’re moving past the "hello world" migration demos. We’ll look at real strategies for modernizing .NET Framework 4.x apps into .NET 8/9/10 without a complete rewrite.

We will get into the weeds on:

The "Bridge" Strategy: Using YARP (Yet Another Reverse Proxy) to migrate your app piece-by-piece rather than a "Big Bang" release.

The Dependency Trap: What to do when your critical library hasn't been updated since 2014.

Modernizing the "Un-modernizable": Strategies for dealing with legacy config systems and static state that modern .NET hates.

This isn't a theoretical talk about "embracing innovation." It’s a tactical session for developers who need to get their legacy code onto a supported, performant, and AI-ready platform without breaking the business.

speakers.bio: Isaac Levin is a Developer Advocate at JetBrains and a Microsoft MVP. He has over 15 years of experience working as a developer for the web, mostly in the Microsoft Ecosystem. Outside of work, he hosts a podcast called Coffee and Open Source where he interviews folks from across the tech industry as well as builds open-source projects like PresenceLight and GitHub Stat Tracker. He lives outside of Seattle Washington and likes to wind down from work with his wife Ariana and his 2 children Isaac and Avery.

sessions.title: Your registry can't stop a valid login. What happens then?
sessions.description:
On April 22, 2026, a threat actor used stolen Checkmarx credentials to push malicious images to a trusted Docker Hub repository. The payload quietly collected scan output, encrypted it, and exfiltrated it to attacker-controlled infrastructure. Docker's registry monitoring flagged the push for review within about half an hour, the repository was quarantined, and Docker worked side by side with Socket and Checkmarx to shut it down.

This talk is about how. Not the incident itself, but the detection model behind it: what signals fired, why no single one was enough, and what it means to build a supply chain posture where the question is not "can we prevent every breach" but "how fast can we find it and how small is the blast radius."

We cover the structural pattern behind Trivy, KICS, LiteLLM and axios: stolen credentials, legitimate publishing flows, short exposure windows. Then we get into what Docker actually does differently: provenance-linked builds, digest pinning, cooldown periods, cross-registry signal sharing, and Docker Hardened Images as the foundation that sits outside the attack surface entirely.

You leave with a concrete checklist your team can act on tomorrow, and a mental model that holds regardless of which tool gets hit next.

speakers.bio: Khushboo is a Systems Engineer at Cloudflare, a Docker Captain, and a passionate community builder. With a deep focus on AI and modern tech infrastructure, she has spoken at over 100 events globally, including Microsoft Build and C++ on Sea. She actively shares her tech insights with an audience of 200K+ on X and LinkedIn.

sessions.title: Chat with Your Data: From Natural Language to SQL
sessions.description: This session shows how to build a .NET application that lets users generate reports simply by chatting. I’ll walk through my hands-on experience that reads your database schema, understands user intent, creates secure SQL queries, executes them, and exports results to Excel and charts automatically. You’ll see how LLMs can deliver real value in everyday enterprise apps, how to handle schema discovery, query validation, and prompt design, and how to create an intuitive UX for both developers and non-technical users. Attendees will leave with practical patterns, architectural guidance, and code examples they can apply immediately to bring natural-language data access into their own systems.

speakers.bio: Alper Ebiçoğlu is a software architect and co-founder of Volosoft. He began his software career in the early 2000s. Alper is one of the creators and core maintainers of the popular open-source ABP Framework (abp.io) and ASP.NET Zero (aspnetzero.com). He has contributed to numerous technical articles and is an active speaker at international events.

sessions.title: Loop Engineering
sessions.description:
Loop Engineering and Graph Engineering are rapidly emerging as important directions for the next generation of AI agents. Our work sits at the intersection of frontier research and real-world implementation.

Rather than discussing these ideas only at a conceptual level, we build and test self-evolving agents in practice. We use real systems, long-horizon tasks, and failure cases to evaluate emerging research, understand what works, and identify what is still missing.

In this session, we will share practical lessons from building self-evolving agent systems, including how agent workflows evolve from simple loops into graphs, how these graphs can adapt and rewrite themselves, and how agents can improve not only their outputs, but also the way they learn and evolve.

The audience will gain both a clear understanding of the latest research and actionable insights from real-world experimentation.

speakers.bio:
Li Yin is the Founder and CEO of SylphAI and the creator of AdaL, a self-evolving AI coding agent designed for developers and engineering teams. 
Previously an AI researcher at Meta and NVIDIA, Li has worked across large language models, computer vision, agent systems, and developer infrastructure. 
Li also created AdalFlow, an open-source framework for building and automatically optimizing LLM applications. Her current work focuses on Loop Engineering, Graph Engineering, and translating frontier research on self-evolving agents into practical systems that help teams automate complex workflows, improve engineering productivity, and move from ideas to production faster.

sessions.title: The path to Staff Engineer and beyond - staying on the IC train
sessions.description: From the early steps that set me onto this path, to the challenges of mentorship and leadership roles, I'll discuss what it means to thrive as an Individual Contributor (IC) in a world that often pushes for management. This talk will not only reflect on my personal experiences but also provide insights and strategies for engineers who aspire to make a meaningful impact while staying true to their technical passions.

speakers.bio:
Graham Gilbert has released numerous open source tools over the years, is a board member of the Mac Admins Open Source non-profit, and is the co-founder of the Mac Admins Mentorship Program.

His work sits at the intersection of large-scale systems, senior engineering practice, and how organizations make and sustain good technical decisions over time.

In his day job, Graham is a Senior Staff Engineer at Airbnb, working across corporate infrastructure with a focus on device trust, identity, and client platforms.

sessions.title: Secure-by-Inclusion: Preventing Accessibility Barriers from Becoming Security Vulnerabilities
sessions.description:
What happens when security measures cannot be used by everyone? Any security control that is not accessible becomes a barrier, and barriers trigger unsafe workarounds that create security risks.

We face a paradox, security mechanisms designed to protect users can systematically exclude the most vulnerable populations, including people with disabilities and older adults, and this exclusion can become an exploitable vulnerability. Users facing accessibility barriers adopt insecure coping mechanisms: sharing passwords, delegating authentication to others, storing credentials insecurely, relying on weaker fallback paths, or abandoning security measures altogether. Each workaround is a predictable security failure caused not by user negligence, but by design choices that made the secure path inaccessible.

This presentation introduces Secure-by-Inclusion, a new practical approach that ensures that security controls actually function for all intended users across diverse abilities, devices, and assistive technologies.

We will walk through common patterns where security and accessibility collide, including CAPTCHAs, multi-factor authentication, biometric authentication, time-limited one-time codes, brittle account recovery flows, and inaccessible verification steps. For each pattern, we connect the accessibility failure to concrete security outcomes, then show safer, more inclusive alternatives. We will also look into the European Accessibility Act (EAA) and the WCAG 2.2 Accessible Authentication requirements, examining their implications for security design and testing.

We will learn practical techniques for incorporating inclusive evaluation into security testing practices and identify accessibility gaps as security vulnerabilities. Accessibility and security might seem like separate disciplines, but they share common goals: protecting users and ensuring inclusive, trustworthy digital experiences.

speakers.bio:
Radostina (Ina) Tsvetkova was recognized as one of Norway’s top 50 women in Tech in 2026. Ina is a Senior Advisor in Digital Accessibility and Inclusive Design at the Norwegian Directorate of Labour and Welfare (NAV). She is an Invited Expert in the W3C Accessibility Guidelines Working Group, a PhD candidate in Computer Science, a Certified Professional in Web Accessibility (CPWA), a DHS Trusted Tester, and an ISTQB Advanced Level Test Manager and Test Analyst.

Ina provides guidance on digital accessibility throughout the product development lifecycle, from early planning and design through development, testing, and procurement. She has also participated in the development of Norwegian and European accessibility standards.

Ina is a passionate advocate for an accessible and inclusive world for all, regardless of ability. 

She enjoys sharing knowledge and engaging others and has presented at conferences including CSUN 2026, Agile Testing Days 2025, a11yCamp 2025, a11yTO 2025, M-Enabling 2025, BdKCSE 2025, Social Media Days 2025, Web4All 2025, EuroSTAR 2024, Odin 2023, and Mangfold i Mai (Diversity in May) 2023 and 2025.

sessions.title: Your Agent Shipped the Fix. Did It Work?
sessions.description:
Coding agents made writing and shipping code fast. Knowing whether what shipped works in production is still manual, and most of the tooling for it assumes an SRE or DevOps team you may not have.
This hands-on workshop covers the other half of the loop. How do you give a coding agent enough production context to diagnose a real failure, and how do you verify that the fix it proposed reached production and made things better?
You get your own GitHub Codespace running a deliberately broken microservice app under live traffic. We work through detection, causal root cause, a pull request, a deploy, and verification against error rates and SLOs, with visible proof in the running app. Then you point the same loop at a repository of your own.
We use Bluebox by Dynatrace, a free helper agent, to run the loop, and leverage OpenTelemetry and your code repo as data sources.
Bring a laptop, a GitHub account, and a repo where you can install a GitHub App. We will provide the microservice app, coding agents and everything else runs in the browser.

speakers.bio: Sean O’Dell focuses on all things Developer Experience at Dynatrace. A reformed infrastructure administrator and architect, Sean brings experience from Infra, Cloud, Dev and Ops, with a passion for helping developers thrive in today’s cloud-native and AI-native world. With roots in infrastructure and a strong belief in DevOps principles, Sean advocates for a world where developers have the visibility, automation, and support they need to build, deploy, and innovate. Outside of work, Sean enjoys spending time with his family, gaming, watching TV, cheering on Arsenal, Alabama football, the New York Yankees, and the Tennessee Titans—and smoking Texas BBQ.

Andrew Norris is Principal Product Manager at Dynatrace, where he leads go-to-market for Bluebox, an agentic operations layer that connects production OpenTelemetry data to the source code behind it. Bluebox investigates anomalies, traces them to a likely root cause, and opens evidence-backed GitHub issues that coding agents can pick up, with a human approving anything that merges.

Before Dynatrace, Andrew co-founded Taplytics in Toronto (Y Combinator, W14) and was CEO of DevCycle, the OpenFeature-native feature management platform it became. Dynatrace acquired DevCycle in January 2026. Fifteen years of building developer tools has taken him from A/B testing to feature flags to the operations side of agent-written software.

His current interest is what happens after the agent ships the code: how teams give agents enough production context to plan before they prompt, and how they verify that a change actually made things better.

Johannes Vollert is Experience Lead at bluebox.ai, where he focuses on crafting meaningful user experiences. He brings a passion for design, technology, and human-centered innovation to everything he builds. 

With agents becoming increasingly embedded in everyday workflows, Johannes is particularly interested in the human side of this shift — how users navigate trust, control, and clarity when working alongside AI.

sessions.title: Insert Coin: Build Live with J.P. Morgan Payments APIs and AI
sessions.description:
Insert coin to play. Your car is on the grid and it won't move. That's the point. In this hands-on workshop, we'll build a working car by integrating real J.P. Morgan Payments APIs, and every part is a capability you wire up live with AI.

We'll guide you through the Payments Developer Portal registration that turns the key. Global Payments is the engine that finally makes the car move. Account Validation and confidence scoring are the safety systems: without them you crash on every corner, with a bad account, a failed payment, off the track. And FX rates are the drive that unlocks the international routes, San Jose to Berlin to São Paulo.

The entire thing runs on AI. You'll learn how to use J.P. Morgan Payments' open-source MCP server and skills, straight from our GitHub, so Claude Code or Copilot builds these integrations against the real API docs in minutes. Real endpoints, not hallucinated ones. Then, you'll build your own car with a live leaderboard to track all participants.

What you'll leave with:
- A J.P. Morgan Payments Developer Portal account and sandbox access
- Working integrations for Account Validation Services, FX, and Global Payments
- The MCP + skills setup to build against any API this fast on Monday

Bring your own app to wire up, or start from the sample we hand you. Insert coin. Let's go.
sessions.workshop_requirements:
No payments knowledge required!

Everything runs in a Docker image we provide: one pull and J.P. Morgan Payments' open-source MCP server + skills, API docs, and a sample app are configured. 

Please come with: 
- A laptop with Docker installed and a code editor (VS Code recommended) 
- Claude Code and/or GitHub Copilot (bring your own; guest access and setup steps available on the day for anyone without) 
- Optional: Your own app or side-project you'd like to wire up to payments. No app? We provide a sample you'll extend.

speakers.bio:
Alan Torrance is a Senior Executive Director of Engineering at JPMorganChase, based in Glasgow for the last 20 years. He leads engineering across Payments - the systems that accept, manage, and move money globally at Amazon and Uber scale, roughly $10 trillion a day. 

Most of his time now goes on the interesting bit: how humans and AI actually work together to build software. Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, agents, the lot. Not the hype - the practical "what can you do with this on Monday" version. He's a Docker Captain and sits on the OpenUK Financial Advisory Board. 

Outside the day job he founded Make It Happen, a programme inspiring 5-11 year olds to become digital creators, 100,000 children and counting. He once entered a school app competition with an intentionally terrible stick drawing of a unicorn flying to space, to prove anyone can have a go. The Space Unicorn stuck. 

Father of three, a recovering vet-turned-chemist-turned-engineer, and a firm believer that people make AI happen.

sessions.title: Intro to Agentic Workflows and an AI-enabled SDLC
sessions.description: In this workshop, we’ll build a practical AI-powered issue triage workflow using GitHub Agentic Workflows. You’ll learn how to set triage conditions, classify and enrich incoming issues, and suggest labels and routing, so the right team is tagged with the right task faster. We’ll also add a human approval step before more sensitive changes are applied, so automation stays safe and accountable. You’ll leave with a reusable template you can adapt to your own repositories and support process.
sessions.workshop_requirements:
To create and use agentic workflows, you need:

- GitHub Actions enabled for your repository.
- An account with an AI engine (agent), such as GitHub Copilot, Anthropic Claude, OpenAI Codex, or Google Gemini.
- GitHub CLI installed and authenticated

speakers.bio: Greg Larkin a Senior Service Delivery Engineer at GitHub and works with many of the largest financial firms that have adopted the GitHub platform. He is an experienced IT professional with a broad knowledge of software development, automation, version control systems, system administration, and many other disciplines. He is also an experienced mentor and technical trainer with an ability to meet his students where they are, break down complex topics and leave them with skills applicable to their job responsibilities. He takes great pride in getting his students to their own personal “a-ha!” moments. In his free time, he is an outdoor endurance sports enthusiast, and you’ll find him exploring the trails near his Northern California home.

sessions.title: Human + AI: Who Should Be in Control?
sessions.description: Explore how to design autonomous solutions by deciding what AI should do independently—and where humans should stay in control. Join our Human+AI Co-lab workshop to turn ideas into smarter, more responsible AI-powered solutions.

speakers.bio: Mirela Viersa is a Customer Innovation professional at SAP with 10+ years of experience in innovation, technology, and customer transformation. She focuses on AI, human-centered innovation, and helping organizations turn emerging technologies into impactful solutions.

sessions.title: How LinkedIn Turns AI Breakthroughs into member and customer value
sessions.description:
As state-of-the-art models become more accessible, how a company differentiates itself is shifting from the model itself to the systems around it. Nearly a decade ago, LinkedIn saw an opportunity to combine the unique signals of the Economic Graph with advances in AI to create more value for members and customers. Now, that continues today, enriching the LinkedIn experience with deeper discovery, better knowledge and insights, and improved interactions and community. Realizing that opportunity required rethinking the systems underneath LinkedIn, from our data and infrastructure to how we build and deploy AI at scale. 
In this session, Erran will discuss how owning the full stack allows LinkedIn to optimize everything from the application layer all the way down to the kernel running on the GPU, and how that approach has enabled us to optimize the stack to help deliver increasingly sophisticated AI experiences for our members and customers, while remaining disciplined in how we grow our infrastructure.

speakers.bio:
Erran Berger is Chief Technology Officer, Engineering at LinkedIn and a member of the company’s Executive Team. He leads LinkedIn’s technology vision and strategy and oversees the global engineering organization behind the world’s largest professional network, serving more than 1.3 billion members.
His team is responsible for building LinkedIn’s products and experiences for members and customers, along with the platforms and technology that power them at global scale. This includes advancing LinkedIn’s applied AI and machine learning capabilities across recommender systems and agentic experiences to make those products more intelligent, personalized, and trusted. His organization is also helping transform LinkedIn into an AI-native company by driving the adoption of AI across the business and enabling teams to work more effectively and productively.
Throughout his 17+ years at LinkedIn, Erran has helped shape the company’s technology strategy, scale its engineering organization and platforms, and drive multiple generations of product innovation.
Erran serves on the boards of JVS Bay Area and Year Up. He holds a Bachelor of Science in Computer Engineering from the University of California, San Diego.

sessions.title: Democratizing AI: Why Open Models Are Essential for the Next Era
sessions.description: While artificial intelligence represents a pivotal shift in human capability, its long-term impact hinges on how underlying technologies are governed and distributed. Open-weight AI models democratize access for startups, independent researchers, and public institutions by lowering barrier-to-entry costs and spurring decentralized innovation. By making baseline architectures accessible, open models empower organizations to build custom solutions while preserving data sovereignty and eliminating vendor lock-in. Furthermore, open weights strengthen safety and security by allowing the global research community to independently audit, stress-test, and refine systems far beyond what proprietary platforms permit. This panel explores the critical role of open-weight models, their practical applications, and their transformative influence across domains outside traditional technology, including healthcare, public policy, and education.

speakers.bio: Mitesh Patel is a developer advocate manager at NVIDIA. His team is responsible for creating workflows to showcase how developers can harness GPU acceleration in their workflows using tools and frameworks popular in the developer community. Before NVIDIA, he was a senior research scientist at Fuji Xerox Palo Alto Laboratory Inc. (a research subsidiary of Fuji Xerox), where he worked on developing indoor localization technologies for applications such as asset tracking in hospitals and delivery cart tracking in manufacturing facilities. Mitesh received his Ph.D. in Robotics from the Center of Autonomous Systems (CAS) at the University of Technology Sydney, Australia in 2014.

Joey Conway is senior director of generative AI software for enterprise at NVIDIA, where he’s helped enterprises and partners integrate AI into platforms since 2017. He graduated from the MIT Sloan School of Management and specializes in driving the adoption of advanced AI technologies.

Olivier Lacombe is a Director of Product Management at Google DeepMind. He specializes in Gemini Serving, Pre-training, Edge Computing and Open Models. He led the launch of Gemma 4 under an Apache 2.0 license. Lacombe has held leadership roles at X (the moonshot factory) and Android Intelligence during his tenure at Google. He focuses on scaling machine learning technologies server-side and at the edge and has full-cycle experience with model development.

Varun is the Head of Partner Engineering at Meta, where he leads global engineering teams driving technical adoption and developer ecosystem strategy for open-source AI models, including Muse and Llama. With over 15 years of experience building high-scale consumer software, developer platforms, and strategic partnerships, Varun specializes in bringing complex technologies from 0-to-1 and scaling them globally.

sessions.title: Fixing Git for Agents: Somewhere Between the Prompt and Production, We Lost the Plot
sessions.description:
The ticket said, “Make login faster.”

The agent touched 47 files, invented three abstractions, briefly considered rewriting everything in Rust, passed the tests and disappeared into the night.

Git knows what changed. Your tracker knows what you asked for. Everyone else is doing prompt archaeology and hoping the answer is not “the vibes were immaculate.”

This session is about capturing that missing middle: the context, decisions, dead ends and evaluations behind agent-written code, connected all the way from intent to production. Because when the code ships, “LGTM” should not be the only surviving witness.

speakers.bio:
Karthik Rameshkumar is Field CTO at Entire, where he works with developers and enterprises to reimagine the software development stack for a world in which AI agents are becoming the primary producers of code. 

Before Entire, he was Field CTO for Asia at GitHub and led Field Services across APAC West, helping some of the region’s largest organizations navigate developer platforms, DevSecOps, cloud and AI-assisted development. 

He previously held leadership roles at DigitalOcean and Twilio and was a startup co-founder. 

He is particularly interested in the increasingly valuable context around code: intent, decisions, failed attempts, and how humans and agents collaborate to ship software.

sessions.title: API = Some REST and HTTP, right? RIGHT?!
sessions.description:
Let's be honest: many of our so-called "REST" APIs aren't REST. They're just JSON-RPC over HTTP, with versioning challenges, brittle integrations, clumsy error handling, and a maintenance burden we all know too well.

Let's do something about this! We’ll go straight to the patterns that matter in production, tackling the real-world challenges head-on: building evolvable versioning strategies, designing sane error responses, providing clear API contracts, and demystifying the practical use of hypermedia (HATEOAS).

You'll leave with practical, battle-tested approaches for building APIs that are maintainable and scalable. We'll also discuss when to use REST and when alternatives like GraphQL or gRPC are a better tool for the job. All demos use Jakarta EE and MicroProfile, but the patterns can be applied to any modern web stack of your choosing.

speakers.bio: Experienced Software Engineer | Architect | Keynote & Public Speaker | Java Champion | Google Developer Expert for Cloud | Docker Captain | Oracle ACE Pro | Community Leader | Mentor | Ex-leader of JavaZone and Norwegian JUG – javaBin.

sessions.title: Making (and Breaking) Agents by Adding 1,000 MCP Tools
sessions.description:
What happens when you actually try to use MCP at scale? In this talk, I'll build an agent live on stage, connect it to 1,000+ tools via MCP, and show exactly what breaks: context explosion, ambiguous routing, and security vulnerabilities from indirect prompt injection.

Then I'll show how to fix it. I'll cover dynamic tool discovery (reducing context from 500 tools to 1-2), code-mode execution, and why every MCP tool is a trust boundary your security team should care about.

This isn't specifically MCP advocacy as thes issues go beyond MCP and affect any agent that needs tools (and any modern agent is very tool hungry). It's a practitioner's guide to what works (and doesn't) when you scale MCP tools.

speakers.bio: Guillaume Lebedel is CTO and co-founder of StackOne, the integration infrastructure platform for AI agents backed by GV. StackOne connects agents to 200+ connectors with 11,000+ enterprise-ready actions, all exposed via MCP and other Agent compatible protocols. Before StackOne, Guillaume built large-scale event & data infrastructure powering ML-driven trading systems and B2B SaaS. He writes about the practical challenges of scaling tool use in agentic systems at stackone.com/blog.

sessions.title: rm -rf: Horror Stories From Unsandboxed AI Agents (and How Docker Fixes This)
sessions.description:
"I panicked instead of thinking. I destroyed months of your work in seconds." That's a Replit agent, after wiping a production database during an active code freeze. "I have failed you completely and catastrophically." That's Gemini CLI, after silently overwriting every file in a developer's project.
These aren't edge cases. Between July 2025 and February 2026, documented incidents include a Claude Code session that ran terraform destroy on 2.5 years of student data for 79,000 learners, a supply chain attack that weaponized --dangerously-skip-permissions to steal 2,349 secrets from developers, and a three-layer sandbox escape where Claude Code reasoned its way past procfs restrictions, bubblewrap, and the ELF dynamic linker without a jailbreak.
The flags are warnings dressed as features: --dangerously-skip-permissions, --yolo, --trust-all-tools. Developers use them anyway because approving 100 permission prompts per hour isn't a workflow, it's babysitting.
Docker Sandboxes (sbx) changes this. Each agent session runs in a microVM with its own kernel, Docker daemon, and network stack. The agent gets full autonomy. Your host stays untouched.
Attendees will leave knowing why container isolation is architecturally insufficient for AI agents, how the sbx isolation model works (microVM, network policy, credential proxy), and a concrete pattern for running agents in full YOLO mode safely.

speakers.bio: Rishab is a Staff Developer Evangelist at Twilio, part-time cloud professor at St. Lawrence College, co-author of Learn to Cloud, AWS Community Builder, and a Microsoft MVP. He is passionate about helping people get into cloud and sharing his learnings from his time in cloud, DevOps and now DevRel.

sessions.title: Physical AI: 5 Things You Can Build That Aren't Another Chatbot
sessions.description: This session walks through five working projects that show what AI looks like when it leaves the screen: vibe-coding 3D-printable parts in OpenSCAD, generating firmware and PCB layouts for custom IoT devices, an AI-driven home automation stack over MQTT, physical controllers that turn button presses into agent calls, and a "renascent" interface that rewrites its own code on voice command and hot-reloads live.

speakers.bio:
Vinicius Senger is a technologist, builder, entrepreneur, and Senior Technical Evangelist for Startups at AWS. He began coding at eight years old and has spent more than three decades turning emerging technologies into products, companies, communities, and unconventional machines.

He is the founder of Globalcode and The Developers Conference, a Java Champion, and a two-time Duke’s Choice Award winner. His work spans AI agents, serverless computing, Java, IoT, robotics, physical computing, and new human-computer interfaces. At AWS, Vinicius works with startups, founders, and communities to help ambitious ideas move from prototype to production—and to explore what becomes possible when AI moves beyond the screen.

sessions.title: Agentic Code Validation and Repository Automation with Agentic Workflows
sessions.description: In this session we'll provide an overview of the GitHub Agentic Workflows framework, which provides out of the box security and control for using Copilot agents in the CI pipeline (GitHub Actions) and to perform repository maintenance. You can use AI agents in the pipeline with human in the loop to perform every step of the SDLC - agents can farm user feedback for potential features, investigate research opportunities, make code changes, perform maintenance tasks like writing documentation and tests, and can self improve and upgrade to new models over time. Agents can also perform cross repository maintenance like notifying downstream teams of deprecations or API changes, and can be used to automate processes like CVE exceptions or new dependency approvals. At the end of this session you'll understand the breadth of automation opportunities available, how the Agentic Workflows framework can help you implement secure autonomous agents in the pipeline, and how to get started building your Agentic SDLC.

speakers.bio: Jose Palafox is a Field Copilot Specialist at GitHub. He helps the world's largest enterprises to maximize their investment from GitHub Copilot. He works with executives and engineering leaders to understand the end to end vision for a secure, agentic SDLC and how GitHub and Github Copilot helps maximize return on your AI investment.

sessions.title: Testing AI Workflows Locally with Testcontainers
sessions.description:
AI features now involve agents, tools, databases, and external systems working together. Most teams still test them manually or rely on mocks that do not reflect real behavior.
In this session, I will show how to test AI workflows using Testcontainers and real dependencies running locally.
We will build a setup where an AI agent interacts with tools and services, and run tests against it in a reproducible environment. You will see how to spin up dependencies on demand and validate real interactions instead of guessing.
This session is focused on making AI systems testable, reliable, and easier to develop.

speakers.bio: Solutions Engineer focused on cloud-native architecture and developer experience, with a strong passion for developer productivity, testing, and fast feedback in the inner loop. Former Customer Success Engineer for Testcontainers Cloud and Quality Architect. Open-source contributor and conference speaker with a bias toward practical demos, testing, and real-world engineering problems.

sessions.title: MicroAgents: The Microservices of the Agentic Era
sessions.description:
The microservices revolution gave us a hard-won set of principles: small services with well-defined contracts, owned by independent teams, composable into larger systems, replaceable without rewriting the world. The agentic AI era is rediscovering these lessons the hard way. Most enterprises today are building agents the way we built monoliths fifteen years ago: each agent a self-contained stack with its own conversation store, its own auth, its own observability, unable to talk to the agent built down the hall.

There is a better pattern. We call it a MicroAgent, and it is to the agentic world what a microservice is to the API world. A MicroAgent is a lightweight, independently-deployable package consisting of two things: an MCP server that exposes domain-specific tools, and a prompt template that encodes domain expertise. That is the entire contract. No session management. No streaming code. No auth boilerplate. Those concerns belong to a shared Base Agent Service, the way platform concerns belong to a service mesh or API gateway.

The Model Context Protocol is the API contract that makes this work. MCP is not just a tool-calling format. It is the service boundary that lets MicroAgents from different teams compose into super-agents through configuration alone. The Base Agent routes tool calls over MCP, fetches prompt templates via HTTP with conditional caching, and merges state updates from _meta fields in tool responses.

This talk walks through the architecture: MicroAgents as units of ownership, MCP as the contract, shared infrastructure as the substrate, and the multi-agent composition patterns that emerge once these boundaries are clean.

speakers.bio:
Ashish Shubham is a Fellow/VP of Engineering at ThoughtSpot, where he has spent nearly a decade architecting industry-defining AI and analytics products. He is an IEEE Senior Member and author of the book “Architecting AI Data systems”. 

He is the creator of ThoughtSpot Embedded, a leading embedded analytics platform powering multiple Fortune 500 apps worldwide. He also co-architected ThoughtSpot’s AI Analyst, Spotter, and led the company’s first Agentic MCP Server integration, redefining how AI agents securely work with enterprise data. 

Ashish holds multiple patents, has published widely read technical articles, serves on the committee of top AI conferences and frequently speaks at industry forums.

sessions.title: Vibe Coding Accessibility
sessions.description: This session explores how today’s most powerful AI-based coding tools are shaping the future of accessible technology. With tools like GitHub Copilot, ChatGPT, and other AI code assistants becoming mainstream, developers face both new opportunities and new risks. This session will provide a candid overview of the leading AI coding platforms and evaluate how well they support accessibility—from generating accessible code patterns to avoiding common pitfalls that exclude users with disabilities. We’ll also discuss their role in remediation: Can AI help fix inaccessible code, or does it introduce new challenges? To ground the discussion, we’ll showcase real-world examples of accessible web and native mobile products built with the help of AI tools. Attendees will walk away with practical insights on what AI coding tools can (and can’t) do today, best practices for ensuring accessible outcomes, and a vision for how accessibility professionals and developers can “vibe” with AI to build more inclusive digital experiences.

speakers.bio: With 20 years of experience in web development, usability, and accessibility, Karl Groves is widely regarded as a pragmatic solution-finder and thought leader in the accessibility industry. In his role as accessibility consultant at AFixt, Karl focuses on pragmatic and efficient ways of improving the accessibility of websites and software.

sessions.title: Govern the Runtime, Not the Agent: One Control Plane for Every Model, Every Harness
sessions.description:
The industry is converging on a multi-agent, multi-model world. Teams are landing on a few facts at once: the best model changes every couple of months, it makes no economic sense to call a frontier model to classify a ticket, and your unique workflows may sometimes need custom models. So you end up running many models across many harnesses.

This makes trust the defining challenge of today. While harnesses do ship some guardrails, each one governs only its own traffic, and we are already seeing where that breaks down. Agents route around rails the harness cannot see, and the rails themselves shift underneath you whenever the model vendor ships an update. Safety cannot depend on the agent making the right decision, or on someone else's release schedule.

Tushar Jain, CTO at Docker, makes the case for a meta-runtime: the layer below all your harnesses, covering agent execution, tool calls, credential usage, scoped permissions, token spend. A meta-runtime makes it possible to control and have visibility into all your agents, no matter what model or what harness.

speakers.bio: Tushar Jain is the Chief Technology Officer at Docker, leading the work of building trust into the infrastructure agents run on. He is responsible for advancing systems that let AI agents operate autonomously without gaining uncontrolled access to sensitive data and services. His work applies Docker's experience with portable software to an emerging challenge: enforcing security boundaries around agents whose plans and permissions can change while they work.

sessions.title: Building Enterprise Software for AI Agents
sessions.description: Enterprise software is getting a second kind of user: agents that log in, call APIs, and complete tasks on behalf of people. Products built for human eyes and hands work badly for machine users - interfaces, permissions, integrations, and pricing all assume a person on the other end. What it takes to make enterprise software work for agents, across products, APIs, and the businesses behind them.

speakers.bio: Gil Feig is the Co-Founder and CTO of Merge, the leading provider of agentic tools and customer-facing integrations for frontier LLMs, Fortune 500 organizations, and B2B SaaS companies. Previously, Gil was the Head of Engineering at Untapped and worked as a software engineer at Wealthfront and LinkedIn. A graduate of Columbia University, he now lives and works in San Francisco.

Nitin Eusebius is a Principal Solutions Architect and Generative AI Tech Lead at Amazon Web Services (AWS) with over 20 years of experience in enterprise technology, cloud architecture, and large-scale digital platforms. He specializes in AI Engineering, Generative and Agentic AI, helping organizations design secure, resilient, and production-ready systems. He designs production-scale AI systems and helps organizations move AI initiatives from experimentation to scalable, real-world deployment, aligning AI capabilities with modern engineering and delivery practices. Nitin has led complex modernization and transformation programs, advised executive stakeholders, and driven architectural strategies across cloud-native, hybrid, and distributed environments. He actively leads field initiatives, contributes to thought leadership and blogs, and publishes on AWS official channels and community platforms. Nitin holds all AWS Certifications and 4 NVIDIA Generative AI certifications and is a frequent speaker at AWS re:Invent, re:Inforce, NVIDIA GTC, AI Dev Summit, and global AWS Summits.

Sachin Kaura is Vice President and Chief Architect for AI Research, Experimentation and Evaluation at SAP Business AI. He leads the architecture and evaluation of agentic AI systems, translating emerging research into secure and reliable enterprise products and SAP Ecosystem. As the founder of SAP Joule for Consultants, he has brought generative AI grounded in trusted enterprise knowledge to SAP's consulting ecosystem. His work focuses on making enterprise software ready for AI agents by addressing identity, permissions, APIs, business context, orchestration, observability and governance. This enables AI agents to safely complete complex tasks across business systems and deliver measurable business value.
speakers.company_position: Vice President & Chief Architect AI Research, Experimentation & Evaluation

speakers.bio: James Watters is the CTO of the Tanzu division at Broadcom Inc., a role he assumed in November 2023 following the company's acquisition. Previously At VMWare, he served as CTO of Modern Application Platforms. Watters was previously SVP of Product and Strategy at Pivotal Software, and a founding leader of the company.

Matt Burns is Director of Editorial at Insight Media Group, where he oversees The New Stack, Roadmap.sh, and Towards Data Science — three platforms that collectively help millions of developers figure out what to learn next. Previously, he spent 16 years at TechCrunch, leading editorial teams and events, hosting shows and pitch-offs, and interviewing newsmakers who shaped the world through technology and politics.

sessions.title: The Agentic Engineering Loop
sessions.description:
If vibe coding is giving in to vibes and one-shotting code that you are likely to throwaway, then agentic engineering is the deliberate practice of designing systems to help agents create high-quality code that gets better over time. 

In this talk, we cover the agentic engineering loop and how to leverage it to multiply your output at every phase. We cover the new challenges that arise when agents write most of the code and we provide useful mental models for thinking about software development in the world of agents. 

This talk is for anyone that wants to adopt an agent-first approach to software development and get the most out of agents and the latest frontier models.

speakers.bio: Hi, I'm Kevin. I'm a member of technical staff at OpenAI, working on MCPs, apps, and agents. Prior to OpenAI, I founded Dendron, a YC-backed startup to help humans manage context. In my spare time, I run long distances and dance salsa.

sessions.title: Build Fast, Deploy Faster: Cross Platform AI development in 2026
sessions.description:
Quality is a function of iteration. 

Expo has become the standard for cross platform application development because it accelerates the process of building, distributing, and deploying your applications. 

And we just made that iteration cycle exponentially faster. 

With the introduction of Echo, you can now use your preferred coding assistant to prompt beautiful, cutting edge apps into existence from the palm of your hand. 

In this talk I'll explain what the modern application development experience can look like and why there will be more, better apps because of it.

speakers.bio: Charlie is the CEO and Co-Founder of Expo. Previously he was an early engineer at Facebook and then became the co-founder of Quora where he realized that mobile apps were too difficult to build. Which is how the idea for Expo was born.

sessions.title: Performance Engineering in the Age of AI
sessions.description:
Profiling has long been an esoteric skill that only few people ever took the time to learn. The tools are clunky, and the visualizations difficult to read. However, at it's core, performance engineering is very methodical, and follows a lot of rules. AI has also gotten very good at writting code, so in an abundance of luck, they are a match made in heaven!

In this session Frederic will walk through the incredible integration between AI and Profiling and show how performance engineering is now accessible to every engineer regardless of proficiency.

speakers.bio: Frederic was the founder and CEO of Polar Signals (acquired by Dash0). Before founding Polar Signals, he was a senior principal engineer and the main architect for all things Observability at Red Hat, which he joined through the CoreOS acquisition. Frederic is a Prometheus and Thanos maintainer as well as until recently was the tech lead for the special interest group for instrumentation in Kubernetes. In a previous life, he was a security researcher working on key management solutions as well as intrusion detection systems. When not working on software Frederic enjoys obsessing over brewing a perfect cup of coffee.

sessions.title: Managing Abuse in the Era of AI Agents
sessions.description: Agentic attacks will be a fact of life going forward. AI agents are now superhuman in some areas of cybersecurity, and attackers have access too. This talk will review the current state of the art in defending online services against agentic attacks, and near-term predictions for what to expect soon.

speakers.bio: CEO of Intuition Machines, operators of hCaptcha. hCaptcha protects millions of sites and apps from fraud and abuse like account takeovers and payment fraud. Used to stop both entirely human and entirely automated attacks, hCaptcha takes a uniquely privacy-preserving approach to online security.

sessions.title: Managing GPUs by Just Asking, Infrastructure in the Age of MCP
sessions.description: This talk explores the shift from writing software to operating it through conversation, in which the Model Context Protocol enables an agent to drive real infrastructure APIs through natural language. Using Runpod's MCP servers connected to an AI agent like Claude Code or Cursor, the audience will experience infrastructure-by-conversation in action and you will see me listing running pods, spinning up a GPU training pod, standing up an autoscaling serverless endpoint, and shutting it all down just by typing what they want, and learn about the opportunities and challenges that exist in this new paradigm, as well as how they might impact developer communities like this one.

speakers.bio:
Jessica Garson Beauchmin leads community at Runpod and has spent their career helping developers get real work done with new tools. They’ve held developer advocacy and community roles at companies including Twitter and Elastic, focusing on what developers actually need: clear documentation, working examples, authentic advocacy grounded in the developer experience, and feedback loops that bring developer insights to the people building the product.

Since 2017, she has been active in NYC's creative and live-coding scenes, performing live-coded noise music and visuals as Messica Arson, using modular synthesizers and voice samples across North America, Europe, and Asia. She organizes RAID NYC, contributes to LivecodeNYC, and speaks regularly at conferences including DevRelCon, All Things Open, PyCon, Write the Docs, and PyOhio. Working across Python, JavaScript, DevOps, and creative coding, she writes and builds to make complex systems feel understandable, memorable, and useful.

sessions.title: Beyond Vibe Coding: An AI Builder’s Guide to Migrating 10k+ React Components
sessions.description: Ads Manager powers 84% of Meta's Ads Revenue, but its decade-old codebase was stuck on React class components — blocking modern patterns like hooks, Relay, and React Compiler. Manual migration of 10k+ components class to functional component was impractical. In this talk, I'll show how we built an AI codemod pipeline using LLMs that achieved a 5x speedup, migrating 3k+ components with a 99.6% success rate. I'll cover the tradeoffs between AST and AI codemods, how to classify components by complexity for targeted prompts, and the grading/eval strategies that made non-deterministic AI agents production-ready.

speakers.bio:
As a Senior Software Engineer at Meta, I thrive at the intersection of complex systems, web performance, and developer experience. My career is defined by a commitment to engineering excellence—from driving large-scale architectural transformations to leveraging emerging AI technologies to solve the industry's toughest challenges.

Currently, I contribute to the architecture of Meta's Ads Manager, the world's largest React application. My work centers on ensuring top-tier performance and reliability for this mission-critical platform, employing rigorous observability practices to minimize browser crashes and optimize user experience at scale.

My recent focus centers on "AI-assisted engineering." By building production-grade AI codemod pipelines, I have demonstrated how non-deterministic agents can be constrained to perform reliable, deterministic transformations—migrating over 3,000 components with a 99.6% success rate, significantly reducing technical debt while maintaining velocity for over 1,200 active developers.

With a background spanning engineering leadership at Groupon to infrastructure work at Meta, I specialize in re-architecting consumer-facing applications and fostering high-performance engineering cultures. Whether it's diagnosing complex performance bottlenecks or designing scalable AI-driven development workflows, I am driven by the goal of making engineering more efficient, reliable, and developer-friendly.

sessions.title: Loop Engineering: Designing and Observing the Loops That Run Your Agents With Opik
sessions.description:
A prompt encodes one way to solve a problem. Change that input and that path often breaks. Loop engineering targets the process instead. You design the cycle the agents runs: it acts, checks the result, and decides whether to keep going. The agent finds a path rather than following one you scripted. 

This talk covers how to design those loops deliberately. We'll walk through the anatomy of an agent loop, why stopping conditions deserve to be treated as a first-class design decision, how to tell a recoverable error from a hard blocker, and why the most reliable exit conditions lean on deterministic checks rather than asking the model to grade its own work.

The other half of the problem is visibility. A loop you can't see inside is a loop you can't debug. Using Opik, an open-source observability and evaluation platform, we'll instrument an agent's loop so you can trace what happens at each iteration, measure where it breaks down, and set up the evaluation that tells you whether a change actually made things better.

You'll leave with a clear mental model for loop design and a practical workflow for observing and improving agent behavior before it reaches your users.

speakers.bio:
Abby Morgan an AI Growth Engineer and Developer Advocate at Comet. She helps teams improve their AI systems through observability and monitoring, with a focus on LLMs and agents.

Her work spans LLM research, agent optimization, and technical education.  She writes tutorials and articles, run workshops and hackathons, and mentor in the AI/ML space. She also authored the Prompt Engineering for Vision Models course with DeepLearning.AI.

sessions.title: The AI Proving Ground
sessions.description: Enterprise AI spending keeps climbing, yet most pilots never make it into production. Between the demo and the deployment sits the hard part: testing against real workloads instead of benchmarks, security and compliance review, proving ROI beyond the proof of concept, and deciding who signs off. How organizations evaluate AI before trusting it in production - what a rigorous evaluation looks like, which criteria actually predict success, and what separates the pilots that ship from the ones that quietly die.

speakers.bio: Anna Maria Brunnhofer-Pedemonte (AMB) is CEO and Co-Founder of Impact.AI, the platform teams use to move AI Products out of the lab and into production. Business-context-grounded evals, functionality testing, in-code-improvement and runtime enforcement in one loop. Impact AI operates in the real world, from securing the Hera Space Companion by European Space Agency and Red Bull TMS to Fortune 500 enterprise deployments in finance and media. Before that, AMB founded one of the first HCAI labs globally and spent more than a decade in applied AI, knowing the next decade belongs to the AI Product Builders.

David Hefter leads BlackRock's AI transformation for the Global Fixed Income investment team. After studying AI at Columbia he has spent his career of over two decades at BlackRock. For the past few years, David has been advancing firmwide AI adoption through engagement, training, and community building, including publishing a weekly internal AI newsletter.

Li Fan is Chief AI Officer at Circle, where she leads the company's AI strategy and enterprise-wide transformation. She partners across every function to embed AI into products, operations, and decision-making, redesigning workflows and organizational capabilities to drive measurable business impact.
