In his role as Head of Firefox, Ajit leads the development of the Firefox strategy, ensuring it’s a delightful experience for current users, as well as those of the future. Ajit has years of product management experience from Square, Google, and immediately prior to joining Mozilla, Meta, where he was responsible for monetization of WhatsApp and overseeing Meta’s business messaging platform. Earlier in his career, he was a co-founder and CEO of Adku, a venture-funded machine learning platform that was acquired by Groupon. Ajit has a BS from the University of Texas at Austin. He is based in the Bay Area.

Ajita is a Staff Technical Program Manager at Google, leading programs within Google Maps to make roads safer and enhance the navigation experience for billions of customers globally. Prior to her role at Google, she successfully led major product and technical product programs at industry-leading companies, including Coinbase and DocuSign, consistently delivering products that achieved global impact and improved people's lives through robust, well-executed engineering initiatives.

With deep experience in navigating high-complexity products and engineering systems from vision through to global scale, Ajita's career has been dedicated to driving impact through product and technical program leadership.

Ajita is a dedicated mentor and thought leader who is passionate about fostering inclusive product and engineering cultures and inspiring the next generation of technical leaders.

Akshay is the Field CTO at Antithesis, a testing platform to help agents produce bug-free code. In the past, he’s been an infra and platform engineer at Uber, Microsoft, other people’s silly startups, and his own silly startup. Apart from computers, he likes bicycles and coffee.

Alan Torrance is a Senior Executive Director of Engineering at JPMorganChase, based in Glasgow for the last 20 years. He leads engineering across Payments - the systems that accept, manage, and move money globally at Amazon and Uber scale, roughly $10 trillion a day. 

Most of his time now goes on the interesting bit: how humans and AI actually work together to build software. Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, agents, the lot. Not the hype - the practical "what can you do with this on Monday" version. He's a Docker Captain and sits on the OpenUK Financial Advisory Board. 

Outside the day job he founded Make It Happen, a programme inspiring 5-11 year olds to become digital creators, 100,000 children and counting. He once entered a school app competition with an intentionally terrible stick drawing of a unicorn flying to space, to prove anyone can have a go. The Space Unicorn stuck. 

Father of three, a recovering vet-turned-chemist-turned-engineer, and a firm believer that people make AI happen.

Hi! I'm Aldan, and I'm passionate about technology and research. I studied Computer Science in Spain, France and Switzerland, founded a few associations and contributed to open source projects. I've also been lucky enough to get some recognition for leadership and academic achievements, and I love learning from the community and participating in events. Currently, I'm working on research that combines Natural Language Processing and Knowledge Graphs, two topics I'm always happy to talk about!

Alex Garnett is doing DevRel at Bluesky! Prior to that, he was a Staff Developer Advocate at Temporal, and before that, he was a Senior Technical Writer at DigitalOcean. He knows too much about ffmpeg.

Alex's favorite title is Robot Scuba Instructor, which he earned building robotic submarines. (He is also a normal, human Scuba Instructor.) Based in Denver, Colorado, Alex is a Developer Educator at Twilio on the Ecosystem team. He brings experience founding startups along with a master’s degree in Robotics and Artificial Intelligence to creating media and experiences that help companies build amazing customer experiences. When not filming YouTubes or hiding puzzles in Twilio ads, you will find Alex doing Improv, reading sci-fi and fantasy, or chasing his toddlers.

Alex Olivier is the Co-founder & CPO at Cerbos, an open-source authorization platform, and co-chair of the OpenID AuthZEN working group, which standardizes fine-grained authorization. He specializes in authorization systems, with a recent focus on workload identity and AI security.

With over a decade of experience building and scaling authorization systems at Microsoft, Qubit, Zencargo, and multiple startups, Alex has published extensively on securing Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and AI agents. A frequent speaker at events on authorization, AI, security, and identity, including KubeCon, Google Cloud NEXT, Identiverse, and EIC, he combines standards development with practical implementation experience, focusing on the future of authorization for traditional applications, distributed workloads, and emerging AI systems.

Alex is the Senior Vice President of AI and Developer Platforms at Arm, where he is responsible for helping developers build their best AI experiences and software applications on the most ubiquitous computing platform on the planet, from Cloud to Edge. He has more than 25 years of experience inventing, transforming, managing, and deploying cutting-edge technology in machine learning (ML) and AI across industries to create products that are useful for people. Prior to Arm, Alex served as Vice President of Product Management for Machine Learning at Google, responsible for TensorFlow and the technologies and infrastructures that power Google’s machine learning and AI services.

I am the Founder and CEO of 8reasons Digital GmbH, a UX agency specialized in complex B2B and enterprise applications. Together with my 15-person team, I design digital products for internal platforms, data-driven tools and sophisticated software systems where UX needs to create real business impact.

My mindset is simple: UX is not decoration, it’s a strategic lever for efficiency, adoption and growth.

8reasons Digital is part of the iits Group with more than 160 experts combining UX excellence with deep technological expertise.

I lead my company fully remote between Germany and Peru and stand for modern leadership built on clarity, trust and responsibility.

Alexandra Lato is the Vice President of Product at Stack Overflow, where she leads product strategy across design, engineering and community to build the trusted knowledge system teams rely on in the age of AI. She brings over 13 years of experience building and scaling product-led businesses across developer platforms, tools and enterprise software, with a focus on intuitive, measurable products that drive adoption. Prior to Stack Overflow, Alex held product leadership roles at GitHub and Booking.com.

Alexandre is the CTO at Les-Tilleuls.coop and a leading figure in the PHP ecosystem.

A major player in the open-source world, he is an active member of the Symfony and FrankenPHP Core Teams and a core maintainer of the PHP language itself. His expertise in crafting robust, high-quality code is distilled in his book, "Clean Code in PHP".

As an international speaker at conferences like SymfonyLive and ForumPHP, Alexandre shares his deep insights on topics ranging from cybersecurity to object-oriented programming theory, all connected by a common thread: designing maintainable software for the decades to come.

Alija Nuredini is the Founder and CEO of Pistacio and DesignOps Lead at 8reasons Digital, a design agency. He built Pistacio to solve a problem he saw firsthand: service businesses juggling too many disconnected tools for time tracking, task management, expenses, and team coordination. Combining a founder's instinct with a builder's hands-on approach, he shipped a full operations platform serving real service teams. He has the scope decisions, dead ends, and lessons to prove it.

Alper Ebiçoğlu is a software architect and co-founder of Volosoft. He began his software career in the early 2000s. Alper is one of the creators and core maintainers of the popular open-source ABP Framework (abp.io) and ASP.NET Zero (aspnetzero.com). He has contributed to numerous technical articles and is an active speaker at international events.
Amjad Masad

I’m Amjad Shaikh - a technology and innovation leader who helps enterprises evolve into truly AI-Native organizations.

Over the past several years at ServiceNow, I’ve led our transformation from traditional digital workflows to agentic, self-learning systems — architecting the foundation for AI employees, decision observability, and knowledge-driven automation.

My focus has always been at the intersection of technology architecture, organizational design, and human potential — building systems where humans and AI agents co-create outcomes.

I’ve driven multiple enterprise-scale implementations, from AgentX (AI Agents that creates AI Agents) and AI Decision Observability to Knowledge and Workflow Data Fabric integration with Snowflake — directly improving self-service rates, decision transparency, and productivity across tens of thousands of employees.

I define success not by how many models we deploy, but by how many high-quality decisions the enterprise can make each day. That’s the true metric of AI maturity.

My next chapter is about scaling this philosophy beyond one organization — shaping how Fortune-500 enterprises design their AI Leadership Stack: Governance, Decision, and Execution layers working in harmony.

In short — I build organizations where algorithms lead responsibly, humans lead wisely, and together we redefine what’s possible.

Amy leads developer productivity, AI transformation and Technical Program Manager for engineering at Snowflake. Snowflake developer productivity has gone through a complete turnaround in 2024 and 2025, boosting both productivity and developer sentiment. With the advent of agentic coding, we have seen productivity more than double in 2026.

Before Snowflake, Amy led the infrastructure team of Azure SQL at Microsoft, which includes observability, supportability, deployment and release infrastructure, data science and business analytics. 

She is passionate about building the team culture where everyone feels a sense of belonging. Amy is known as the “Carrie Bradshaw of Snowflake” for her enviable shoe collection.  

Amy grew up in China, and got her BS and MS in CS from University of Maryland. In her infinite free time, she enjoys baking 🍰, traveling ✈, reading 📖 and being tiger mom 🐯 to her two tiger cubs.

An Phan is a Senior Data Infrastructure Engineer working at the intersection of data, infrastructure, robotics, decision-making systems, and machine learning.

His work focuses on building the reliability layer beneath AI systems, where telemetry, reproducibility, and historical truth matter more than novelty. He designs architectures for sensor-rich and autonomous systems operating across cloud and edge environments, where signals are incomplete, environments change, and failures often cannot be replayed once they are lost.

Over the years, he has worked across industrial AI, manufacturing, maritime systems, and robotics, where many production failures emerged not from the model itself, but from fragmented ownership, missing telemetry, and systems that could no longer explain reality over time.

Anagha Rumade is an Applied AI/ML Lead pioneering production-scale generative AI systems at the intersection of search, natural language processing, and large language models. She currently leads a machine learning team architecting an innovative internal search chatbot system powered by sophisticated LLM workflows, bringing cutting-edge retrieval and agentic AI to thousands of users.

A recognized thought leader in AI/ML, Anagha was a featured speaker at Grace Hopper Celebration 2025 and holds multiple patents as an inventor in the AI/ML field. Her expertise spans GenAI, NLP, LLMs, MLOps, large-scale data engineering, and team leadership.

Beyond her technical achievements, Anagha is deeply committed to expanding access to technology—dedicating her time to teaching underprivileged children and empowering the next generation of technologists. She brings both deep technical expertise and a passion for inclusive innovation to every stage and classroom.

LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/anagharumade/
Google Scholar: https://scholar.google.com/scholar?as_vis=0&q=Anagha+Rumade&hl=en&as_sdt=7,33

Anahita Havewala is a Development Architect in the Office of the CTO at SAP, where she defines technical strategy and hands-on execution for enterprise AI runtimes, multi-agent orchestration, and real-time streaming voice systems. A holder of multiple AI/ML patents, she specializes in taking frontier AI models and grounding them in resilient, cloud-native enterprise platforms. With over a decade of software architecture experience, Anahita bridges high-level executive strategy with low-level engineering execution to ship low-latency, production-grade AI infrastructure at global scale.
speakers.company_position: Expert Development Architect Office of the CTO

speakers.bio: Andrea Griffiths is a Senior Developer Advocate at GitHub. She hosts The GitHub Podcast, Open Source Friday, and GitHub Checkout, and writes Main Branch, a weekly newsletter on developer fundamentals. She learned to code through freeCodeCamp in 2016 while raising her kids, made a career pivot in her mid-30s, and has been building developer tools ever since. Based on Florida's west coast, she creates content in English and Spanish and has deep ties to the Latin American developer community.

Andrea Muttoni is CEO of DATA Foundation, the infrastructure layer to source, verify, and license AI training data at scale. With over a decade of experience at the intersection of technology, product development, and developer ecosystems, Andrea has built and scaled products used by millions. Previously, he led the technical product management team responsible for developing Amazon's Alexa and Kindle, and led developer relations at Dapper Labs, overseeing initiatives across the Flow blockchain.

At DATA Foundation, Andrea's leadership is focused on building the infrastructure that gives frontier AI labs access to rights-cleared, provenance-verified training data at scale - combining sourcing, auditability, and contributor compensation on one set of rails.

He brings a deep technical background to the role, having co-authored a research paper on AI agent-to-agent transactions involving intellectual property (Agent TCP/IP) onchain, and has spoken at global stages including AWS re:Invent and WebSummit.

Andreas spent most of his professional life and a career of over 25 years integrating "backend" applications. First inside or between Enterprises and Startups directly, then - "in the cloud".
Before that, Andreas dabbled with Virtual Reality in the 90s. In 2013, he integrated an innovation focus into his work - from Kinect for Windows, Microsoft HoloLens, and Mixed Reality, to a strong focus on Applied Artificial Intelligence. Andreas told audiences years before ChatGPT to look at Generative AI.
He cannot stop talking about technology, which apparently some people like so Microsoft gave him the MVP award. Because he has shown leadership can advise C-levels and business, he also got accepted into the ranks of the Microsoft Regional Directors .
Andreas helps customers as a trusted advisor, external CTO and innovation consultant, he also produces exciting applications and solutions with a great team of skilled individuals.
He acts as CTO Applied AI for daenet.

Andrew Carlson is a Principal in PwC's Cloud, Engineering, Data & Analytics (CEDA) practice, where he focuses on Data, Engineering and Analytics. With over 25 years of experience spanning GenAI, AI, advanced analytics, and data-driven product development, Andrew brings a rare combination of technical depth and business acumen.

At PwC, Andrew has been at the forefront of transforming how enterprises build software — integrating GenAI and agentic approaches that accelerate end-to-end software development and elevate LLM performance. Previously he served as Director of Product Management for PwC Digital, leading 1,200+ professionals across more than 60 build teams through a GenAI-powered modernization of the software development lifecycle from ideation through DevSecOps.

Earlier in his career Andrew held roles in consulting, finance, and analytics at Arthur Andersen, Diamond Technology Partners, and Credit Suisse, and has delivered impact across the US, Asia, and Europe for startups, turnarounds, and large multinationals alike.

Andrew is equal parts tech enthusiast, educator, and the kind of person who can’t resist pressing buttons just to see what happens (sometimes even twice). A former classroom teacher with nearly a decade of experience crafting learning experiences for techies of all ages, he traded chalkboards for the keyboards of the tech industry in 2020 and hasn’t looked back. Since then, he’s worn many hats—Community Manager, Developer Advocate, and now Developer Educator at Twilio—where he helps developers connect the dots between imagination and implementation. When he’s not building (or breaking :sweat_smile:) things with tech, you’ll find Andrew soaking up the west coast vibes on Vancouver Island, Canada—where he tries (and often fails) to look outdoorsy.

Andrew Norris is Principal Product Manager at Dynatrace, where he leads go-to-market for Bluebox, an agentic operations layer that connects production OpenTelemetry data to the source code behind it. Bluebox investigates anomalies, traces them to a likely root cause, and opens evidence-backed GitHub issues that coding agents can pick up, with a human approving anything that merges.

Before Dynatrace, Andrew co-founded Taplytics in Toronto (Y Combinator, W14) and was CEO of DevCycle, the OpenFeature-native feature management platform it became. Dynatrace acquired DevCycle in January 2026. Fifteen years of building developer tools has taken him from A/B testing to feature flags to the operations side of agent-written software.

His current interest is what happens after the agent ships the code: how teams give agents enough production context to plan before they prompt, and how they verify that a change actually made things better.

Andrew is a Senior Developer Relations Engineer at Box, where he helps developers build secure, AI-powered content workflows on the Box platform. With a background in developer education, he has spent over a decade designing and teaching engineering courses, creating resources that make complex technologies approachable. Andrew is passionate about empowering developers through clear learning pathways, engaging demos, and real-world applications of APIs and AI.

Angie Jones is the VP of Developer Experience at the Agentic AI Foundation where she guides how agentic systems are designed, implemented, and adopted across the global developer ecosystem.

An award-winning educator and international keynote speaker, Angie shares her extensive knowledge with software companies and conference audiences worldwide.

As a Master Inventor, Angie is recognized for her innovative, out-of-the-box thinking, which has led to 27 patented inventions in virtual worlds, collaboration software, social networking, smarter planet initiatives, and software development processes.

Anita Ganti is a 2024 NACD Directorship 100 honoree and serves on the boards of Silvaco Group and Power Integrations, where she chairs the compensation and cybersecurity and data committees. A former Senior Vice President at Wipro, she led 11,000+ engineers delivering $600M+ in services across software, hardware, and cloud platforms. Anita brings deep expertise in AI transformation, finance, digital strategy, and enterprise governance to her board and advisory work. She advises KAVIA AI on operations, strategy, and enterprise growth. Her writing on AI governance has been published in NACD's Directorship Magazine.
speakers.company_position: Board member, Corporate Director & Technology Executive

speakers.bio:
Anjana Umapathy is an Applied AI & ML Tech Lead and Manager in Global Banking at JPMorgan Chase, where she drives GenAI and Agentic AI intiatives. She holds an M.S. in Machine Learning & Natural Language Processing from Carnegie Mellon University and a B.Tech in Computer Science Engineering from PES University, India.
Early in her career, Anjana honed her data science and software engineering skills at Adobe and SAP Concur. At JPMC, she has architected and developed the firm’s first Agentic AI solution - streamlining complex workflows and delivering measurable business impact. A prolific inventor and author, Anjana holds numerous publications and patents, both within and beyond JPMC.
Anjana is passionate about mentorship and fostering diversity in tech and regularly advises in internal women’s networks.
LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/anjanaumapathy/ 
Google Scholar: https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=cKMbToEAAAAJ&hl=en

Ankit Patel is a vice president at NVIDIA, leading developer engagement for the company’s ecosystem of libraries, compilers and developer tools. Ankit joined NVIDIA in 2011 as a GPU Product Manager helping pioneer GPU-accelerated virtual machines, and pushed the boundaries of server GPUs, including NVIDIA's early 8-GPU server appliance. His career transitioned to software, notably leading product management for NVIDIA's OptiX library for ray tracing and AI denoising, a key development that leveraged RT Cores and deepened his connection to deep learning. Prior to NVIDIA, he held product management roles at Matrox Video and Blackmagic Design. Working on systems for over two decades has given him perspective and expertise at the intersection of silicon and software. Ankit holds a Bachelor's in Computer Science from Concordia University, an MBA from Cornell University and currently serves on the PyTorch Governing Board.

Ankita is a Google Developer Expert in Angular, currently adulting in Austin, Texas . Depending on the weather, she can be found outdoors hiking, biking, paddle boarding, trying to pet other peoples' dogs OR staying indoors reading a book. She has an avid interest in all things Design and Angular. She's been a frontend engineer all her adult working life, which is approximately either 10 years or 100 years, because she has lost sense of time since the pandemic.

Ankur Gupta is a senior staff technical program manager in AI infrastructure at LinkedIn in San Jose, California, USA. His research interests include large-scale AI inference platforms, GPU capacity planning, and production reliability engineering. Gupta received his master’s degree in information management from Syracuse University. He is a member of IEEE.

Solutions Engineer focused on cloud-native architecture and developer experience, with a strong passion for developer productivity, testing, and fast feedback in the inner loop. Former Customer Success Engineer for Testcontainers Cloud and Quality Architect. Open-source contributor and conference speaker with a bias toward practical demos, testing, and real-world engineering problems.

Anna Maria Brunnhofer-Pedemonte (AMB) is CEO and Co-Founder of Impact.AI, the platform teams use to move AI Products out of the lab and into production. Business-context-grounded evals, functionality testing, in-code-improvement and runtime enforcement in one loop. Impact AI operates in the real world, from securing the Hera Space Companion by European Space Agency and Red Bull TMS to Fortune 500 enterprise deployments in finance and media. Before that, AMB founded one of the first HCAI labs globally and spent more than a decade in applied AI, knowing the next decade belongs to the AI Product Builders.

Annie Wang is an AI Engineer and Developer Advocate at Google who is passionate about helping developers move from simple chatbots to robust, stateful agentic workflows. Over her 7-year engineering career, she has shipped 60+ open-source agent demonstrations and led extensive developer workshops across the globe. In addition to her technical curriculum, Annie has spent over 500 hours coaching engineers within Google to set meaningful goals and accelerate their career growth. As a speaker and instructor, she excels at breaking down complex topics like memory hierarchy, real-time bidirectional streaming, and GraphRAG into practical, hands-on lessons for developers.

Anuj Gupta has been working on Applied AI, Distributed Systems and Low Latency applications for more than 15 years. He loves solving the most challenging problems. In this his current role, he focuses on Agentic platforms, context engineering, agentic orchestration, agents framework, enterprise agents, A2A, MCP strategy and other company-wide strategic goals.

Anurag Goel is the founder and CEO of Render, the modern cloud platform helping millions of application developers and teams innovate and scale faster. The company has raised over $250M from top investors and was recently valued at $1.5B. He previously founded and exited Crestle, a GPU-powered notebook platform for data scientists. Earlier, he was the eighth employee at Stripe, where he led the Risk organization and played a key role in scaling the company through its hypergrowth phase. Anurag holds a B.Tech in Computer Science from IIT Delhi.

Anurag Malik is a Staff Software Engineer at Intuit, where he leads the data infrastructure powering QuickBooks Capital — a lending platform that has originated over $4 billion in small business loans. He specializes in real-time distributed data systems, ML-driven credit decisioning, and large-scale Apache Spark and Databricks pipelines in production FinTech environments.

His work includes reducing ML scoring latency from 24 hours to under 10 minutes, migrating 400+ legacy pipelines to optimized PySpark, and architecting Intuit's privacy-safe lending data collaboration platform using Databricks Clean Rooms — a first-of-its-kind implementation in financial services that he presented at the Databricks Data + AI Summit 2025.

Anurag writes for HackerNoon, DZone, and Medium's Towards Data Engineering publication, and has served as a peer reviewer for ICML, ICCV, and NeurIPS workshops. He holds an M.S. in Computer Science (Distributed Systems & Big Data Analytics) from Rochester Institute of Technology.

Aparna Dhinakaran is the Co-Founder and Chief Product Officer at Arize AI, a pioneer in AI observability and evaluation trusted by Fortune 100 companies. A frequent speaker at top conferences and a top-read technical voice in AI, her perspectives on AI engineering and agent infrastructure on X receive millions of views every month. Before Arize, she built for and led teams at Uber, Apple, and TubeMogul (acquired by Adobe), including Uber's core ML infrastructure platform, Michelangelo. She holds a B.S. in Electrical Engineering and Computer Science from UC Berkeley, where she published research with the Berkeley AI Research group.

Apoorva Jaiswal is an Applied AI Lead at JPMorgan Chase focused on translating research into production systems by developing graph machine learning (graph ML) and LLM-powered agentic systems that serve Global Banking. She began her career at JPMC India in 2018 as a Software Engineer, building a strong foundation in systems and software design. In 2020, she pivoted to the India-based AI team, architecting cloud infrastructure to deploy ML models at scale before moving into hands-on model development. In 2023, she relocated to the US-based AI team and advanced into her current leadership role, leading cross-functional delivery of graph ML and agentic AI capabilities. Apoorva is a strong advocate of continuous learning. She earned her MS in Computer Science from the University of Massachusetts Amherst while working full-time. She contributes to the broader AI community through mentorship, teaching and talks: she has led workshops at the Grace Hopper Celebration on LangChain-based multimodal workflows (2024) and on LangGraph-based multi-agent workflows (2025), and has spoken at AI meetups in Silicon Valley. She organizes AI Meetups at the Silicon Valley Tech Center, JPMC and is a BobaTalks mentor. She holds patents in AI/ML and brings a global perspective from building and scaling production AI systems across India and the United States. 
Linkedin: https://www.linkedin.com/in/apoorvajaiswal
Google Scholar: https://scholar.google.com/citations?hl=en&user=hLJgexgAAAAJ&view_op=list_works

Aron Eidelman is a Senior Developer Relations Engineer focused on Security Advocacy at Google. Specializing in DevSecOps, AI runtime controls, and applying Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) to cybersecurity, he helps organizations build resilient, proactive defenses. A hands-on practitioner, Aron has demoed cloud and security innovations at major conferences, including RSAC, Next, and Google I/O.

Artem Mukhin is a Software Engineer at Microsoft with 10+ years of experience in frontend development and developer experience. He advocates for bottom-up Developer Experience - the idea that DX improvements should start from developers themselves, not wait for management initiatives.

At Microsoft Skype, Artem's systematic approach to documenting and fixing developer pain points led to the creation of a dedicated DX engineering role - a position that hadn't existed before. Previously at Yandex, he built 15+ internal tools including a media planning system that evolved from an Excel spreadsheet into a production feature of Yandex.Direct, the company's flagship advertising platform.

His research on bottom-up developer experience has been published in The American Journal of Engineering Technology and reached #1 trending in The New Stack's Software Development section. He is the author of "Claude Code for Developer Experience" (Leanpub) and is currently working on a book "Bottom-Up DevEx." Artem founded and grew developer communities totaling 6,000+ members.

He speaks in personal capacity. Views are his own.

Arthur Hicken is an evangelist at Parasoft with over 30 years of experience automating software development practices across the SDLC, application security, and functional safety in industries like automotive, aerospace, and medical. 

He’s a contributing author to Parasoft's blog and writes the popular Code Curmudgeon blog, known for its Hall-of-Shame lists on SQL injection and IoT vulnerabilities. Arthur also hosts a YouTube channel on development and AppSec, speaks frequently at conferences, and serves on safety and security standards committees, including UL 1998, UL 2900, and IEEE P1228. He is a member of IEEE, ASQ, and the Rust Safety-Critical Consortium.

Ashish is a Partner at IronArc Ventures, where he invests in growth-stage companies from Series B onward across Full-Stack AI and Physical AI. IronArc's portfolio includes Anthropic, SpaceX, xAI, CoreWeave, Groq, Anduril, Saronic, Scale AI, Replit, Supabase, Path Robotics, Atoms, and many others. 


With 22+ years of experience as an operator, founder, and investor, Ashish was previously a Partner at Chamaeleon and an investor at Grishin Robotics. Earlier, he led M&A and corporate strategy at Opera Software, held engineering leadership roles at Yahoo!, and founded two startups in India. A Kauffman Fellow (Class 24) and former board member of NextGen Partners, he holds an MBA from Kellogg and London Business School, an MEM from Northwestern University, and a BE in Information Science from RVCE.

Ashish Shubham is a Fellow/VP of Engineering at ThoughtSpot, where he has spent nearly a decade architecting industry-defining AI and analytics products. He is an IEEE Senior Member and author of the book “Architecting AI Data systems”. 

He is the creator of ThoughtSpot Embedded, a leading embedded analytics platform powering multiple Fortune 500 apps worldwide. He also co-architected ThoughtSpot’s AI Analyst, Spotter, and led the company’s first Agentic MCP Server integration, redefining how AI agents securely work with enterprise data. 

Ashish holds multiple patents, has published widely read technical articles, serves on the committee of top AI conferences and frequently speaks at industry forums.

Ashok Prakash is a Staff Engineer at Apple, where he leads engineering initiatives for Responsible AI and safety infrastructure. He specializes in designing high-performance cloud platforms that make complex GPU-accelerated workloads reliable and easy to use. His work focuses on turning difficult infrastructure problems into predictable, self-service systems that allow engineering teams to move faster without breaking things.

Before joining Apple, Ashok spent six years at Oracle Cloud as a Senior Principal Engineer. There, he led the platform engineering efforts to build a Kubernetes-based GPU platform that abstracted bare-metal clusters behind simple APIs. His work allowed product teams to launch AI workloads in minutes instead of days, providing consistent provisioning, quota controls, and clear cost visibility. He has extensive experience building multi-tenant schedulers, automating cluster lifecycles, and creating developer tools that enforce good defaults for security and observability.

Ashok is a regular speaker at engineering and data conferences, including the Airflow Summit, AI Risk Summit and Linux Foundation Workshops, where he shares practical, vendor-neutral patterns for using AI safely. His talks often cover topics like automating documentation, generating unit tests, and establishing human-in-the-loop review processes for AI-generated code.

Ashok holds three published U.S. patent applications and has authored multiple international publications in AI and NLP, which have been cited by both academic researchers and industry practitioners. His core philosophy is simple: pave the path so the right thing is the easy thing to do.

Based in Seattle, Ashok also contributes practical guidance on AI adoption for non-specialists. He is the author of Human Reimagined: Thriving in the Age of AI, a guide for professionals looking to use AI as a helpful assistant rather than a source of anxiety.

Dr. Ashutosh Saxena is a pioneering force in the field of Physical AI & Robotics. As the Founder and Chief AI Officer of TorqueAGI, he is leading the development of AI foundation models that enable enterprise-grade robots to perform complex, real-world tasks in high-stakes industries.
Dr. Saxena holds a Ph.D. in Computer Science from Stanford University, with AI luminary Andrew Ng. He went on to become an accomplished professor at Cornell University, where he led the "Wikipedia for Robots" project (MIT 10 technology breakthroughs).
With over 20,000 citations and more than 100 published papers, his foundational work on 3D computer vision and deep learning has been recognized with numerous awards, including the MIT Technology Review TR35 Innovator Award, a Sloan Fellowship, and the World Technology Award. His entrepreneurial experience includes co-founding Katapult (NSDQ: KPLT), Brain of Things ($8 million ARR), and Caspar AI (Top 100 AI Companies by CB Insights).

Audrey Kim is the founder and curator of the Misalignment Museum. She is fascinated by the ways movement shifting art are often predicated on technology, and the historical evolution of museums. She has previously created collaborative art with the composer Philip Glass and OpenAI. Prior to that, she worked for YCombinator, lead private-public partnership programs for the United Nations, operations for a self-driving car startup (from pre-seed to post-GM acquisition), and business development for Google. She has also created international tech conferences in collaboration with the US Embassy and Austrian Foreign Ministry to  bridge tech communities globally.

Austen Stone is a Senior Field Actions Specialist at GitHub, where he helps enterprise teams modernize CI/CD and adopt GitHub Actions and GitHub-hosted runners at scale. A former solutions engineer and lifelong builder, he specializes in developer automation, cloud architecture, and making complex delivery systems practical. He is passionate about helping developers ship secure software faster and spends an arguably unreasonable amount of time experimenting with GitHub Copilot.

Bala Subrahmanyam Kambala is a Staff Platform Engineer at Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, focused on distributed systems, service platforms, and reliability at cloud scale. His work focuses on Tier-0 distributed systems, API gateway architecture, multi-cloud integration, platform standardization, and reliability for large-scale cloud infrastructure.

His talks focus on vendor-neutral lessons from operating distributed systems, including incident patterns, platform boundaries, user-impact visibility, and the gap between local correctness and system-wide reliability. 

Bala has presented at SREcon Americas 2026 on reliability lessons from a root certificate rotation incident.

Bartosz Leczycki is an Automation Team Lead and Product Owner of Automation at Awaed Alosool Capital, where he leads initiatives focused on building scalable test automation frameworks and advancing QA engineering practices. With hands-on experience in .NET/C#, JavaScript, TypeScript, Java, Scala, and Robot Framework, he bridges technical depth with strategic vision to ensure product reliability and maintainability. His career has been centered on designing automation solutions that improve efficiency, reduce risk, and support continuous delivery pipelines. speakers.bio:
Chris Waterson has spent three decades working toward a single goal: building systems that can reason, plan, and act on their own. He started chasing that vision in the ‘90s, long before the tools to realize it existed. Since then, he's helped build many of those tools himself, contributing to foundational embedding research and deep learning ranking models at Google, and later leading the team behind DevMate, Meta's internal agentic coding framework.

That work convinced him that building agents is no longer the hard part – managing them reliably in production is. It's why he co-founded Guild.ai, the control plane for AI agents, giving engineering teams the access controls, observability, versioning, and sharing infrastructure needed to run agents at scale with confidence.

Former Yahoo, Mozilla, Microsoft. JavaScript and Accessibility expert. Worked on Chromium Developer Tools. Author of the Developer Advocacy Handbook, LinkedIn Learning and Skillshare Trainer. Cinephile.

Christopher is a longtime geek and developer at heart. He's spent the better part of the last couple of decades enabling and upskilling developers on a variety of languages and platforms. At present he's at GitHub focusing on aiding organizations in improving their DevOps processes. When not in front of a monitor he can be found running many miles or spending time with his partner and their adopted fur-baby.
Colleen Lake

Dan Fu is VP of Kernels at Together AI and an incoming Assistant Professor of Computer Science and Engineering at UCSD. His research develops efficient algorithms for machine learning, with a focus on solutions that are both theoretically efficient and practically fast on modern hardware. His work has been recognized with multiple awards at major ML conferences, including Best Student Paper Runner-Up (UAI) and multiple oral and spotlight presentations (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR), as well as multiple graduate fellowships (Department of Defense NDSEG, Brown Institute). His research has also been deployed in production at major technology companies (FlashAttention). Dan conducted his PhD training at Stanford and his undergraduate and master’s studies at Harvard, all in computer science.

Dan Ndombe is on Docker's developer relations team, where he runs hands-on workshops on running coding agents safely inside Docker Sandboxes. He has led sandbox sessions for developer audiences at AI Engineer World's Fair, AgentCon Silicon Valley, and AI Camp.

Daniel Dafoe is co-founder and CEO of Supermodel Labs. He previously led accessibility engineering at Apple and launched the iPhone Air, MacBook Neo, and Apple Vision Pro. His background is in computer systems.

Daniel Fau has been involved with TYPO3 since 2006 as the CEO of his own agency. Daniel is well-known for his exceptional coffee-making skills and his active engagement with the community in shaping the future of the TYPO3 Project, all while enjoying a cup together.

Daniel's expertise also encompasses multi-cloud architecture, where he designs and implements solutions across various cloud platforms to address complex business challenges. Daniel Oh is a Java Champion and Senior Principal Developer Advocate at IBM, where he leads efforts to advance cloud native innovation through open source technologies. Renowned for his ability to bridge technical and collaborative gaps, he empowers developers and organizations to build transformative solutions from AI-driven applications and serverless architectures to resilient microservices. As a CNCF Ambassador and TAG DevEx co-chair, Daniel actively shapes the cloud native ecosystem, fostering partnerships between enterprise developers, AI engineers, and platform engineering teams to accelerate hybrid cloud adoption. His technical leadership extends beyond code contributions, as he mentors communities and champions strategies that enable businesses to thrive in evolving digital landscapes. A dynamic storyteller and educator, Daniel captivates global audiences through keynote speeches, workshops, and interactive sessions, where he demystifies emerging technologies and inspires the tech community to embrace the future of open source innovation.

A seasoned Full Cycle Web Development Expert and R&D Manager, brings over two decades of experience, skillfully leading both local and international development teams from concept to delivery. As a recognized public speaker and blog writer, he also makes notable contributions to the open-source community.

In addition, Daniel leads the "NG-Heroes" meetup, creating networking and knowledge-sharing opportunities within the tech industry. Beyond his professional endeavors, he values family time above all else, proudly owning the title of "The Best Developer in the World," humorously awarded by his wife. Combining technical leadership, community involvement, and a strong family focus.

Daniela Dimitrova is Vice President of IT and CIO for North America at Mercedes-Benz, where she leads technology strategy, digital transformation, and AI-driven innovation. With global leadership experience across Mercedes-Benz, BMW Group, and Toyota, she has driven IT, sales, and marketing initiatives across Europe, the Middle East, and North America. Daniela holds an Executive MBA and certifications in neuroscience and professional coaching, combining technology leadership with a passion for empowering people and accelerating business transformation.

I am a computer person who writes Rust, breaks things on AWS, and collects computers older than most of my audience. By title I'm a Distinguished Developer Advocate, by practice I'm live-coding on Twitch or convincing a 1974 minicomputer to do something useful. I build CLI tools nobody asked for but everyone ends up using, blog about Rust and cloud development right here, and firmly believe the terminal is the best UI ever made. I'm happiest when a demo works on the first try, which almost never happens.
I also care deeply about developer productivity and coding assistants. I spend an unreasonable amount of time teaching AI agents to be better coding companions, building MCP servers, and automating everything that stands still long enough. If there's a way to make developers faster and happier, I'm probably already tinkering with it.

David Hefter leads BlackRock's AI transformation for the Global Fixed Income investment team. After studying AI at Columbia he has spent his career of over two decades at BlackRock. For the past few years, David has been advancing firmwide AI adoption through engagement, training, and community building, including publishing a weekly internal AI newsletter.

Highly regarded engineering leader, specializing in IT modernization with a proven track record in driving strategic IT governance and architectural transformation for federal agencies. Expert in developing and implementing enterprise reference architectures, enhancing data protection, and accelerating AI integration to optimize operational efficiency.  Known for fostering innovation through strategic use of Amazon, Microsoft, and Azure platforms.

He holds an undergraduate degree in French Literature from Princeton and an MBA from Stanford, both of which ended up way more useful for Acquired than he ever anticipated. (Something about only connecting the dots looking backward…) He lives in San Francisco with his wife, two young daughters and goldendoodle/research assistant.

David is a Senior AI/ML Engineer within the Office of the CTO at NetApp, where he’s dedicated to empowering developers to build, scale, and deploy AI/ML solutions in production environments. He brings deep expertise in building and training models for applications such as NLP, vision, real-time analytics, and even classifying debilitating diseases. His mission is to help users build, train, and deploy AI models efficiently, making advanced machine learning accessible to users of all levels.

Before NetApp, he was heavily involved in the AI/ML community, specifically in conversational AI solutions and driving AI platform growth in a DevRel and pre-sales role. David frequently shares his insights at industry conferences and events, offering hands-on guidance for implementing AI/ML in cloud environments. David's prior experience includes contributing to the Kubernetes and CNCF ecosystems, working hands-on with VMware virtualization, implementing backup/recovery solutions, and developing hardware storage adapter firmware and drivers.

Debashis Saha is the Senior Vice President, Technology in Travel Foundations at Expedia Group, where he leads the engineering teams powering communications, loyalty, identity, payments, orders and reservations across the company's global portfolio of brands. His work spans scalable, high-volume platform capabilities that underpin experiences for travelers and travel partners worldwide.
An innovative engineering leader with a career spanning Oracle, eBay, PayPal, Intuit, and AppZen, Debashis brings deep expertise in distributed systems, AI-first product architecture, and large-scale platform transformation. 
Debashis holds an MS in Electrical Engineering and Computer Science from MIT and a B.Tech in Computer Science from IIT Kharagpur. Beyond his operating roles, he is an active participant in the startup ecosystem, advising and investing in early-stage companies and supporting founders as they build and scale.

Denise Kwan is a senior developer advocate at Google. With over 15 years of software engineering experience and a decade in developer relations, she brings a deep understanding of the software development lifecycle and what constitutes an outstanding developer experience. Her technical background spans frontend, backend, REST API development, and performance testing, complemented by extensive experience in developer support. She leverages this technical knowledge and her expertise in developer experience to champion and build developer tools that engineers genuinely appreciate.

Desmond is a full stack engineering leader and Certified Ethical Hacker with 13 years of experience in tech. He has built a career defined by impactful contributions and global recognition, speaking at prestigious conferences like Afrotech in Austin, GOTO in Chicago, Apidays in Paris, and MWISE in DC. Desmond is an engineer at heart with a leader's vision. He is energized by the potential to motivate teams and empower engineers towards a large vision!

Devanshi is the co-founder and CTO of Headroom Labs, where she’s building tools to make AI coding agents more efficient and affordable. AI agents spend an increasing share of their context budget rereading verbose tool outputs, logs, files, and conversation history. Headroom, a popular Github repository(72K+ GitHub stars), compresses context locally while preserving the information agents need to solve problems.
A second-time founder, Devanshi has spent her career building the infrastructure behind large-scale AI systems. At Netflix, she helped build the embedding feature store powering ML training and inference across the company. At Amazon Music, she developed recommendation and search models serving a catalog of more than 100 million tracks, including Alexa use cases. She previously co-founded an ML observability startup focused on model drift, data quality, and fairness, and began her career building cloud infrastructure at AWS EC2.

Dex is CEO and co-founder at HumanLayer, building an agentic IDE and collaboration platform that helps teams solve hard problems in complex codebases without devolving into slop. Dex coined the term context engineering in April 2025, has keynoted AI Engineer conferences and his practical, no-hype talks on agentic coding have over 1 million views on YouTube. Dex built lunar exploration tooling for NASA researchers in high school, and spent 10+ years in the Kubernetes/Infra space before getting into AI.

Diptamay Sanyal is a principal-level engineer and data and AI platform architect with more than 20 years of experience building large-scale, real-time distributed systems across cybersecurity, public safety, and enterprise SaaS. He has designed multi-petabyte, AI-native platforms that process trillions of telemetry events daily, including production systems at CrowdStrike, HubSpot, and Dataminr. He focuses on AI-native security architectures, streaming systems, and policy-constrained automation. He is a Senior Member of the IEEE and a member of the Forbes Technology Council.

speakers.bio: Dr. Ramin Hasani is the co-founder and CEO of Liquid AI.  Previously, he was jointly appointed as a Principal Machine Learning Scientist at the Vanguard Group and a Research Affiliate at MIT CSAIL.  Ramin’s research focuses on robust deep learning and decision-making in complex dynamical systems.  Prior to that, he was a Postdoctoral Associate at CSAIL MIT, leading research on modeling intelligence and sequential decision-making.  He received his Ph.D. degree with distinction in Computer Science from the Vienna University of Technology, Austria.  His Ph.D. dissertation and continued research on Liquid Neural Networks have been recognized internationally with numerous nominations and awards.

Yvonne has served as an active Board Member for multiple startups, guiding their strategic direction and growth. With extensive international experience across North America, Europe and Asia, she brings a global perspective to her work. Yvonne received a diploma in Experimental Physics from University of Siegen, Germany, and holds a PhD in Applied Physics from University of Tuebingen, Germany. Recognized by Global Corporate Venturing in 2022 as one of the top 50 Rising Stars in global CVC funds, 49 Women to Watch in Venture on the US West Coast in 2023, and top 50 Emerging Leaders in global CVC in 2024.

Co-founder and CTO at PingCAP (the company behind TiDB), an entrepreneur with a hacker's mind & heart. Full-stack engineer, for real. Pioneer in building cloud-native systems. Building distributed systems and databases with ♥️. Building a company like a distributed system.

Edward Aryee is a San Francisco-based software engineer, AI researcher, and startup founder who serves as the Co-Founder and Chief Technology Officer (CTO) of Laminar (formerly SRE.ai). Backed by Y Combinator (F24), Laminar is a Salesforce delivery company that builds AI agents to analyze, build, and govern enterprise systems—streamlining deployments, releases, and testing for orgs ranging from SMBs to the Fortune 10.

Before launching Laminar in 2024, Edward worked as an engineer and AI researcher at Google Research, developing automation tools and helping build some of the world's most widely used AI software, including Translate and Gemini. His experience navigating Google's internal infrastructure revealed a stark gap in mainstream enterprise tooling, inspiring him to co-found Laminar and bring context-aware delivery to business software.

Additionally, Edward is an active operator angel in the early-stage startup ecosystem, investing in and advising early-stage founders as a member of the BAG Collective, a network of tech operators and investors funding seed and Series A technology startups.

Eftal Yurtseven is Co-Founder and CEO of each::labs, where he's building the production layer for AI-generated media - one API across 600+ image, video, and audio models with routing and failover built in.

Before founding each::labs, he spent his career on the infrastructure side of scale: platform engineering at Getir, running Kubernetes autoscaling across multiple clusters, and backend systems at Insider handling thousands of requests per minute. That work shaped the thesis behind each::labs that the gap between what people imagine and what AI actually ships is an infrastructure problem, not a model problem.

Based in San Francisco.

CEO of Intuition Machines, operators of hCaptcha. hCaptcha protects millions of sites and apps from fraud and abuse like account takeovers and payment fraud. Used to stop both entirely human and entirely automated attacks, hCaptcha takes a uniquely privacy-preserving approach to online security.

Elizabeth Fuentes is a Developer Advocate and AI engineer specializing in agent harness architecture. Her work spans context engineering, agent memory, security guardrails, and taking agents to production. Through hands-on demos she breaks complex concepts into simple, understandable pieces of code, helping developers build more efficient agents and democratizing the adoption of advanced AI for everyone

Emmanuel Acheampong is a Senior Manager Developer Relations at Crusoe AI, where he is a founding member of the Developer Relations team for Managed AI, bridging the gap between managed inference infrastructure and the open-source developer ecosystem. 

He focuses on enabling engineers to leverage Crusoe's high-performance GPU infrastructure to build and deploy the next generation of AI agents and frontier models.

Before Crusoe, Emmanuel was Co-Founder and Head of AI at yShade.ai (Google for Startups Black Founders Accelerator '24), where he led development of proprietary computer vision algorithms trained on a 12M+ image dataset, shipping production AI systems across e-commerce, beauty, and vision-critical applications.

Emmanuel is passionate about open-source AI, agentic systems, machine learning, and the future of cloud infrastructure for AI workloads

Emre Okcular is a Senior Solutions Architect at OpenAI, where he partners with enterprises to design and deploy advanced agentic AI systems. His work focuses on Context Engineering and LLMOps practices that enable long-running, adaptive AI workflows in production environments. Emre previously worked at Google as a Solutions Architect, supporting global organizations on large-scale cloud and ML initiatives. He is passionate about bridging research breakthroughs with real-world business applications, and regularly collaborates with product, engineering, and customer teams to push the boundaries of enterprise AI adoption.

Eric Bahn is a Co-Founder and General Partner at Hustle Fund, an early-stage venture capital firm ($200M+ under management) based in San Francisco. Hustle Fund invests in software startups at the pre-seed and seed stages, backing founders who exhibit great execution and high velocity (we call it ‘hustle’).

Previous to Hustle Fund, Eric was an angel investor and venture partner at 500 Startups. And prior to becoming a professional investor, he spent over a decade as an operator and entrepreneur (3 exits). Eric draws from his product and growth experience to advise his founders in scaling their own enterprises.

Eric is a native of Detroit, Michigan and first arrived in Silicon Valley to attend Stanford University (BA, MA), which launched his career into software and startups. Eric is happily married with two kids.

Eric Deandrea is a Java Champion & Senior Principal Software Engineer at IBM on the Quarkus engineering team. Eric has over 26 years of experience designing and building Java-based solutions and developer training programs. He is a contributor to various OSS projects, including Quarkus, Spring, LangChain4j, Docling, WireMock, and Microcks, as well as a speaker at many public events and user groups around the world. Eric recently put his Quarkus and Spring knowledge to use by publishing his first book, “Quarkus for Spring Developers (https://red.ht/quarkus-spring-devs).” Outside of work, Eric enjoys boating on the lakes of New Hampshire, ice hockey, and martial arts, in which he holds a black belt in Kempo Karate.

Eric Wang is a Senior Staff Engineer on Uber’s Michelangelo ML Platform team. He leads Opensource project and his work focuses on building Kubernetes-native infrastructure that helps teams move ML and data workflows from experimentation to production reliably.

Erran Berger is Chief Technology Officer, Engineering at LinkedIn and a member of the company’s Executive Team. He leads LinkedIn’s technology vision and strategy and oversees the global engineering organization behind the world’s largest professional network, serving more than 1.3 billion members.
His team is responsible for building LinkedIn’s products and experiences for members and customers, along with the platforms and technology that power them at global scale. This includes advancing LinkedIn’s applied AI and machine learning capabilities across recommender systems and agentic experiences to make those products more intelligent, personalized, and trusted. His organization is also helping transform LinkedIn into an AI-native company by driving the adoption of AI across the business and enabling teams to work more effectively and productively.
Throughout his 17+ years at LinkedIn, Erran has helped shape the company’s technology strategy, scale its engineering organization and platforms, and drive multiple generations of product innovation.
Erran serves on the boards of JVS Bay Area and Year Up. He holds a Bachelor of Science in Computer Engineering from the University of California, San Diego.

Principal software engineer @ Entire, previously founded Neosync, an open source data security company (YC S22, acquired by Grow Therapy). Rust and Go enthusiast. Past lives at IBM, Oracle and other startups.

Eystein Stenberg is the CTO of NorthernTech, a leader in device lifecycle management, and the creator of Mender, the market-leading solution for robust, secure, and customizable over-the-air (OTA) software updates. With over 15 years of experience in security and systems management, Stenberg has served on the frontlines of some of the largest production environments and possesses in-depth knowledge on solving real-world system security challenges. An expert in embedded system security and IoT device management, Stenberg routinely shares his insights at industry technology conferences and other sector-focused events like automotive.

Fabiano Amorim is a Microsoft Data Platform most valuable professional (MVP) since 2011. With over two decades of experience, Fabiano is well known in the database community for his performance tuning abilities and the many conference speaking engagements around the world.
He writes articles for Simple-Talk (https://www.simple-talk.com/author/fabiano-amorim/) and his blog is on http://blogfabiano.com.

Farshad Abasi is the Founder and CEO of Forward Security and Eureka DevSecOps, bringing over 27 years of industry experience to the forefront of cybersecurity innovation. His professional journey includes key technical roles at Intel and Motorola, evolving into senior security positions as the Principal Security Architect for HSBC Global, and Head of IT Security for the Canadian division. Farshad's commitment to the field extends to his role as an instructor at BCIT, where he imparts his wealth of knowledge to the next generation of cybersecurity experts. His diverse experience, which spans startups to large enterprises, informs his approach to delivering adaptive and reliable solutions.

Engaged actively in the cybersecurity community through roles in BSides Vancouver/MARS, OWASP Vancouver/AppSec PNW, and as a CISSP designate, Farshad's vision and leadership continue to drive the industry forward. Under his guidance, Forward Security is setting new standards in application and cloud security.

Fatih Kadir Akın is a software developer and public speaker from Istanbul, currently working as DevRel at WordPress, Automattic. He is an award-winning GitHub Star recognized for his impact on open source and developer communities worldwide.

Author of books on JavaScript and prompt engineering for AI tools, Fatih is passionate about the intersection of web technologies and AI-assisted development. He actively contributes to open-source projects, builds experimental tools on GitHub, and shares insights at conferences around the world.

A strong advocate for open-source collaboration, Fatih specializes in JavaScript and Ruby (particularly Ruby on Rails). Beyond coding, he enjoys organizing tech events, mentoring developers, and exploring new ways AI can empower software engineers.

He is also the creator of prompts.chat, a platform for discovering and optimizing AI prompts for large language models.

Born in Stuttgart in 1987. Studied economics and journalism in Cologne and Auckland, New Zealand. Previous positions include „Südwest Presse“, „Süddeutsche Zeitung“ and „Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung“. Business editor and advisor to the radio director at the West German Broadcasting Corporation (WDR). With Handelsblatt since 2017. Banking and fintech reporter in Frankfurt, correspondent and US bureau chief in New York and San Francisco covering tech and automotive since 2022. State Street Institutional Press Award, German Journalism Prize, Ernst Schneider Prize, Private Media Prize, Georg von Holtzbrinck Prize, DDV Prize for Business Journalism. Author of „Geniale Betrüger – Wie Wirecard Politik und Finanzsystem bloßstellt“ (nominated for the German Business Book Award).

Filippos Tourlomousis is the founder of Biological Lattice Industries (BLI), a company building a new way to advance the bioeconomy through collaborative cyber-physical AI agents for innovators who design and make advanced formulations and devices serving human health and the environment.

His work bridges entrepreneurship, autonomous laboratories, biofabrication, materials engineering, and open-source scientific instrumentation. He also leads the Autonomous Science Lab at NCSR Demokritos in Athens and previously conducted postdoctoral research at MIT's Center for Bits and Atoms. His mission is to make AI-powered experimental platforms and self-driving labs more accessible, scalable, and impactful for materials discovery and bioengineering.

Floriane is a Product & Tech executive with 20+ years building $B+ revenue products across FinTech, eCommerce, and AI-driven platforms for eBay, PayPal, Twitter, Zalando and more. She has a proven track record of scaling global teams (100+), launching market-defining products, and driving measurable outcomes through AI/ML, GTM strategy, and operational excellence and is a multicultural leader with deep expertise operating across the US, Europe and APAC.
