speakers.bio:
Hi, I'm Francesco, based in Rome, Italy. I'm a Computer Scientist, and from 2017 to 2020, I contributed to the European Space Agency's Copernicus project.

I'm an active presence in online developer communities, especially on Twitter, YouTube, and Discord. Recognized as a Docker Captain, I've hosted official Docker events and appeared on their YouTube channel. Professionally, I focus on roles within developer relations, centered around content strategy and community engagement.

Currently, my main creative efforts are directed towards my YouTube channel, where I've interviewed over 250 developers. My content primarily covers Rust, Blockchain technologies, DevOps practices, and Web Development. I also enjoy engaging with the community through live streams

Frederic was the founder and CEO of Polar Signals (acquired by Dash0). Before founding Polar Signals, he was a senior principal engineer and the main architect for all things Observability at Red Hat, which he joined through the CoreOS acquisition. Frederic is a Prometheus and Thanos maintainer as well as until recently was the tech lead for the special interest group for instrumentation in Kubernetes. In a previous life, he was a security researcher working on key management solutions as well as intrusion detection systems. When not working on software Frederic enjoys obsessing over brewing a perfect cup of coffee.

Garvit Kataria is a technical leader specializing in large-scale, high-traffic distributed systems. At Intuit, he leads the development of Kubernetes-based infrastructure and shared platforms that operate across hundreds of clusters.

His key contributions include building infrastructure resiliency and disaster recovery systems that safeguard thousands of services, continuously evaluating the health of more than 300,000 assets. He has also driven initiatives to improve system reliability, scalability, and operational efficiency in complex, production-grade environments.

Currently, Garvit spearheads the delivery of statically stable, fault-tolerant disaster recovery solutions, ensuring high availability and performance for Intuit’s critical business applications.

Gene Kim has been studying high-performing technology organizations since 1999. He was the founder and CTO of Tripwire, Inc., an enterprise security software company, where he served for 13 years. His books have sold over 1 million copies—he is the WSJ bestselling author of The Unicorn Project, and coauthor of Wiring the Winning Organization, The Phoenix Project, The DevOps Handbook, and the Shingo Publication Award-winning Accelerate. His latest book, Vibe Coding, was released in October 2025.

In 2025, he won the Philip Crosby Medal from the American Society for Quality (ASQ) for his work in the 2023 book Wiring the Winning Organization. Since 2014, he has been the organizer of DevOps Enterprise Summit (now Enterprise AI Summit), studying the technology transformations of large, complex organizations.

Gerardo Pardo, CTO at RTI since 1998, led the development of RTI Connext DDS. Gerardo leads standardization efforts, authoring numerous DDS-related standards and chairing revision task forces. He co-founded and co-chairs the Data-Distribution SIG within OMG and serves on the OMG board of directors. With expertise in security, middleware, and publish-subscribe systems, he has led multiple research grants, holds patents, and has published extensively on real-time and secure distributed systems

Gerhard Eschelbeck, former Google Vice President Security & Privacy Engineering (CISO) is a well-regarded information technology executive with strong operational and strategic experience. He has launched innovative and successful companies and has built high-performance multi-national teams in the U.S. , Europe and Asia. Gerhard has a passion for championing new technologies and is a trusted advisor and board member to several early stage startup companies. He published the “Laws of Vulnerabilities” and is one of the inventors of the Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS), and holds numerous patents in the field of managed network security. Prior to joining Google, Gerhard was CTO and Senior Vice President at Sophos and Qualys, and served in senior product and technology roles at companies including Network Associates and McAfee. Gerhard has a Ph.D in computer science from University Linz, Austria.

Gil Feig is the Co-Founder and CTO of Merge, the leading provider of agentic tools and customer-facing integrations for frontier LLMs, Fortune 500 organizations, and B2B SaaS companies. Previously, Gil was the Head of Engineering at Untapped and worked as a software engineer at Wealthfront and LinkedIn. A graduate of Columbia University, he now lives and works in San Francisco.

Over 20 years in M&A, corporate development, and capital markets advisory across the US and Europe. Giovanni helps technology and tech-enabled companies navigate sell-side and buy-side transactions, capital raises, growth equity, strategic partnerships, and cross-border expansion.

Graham Gilbert has released numerous open source tools over the years, is a board member of the Mac Admins Open Source non-profit, and is the co-founder of the Mac Admins Mentorship Program.

His work sits at the intersection of large-scale systems, senior engineering practice, and how organizations make and sustain good technical decisions over time.

In his day job, Graham is a Senior Staff Engineer at Airbnb, working across corporate infrastructure with a focus on device trust, identity, and client platforms.

Greg Larkin a Senior Service Delivery Engineer at GitHub and works with many of the largest financial firms that have adopted the GitHub platform. He is an experienced IT professional with a broad knowledge of software development, automation, version control systems, system administration, and many other disciplines. He is also an experienced mentor and technical trainer with an ability to meet his students where they are, break down complex topics and leave them with skills applicable to their job responsibilities. He takes great pride in getting his students to their own personal “a-ha!” moments. In his free time, he is an outdoor endurance sports enthusiast, and you’ll find him exploring the trails near his Northern California home.

Guillaume is a tech founder turned VC, who built and scaled companies for over 20 years in Paris, San Francisco, and New York, including four exits - such as Musiwave to Microsoft and Linkfluence to Meltwater. He spent the past several years leading Serena Data Ventures, an early-stage specialized seed fund focused on foundational technologies. He's now working on his own project in that space, building on the experience he gained backing companies such as Emmi AI (foundational AI for physics-informed simulation, acquired by Mistral AI), Waiv (foundational AI for cancer-treatment triaging), Naftiko (AI/data API infrastructure), Kleio (agentic commerce infrastructure), Edgee (AI gateway for agentic coding), and others.

Guillaume Lebedel is CTO and co-founder of StackOne, the integration infrastructure platform for AI agents backed by GV. StackOne connects agents to 200+ connectors with 11,000+ enterprise-ready actions, all exposed via MCP and other Agent compatible protocols. Before StackOne, Guillaume built large-scale event & data infrastructure powering ML-driven trading systems and B2B SaaS. He writes about the practical challenges of scaling tool use in agentic systems at stackone.com/blog.

Gustavo is an AI Engineer and Developer Advocate from Venezuela, specialized in building practical solutions and tackling real-world scenarios. He has carried research in the field of Natural Language Processing and has worked in Mixed Reality in the past, and currently focuses on all things Agents.

Hi, I'm GPS, whether I’m replying online, sharing feedback with teams, speaking at conferences, leading workshops, building demos, or making memes, I do whatever is needed to help improve the developer experience across GitHub services. In my free time, I build the most popular cloud engineering courseware at learntocloud.guide.

Han Wang is co-founder and CEO of Mintlify, the knowledge infrastructure layer that makes technical knowledge accessible to humans and AI agents. He started Mintlify with Hahnbee Lee in 2022, their senior year at Cornell. Mintlify now powers documentation for more than 20,000 companies including Anthropic, Microsoft, Coinbase, PayPal, and Amazon.

Hannes Steiner is the Founder & CEO of Story.one, an AI startup building a new layer for structured knowledge. His platform transforms complex content, from talks to research notes, into professional books within hours, ready to be published worldwide instantly. The Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung describes this approach as one that is ‘revolutionizing the way nonfiction books are written.

I'm Harald Kirschner, a Principal Product Manager at Microsoft working on Visual Studio Code and GitHub Copilot, supporting over 40 million active developers code faster and more efficiently across virtually any programming language. Before Microsoft, I led Developer Experience at Mozilla, where I led Firefox DevTools and helped deliver Firefox Quantum, which doubled browser performance. My background in software engineering, including early work on MooTools, gives me hands-on insight into the challenges developers face daily. When I'm not working, I enjoy hiking California's coastal trails and experimenting with generative art.

Hari Lingamagunta is the Head of Engineering for Developer Infrastructure at Atlassian, where he’s currently leading the company’s AI-first engineering transformation. Hari leads a global team building the platform, developer loop, and tooling behind Jira, Confluence, and Trello. With 18+ years across Amazon, Concur, and SAP, Hari is known for building high-performance teams and obsessing over reliability, scalability, and performance at scale.

With over 15 years of experience in quality engineering and automation framework design across diverse domains including finance, healthcare and retail. Expertise in leading high-performing testing teams and managing end-to-end testing processes, from defining test strategies to implementing automated solutions. Skilled in latest automation and RPA tools like UiPath, Selenium and IntelliJ (with Gemini AI Code Assist), adept in programming languages including Java, JavaScript and VBScript. Possesses hands-on experience with Generative AI technologies, leveraging LLMs (like Open AI’s GPT models, Google Gemini model, Anthropic Claude) to optimize test cases generation, automate test data creation, and enhance defect triage processes. Has successfully led the initiative and integration of GenAI tools to enable faster automation of regression and smoke tests, thereby reducing testing time and enhancing product quality. Also used Model Context Protocol(MCP) to integrate existing automation framework with AI-driven agents.

Hiroto Udagawa leads ML Research and ML Infrastructure in AI Core at Nu, the team behind nuFormer, Nu's foundation model for customer financial behavior.

He has worked on recommendation, pricing, and user understanding systems for his entire career. At LinkedIn he built ads personalization and ranking models, where the core problem was inferring intent from sequences of behavior. He then joined Hyperplane as a founding-team machine learning engineer, applying that same thinking to bank transaction data. Nu acquired Hyperplane in 2024, and that team became the core of Nu's AI research effort. His teams now pretrain billion-parameter sequence models on trillions of transactions and run them in production for credit, pricing, and personalization decisions serving more than 140 million customers across Brazil, Mexico, and Colombia.

With 11 years in the software trenches and a recently completed Master’s in Data Analytics, I live at the heart of the AI revolution. Their expertise spans Deep Learning and Neural Networks, fueled by a passion for building intelligent systems that actually work. When not training models, you can find me perfecting their backhand on the table tennis court or navigating the backroads of America. Having driven a Tesla through almost every state in the Union, they are as comfortable navigating cross-country charging networks as they are navigating complex datasets

Ian is an accomplished and disruptive thought leader with over 30 years of experience leading and driving strategic organizational change and digital transformation within complex and dynamic global organizations, with a more recent focus specifically on AI adoption at scale. 

He is a skilled storyteller and change agent having successfully guided and reinvented organizations through challenging change and growth initiatives, including business process optimization, cultural transformations, and large-scale systems implementations.

Ian is a passionate rugby fanatic, and active coach and referee for this wonderful sport.

Ian Smith spent the late 20th century at Georgia Tech in Atlanta GA  USA getting a Ph.D. in computer science; he's recovering nicely.   Later, he worked at prestigious research labs like Xerox PARC and Intel Research.  Recently, he has been working at numerous startups and is currently the CTO and co-founder of LYOS (lyos.com)..  He has published more than 30 peer-reviewed scientific publications with thousands of citations, and holds more than 10 US patents.  He started using go before there was the error interface.

Ignacio Riesgo is Senior Director, Developer Advocacy, for IBM & Red Hat Runtimes. In his role, he leads all Developer Outreach Programs, Content and Advocacy initiatives for the IBM and Red Hat Java portfolio, adopted by tens of thousands of enterprise customers, and millions of developers.

Isaac Evans is co-founder and CEO of Semgrep, a company dedicated to improving software security and reliability. Previously, he served as a researcher at the US Defense Department under a SFS program and at MIT Lincoln Laboratory, conducting research into binary exploitation bypasses for techniques like control-flow integrity and novel hardware defenses on new architectures like RISC-V. Isaac received his BS/MS degrees in EECS from MIT. Other interests include next-generation programming languages, secure-by-design frameworks, software-defined radio, and the intersection of cryptography and public policy.

Isaac Levin is a Developer Advocate at JetBrains and a Microsoft MVP. He has over 15 years of experience working as a developer for the web, mostly in the Microsoft Ecosystem. Outside of work, he hosts a podcast called Coffee and Open Source where he interviews folks from across the tech industry as well as builds open-source projects like PresenceLight and GitHub Stat Tracker. He lives outside of Seattle Washington and likes to wind down from work with his wife Ariana and his 2 children Isaac and Avery.

Ishan Shah is a Software Engineer with 10+ years of experience designing and delivering large-scale, event-driven, and cloud-native systems across PayPal, Nordstrom, and Securonix. He has built real-time data platforms, CDC pipelines, inventory and decisioning systems, and high-throughput search and analytics infrastructure.

His work increasingly sits at the intersection of AI and engineering operations, including AI-assisted development workflows, context engineering, agent guardrails, and AI-native reliability patterns. Ishan is especially interested in practical approaches to autonomous software development, AI SRE, incident-response agents, and “AI gardening” — managing context, memory, and entropy in long-running agentic systems.

He mentors teams on reliability, observability, schema governance, and scalable platform design, with deep expertise in Java, Kafka, Debezium, AWS, Redis, Postgres, DynamoDB, and distributed systems.

Itamar Friedman is CEO and Co-founder of Qodo, the AI Code Quality and Governance Platform that helps enterprises maintain code quality, enforce standards, and govern code at AI velocity. He brings over 20 years of experience in machine learning, including participating in and leading world-class teams in training and fine-tuning foundational models, as well as winning multiple ML and programming competitions. Before Qodo, he held technical leadership roles at startups and at Alibaba, where he led machine vision research.

Ivan Sekyonda is a Developer Relations Engineer specializing in bridging knowledge gaps between technology, developers, and the communities they serve. Drawing on experience across industry, academia, and open source, he helps make complex technical concepts accessible and actionable. Ivan has taught at multiple universities and is passionate about fostering collaboration, learning, and innovation through technology.

Jack Danger is the VP of Platform at LaunchDarkly, making production safer for everyone. He loves building things, and he hopes to eventually get over how useless many of his old coding skills now are. He's founded four companies, sold two, and was an early engineering lead at Square.

Publication: One of the Greatest Inventors Alive along with Elon Muck by www.grunge.com · Mar 30, 2022
Jack McCauley is an engineer, hardware designer, inventor, video game developer, and philanthropist.
Jack is best known for designing the guitars and drums for the Guitar Hero video game series, and as a co-founder and chief engineer at Oculus VR. Jack holds numerous U.S. patents for inventions in software, audio effects, virtual reality, motion
control, computer peripherals, and video game hardware and controllers
Jack has worked with companies like Oculus, Atari, RedOctane, Electronic Arts, Activision, and Microsoft. He is a member of the MEMS Industry Group and an expert in the video game peripheral engineering space.
Jack co-founded Oculus VR with Palmer Luckey, Brendan Iribe, Nate Mitchell, Michael Antonov and Andrew Scott Reisse. Jack produced the DK1, DK2 and DKHD products for Oculus and managed the engineering design and production until the company was acquired by Facebook for $2 billion.
Previously, Jack was the key developer on Activision's GuitarHero franchise. Jack designed the guitars and drums for GuitarHero , including the XBOX, PS2, PS3 and Nintendo Wii. Jack has numerous awards and patents in the video game space, including a RED-DOT award for product design for bone-conducting headphones.
In 1987, Jack invented the scrolling wheel mouse. Jack is also one of the originators of the USB specification. He served on the HID USB device working group whilst developing the USB. He also has publications for artificial intelligence algorithms and is a researcher in this field.

James has spent his career working closely with engineering, design, and cross-functional teams to build products customers love. Most recently, he led product at FluidCloud, and before that spent over five years at HashiCorp. His background also includes time at Pivotal Software.

James Clancey is a Principal Product Manager at GitHub, where he works on the GitHub Copilot app and helps shape AI-powered software development. A self-taught technologist with more than 18 years of experience, his career spans developer tooling, mobile, VR, and developer relations. At Microsoft, he architected the company’s Mobile SDK and pioneered work on C# Hot Reload, Hot Restart, Comet, and .NET MAUI; at Meta, he worked as a VR software engineer. He has also helped more than 30 companies ship apps across platforms and built native and remote development workflows for the Godot Engine. Today, he focuses on making AI coding agents practical, powerful, and approachable for developers.

James is the CEO and co-founder of Guild.ai, the control plane for AI agents where engineers build, reuse, and evolve intelligent software together.

Most recently, James was the Vice President of Engineering at Meta Devinfra, responsible for building and running the core developer tools, services, and platforms that power Meta's products. He and his team built Meta's first internal AI agent, which delivered immediate impact on how Meta engineers use AI tooling. During his time at Meta, James co-created Diem and served as Instagram's Head of Engineering.

With a 40-year career as a manager, entrepreneur, and technology developer, James has led numerous world-class engineering teams. At Yahoo, he served as Vice President of Engineering for Yahoo's media properties after the acquisition of Luminate, an interactive image technology company he founded. His previous roles include co-founder and SVP, Engineering, at Lightspark; CTO and founding team member at LiveOps; Senior Director of Engineering at Tellme (acquired by Microsoft); and Senior Director of Engineering at Netscape Communications, where he was responsible for the flagship Netscape browser. Before joining Netscape, James held engineering and management positions at Oracle and Borland International.

James Watters is the CTO of the Tanzu division at Broadcom Inc., a role he assumed in November 2023 following the company's acquisition. Previously At VMWare, he served as CTO of Modern Application Platforms. Watters was previously SVP of Product and Strategy at Pivotal Software, and a founding leader of the company.

Jared Jordan is a distinguished business and technology executive renowned for building products and platforms that have reached more than a billion users and
generated billions of dollars in growth. As Managing Vice President of the Capital One Garage, the innovation arm of Capital One Financial Services, he leads a team of 200
engineers, product managers, and designers focused on next-generation solutions in AI, developer platforms, and new product innovation across auto lending, refinancing, and servicing.

Across his career, Jared has consistently delivered measurable results. At Google, he led the launch of YouTube's Primetime channels and Live sports, including NFL Sunday Ticket, a move that drove 50 million new subscriptions and generated over $100 million
in new annual revenue. At Gmail, he guided the release of AI-powered features like "Help Me Write." Before Google, he engineered the platform strategy for account-sharing enforcement at Netflix, which unlocked tens of millions of new global subscriptions.

His leadership philosophy is grounded in three core principles: growth, efficiency, and people. Currently, Jared is pursuing an Executive MBA at Cornell University to further expand his business expertise and prepare for his next chapter as a general manager, exceptionally well-positioned to lead businesses that grow at scale.

Raised in Seattle and now based in Dallas, Jared is a first-generation engineer in his family. He and his wife Heather, his college sweetheart of 19 years, are raising three children and 2 Rhodesian Ridgeback dogs. He remains committed to investing in the next generation through open office hours, mentorship, and community service rooted in faith and family.

From Netflix to Google to Capital One, Jared Jordan’s career is a testament to innovation, measurable business impact, and a consistent focus on people as the
ultimate driver of growth.

I'm a technical lead at Meta and a distributed-systems specialist with 14 years of experience building infrastructure at global scale. I was a founding engineer and lead engineer on the Facebook Ordered Queueing Service(FOQS), Meta's distributed priority queue that scaled from thousands to trillions of tasks per day across Meta's products and AI systems. As an engineering manager, I went on to lead Meta's Functions-as-a-Service(FaaS) team, driving the strategy and reliability of the company's next-generation serverless compute platform. I now work at the intersection of large-scale distributed systems and AI.

Jason Stine is actually in no way related to Unsloth. He's just a passionate AI hobbyist who enjoys mentoring others and found that Unsloth Desktop was the most straightforward software for this workshop. He's a fullstack web developer (software engineer) who uses Cursor AI every day at work.

TL;DR Developer Advocate @ Snyk, co-author of O’Reilly’s "Learning HTTP/2” book, blogger & speaker. 

Javier Garza is a Technology evangelist that has written many articles on HTTP/2, security and web performance, and is the co-author of the O’Reilly Book “Learning HTTP/2” (https://amzn.to/2TJbpUU). Javier has spoken at more than 30 events around the world, including well-known conferences like Velocity, AWS Re:Invent, and PerfMatters and is the host of the "AI Security Engineers San Francisco Bay Area Chapter" (https://snyk.io/community/). His life’s motto is: share what you learn, and learn what you don’t. In his free time he enjoys challenging workouts and volunteering with different non-profits.

Jay Rodge is a developer advocate for Agents and large language models (LLMs), where he demonstrates how developers can leverage GPU acceleration in their agentic pipelines, using tools and frameworks that are widely used by the developer community.  Jay received his master’s degree in computer science from Illinois Tech, Chicago. Lee Faus Founder & CEO, Atomic Software, Co.
https://atomic.dev
Lee is the Founder and CEO of Atomic, a code intelligence platform rebuilding version control from the ground up for the software factory era. He bootstrapped Atomic through pre-seed, assembled the founding team, and led the company to v1, drawing on two decades of experience inside the infrastructure of how software gets built.
That experience includes engineering and go-to-market roles at Borland, Compuware, Red Hat, GitHub, and GitLab, as well as direct advisory work with engineering leaders at Fortune 100 and Global 2000 companies including State Farm, Pfizer, Wells Fargo, Travelport, and Nokia. Those tools and those organizations were the right answer for their era. But after years of watching enterprises strain under the weight of agent-driven development, the architectural gap became impossible to ignore. Git was designed in 2005 for humans editing text files one commit at a time. It was never built for what is coming next.
Atomic was built to replace it. Where legacy platforms bolt AI onto infrastructure designed for human-rate commits, Atomic starts from a different foundation: immutable changes, Merkle-bound policy, cryptographic attestation, and a decision ledger that tracks every input and output from intent to integrated code. The inner loop, where agents actually work, has no serious tooling today. That is the white space Atomic was built to own.
Lee speaks at international conferences on AI-native engineering, software supply chain integrity, and the architectural consequences of machine-rate development. His focus is practical: what engineering organizations actually need to govern, audit, and scale a software factory where agents generate the majority of code.

She likes JavaScript, Python, and working with AI. When not organizing or attending hackathons and meetups, she enjoys tennis, ping pong, and all things Disney.

Loris Degioanni is the founder and CTO of Sysdig and a pioneer in open source security. He created sysdig and Falco, the CNCF runtime security project, and was a core contributor to Wireshark, now used by over 20 million people worldwide. With a Ph.D. in computer engineering, Loris has spent his career building the tools developers rely on to understand and secure modern systems.

Luis Pujols is a Staff Customer Success Architect at GitHub, where he serves as a trusted technical advisor to some of GitHub's largest strategic customers, helping them turn AI-assisted, agentic development into a scaled team capability rather than a series of individual wins. His focus sits at the intersection of developer productivity and platform adoption strategy, helping engineering organizations make their repositories AI-ready and turn successful workflows into reusable, governed resources. Luis partners with technical leaders to drive adoption across the full software development lifecycle from CI/CD to security and GitHub Copilot, helping them define the governance guardrails that make agentic development safe and accountable at scale.

Maezza Romero, Community Manager at Romero Games, has 6 years of industry experience, managing large community spaces like the Romero Games Discord, now with 7,000 members. The company's Twitter, with over 10,000 followers, engages fans of legacy titles like DOOM and Quake through polls and Q&As. In 2024, Maezza adapts to the evolving social media landscape by using TikTok, Discord and Instagram, alongside Facebook and Twitter, to create content for dedicated Millennial and Gen-X fans.

Manfred Moser is an pen source coder, mentor, educator, and advocate, bringing a profound focus on software supply chain security to the open source world. A dedicated community leader and published author, his technical expertise spans decades as a software engineer and advocate. He has a deep, influential history with the Apache Maven ecosystem, including authoring prominent reference books, and is an active Trino maintainer, advocate, and podcast host. Manfred leverages his versatile background to drive technical excellence and foster collaboration across diverse developer communities.

Mang-Git is the CEO of Anvil. Used by Fortune 100 companies and growing startups, Anvil helps organizations transition knowledge and office work beyond paper and PDF. Earlier in his career, he held engineering roles at Dropbox, Dialpad, and Flexport.

Manish Kapur is a technical product leader with a strong background in product management, developer relations, marketing, and strategy. He is currently a VP of product marketing and DevRel at Sonar, based in Austin, Texas. He specializes in LLMs, AI coding tools, Agents, and Model Context Protocol (MCP), as well as cloud-native, Kubernetes, and DevSecOps, translating complex concepts into clear value for CTOs and developers alike.

Manjari Akella is a Software Engineer on Uber’s Developer Platform team. Since joining in 2018, her work has spanned multiple workstreams aimed at enhancing and modernizing developer experience and productivity at Uber. Her most significant achievements include contributing to the establishment of Go Monorepo, implementing improvements to Go libraries, optimizing artifact management, and merge queues.

Manu Gurudatha is a VP of Engineering at PagerDuty, where he drives the Incident Management, AIOps, CSOps, Status Pages that power PagerDuty's end-to-end customer journeys. 

Prior to PagerDuty, Manu led Engineering organizations in several companies, ranging from Series A startups to giants like Salesforce, where he led engineering for their Health Cloud unit. With his previous experiences, Manu has a proven track record of building strong products and platforms, sometimes from scratch and scaling those to sustain performance for thousands of customers.

He is based in the San Francisco Bay Area.

Mariane Bekker is the founder of Founders Bay, a community of 200,000 founders, executives, and investors built to bring more diversity into tech. She believes great ideas can come from anyone, and has created one of the most inclusive networks in the startup world.

Mariane also leads Developer Relations and Engineering at You.com, an AI-powered search platform, where she helps builders and developers get the most out of the product.

Mark Cavage is President of Docker. Over a 25-year career spanning AWS, Oracle, Heroku, Stripe, and Docker, he has moved from senior and principal engineer to engineering leader to business leader. That arc gives him a perspective few executives have: he has written the systems, led the teams building them, and run the businesses that depend on them. Today, Mark is leading Docker through the shift to agentic software development, helping more than 20 million developers give AI agents real autonomy while keeping control of their code, credentials, and infrastructure.

Mark Lechner is CISO at Docker, where he leads security across the platform millions of developers use to build, ship, and run software - including the agentic workloads reshaping modern engineering. Before Docker, he was CISO at DeepOpinion/Otera driving enterprise AI and LLM agentic security, CISO at Bitpanda scaling security through Europe's largest crypto platform, and Head of Cybersecurity at Solaris Bank. Before that he spent nearly a decade at Morgan Stanley in various security roles including the global leadership of security tooling. His focus today: supply chain integrity, agentic AI security, and secure-by-default developer platforms. He is based in Berlin.

Matan Grinberg is CEO and Co-Founder of Factory, the enterprise platform for autonomous software development with customers including NVIDIA, Adobe, Palo Alto Networks, EY, and Adyen. Before co-founding Factory, Matan studied string theory at Princeton and UC Berkeley.

Mathias (Matt) Biilmann is CEO of Netlify, a company he co-founded in 2014 and today is one of the fastest growing web development platforms. He has been building developer tools, content management systems and web infrastructure for more than 30 years and is recognized for coining the term “Jamstack.” An active participant in open source, Matt has contributed to well-known projects in more than a dozen languages at all layers of the stack. Matt grew up in Denmark, where he trained as a musician and music journalist.

Matt Burns is Director of Editorial at Insight Media Group, where he oversees The New Stack, Roadmap.sh, and Towards Data Science — three platforms that collectively help millions of developers figure out what to learn next. Previously, he spent 16 years at TechCrunch, leading editorial teams and events, hosting shows and pitch-offs, and interviewing newsmakers who shaped the world through technology and politics.

Matt Duchesne, AVP, Sales: Matt Duchesne leads GitLab's West Enterprise organization, working closely with many of the company's largest customers as they run mission-critical software delivery at scale. He specializes in connecting with GitLab customers to help them navigate the shift into the agentic era. Matt is focused on ensuring customers have the proper resources they need to build the workflows defining the next generation of how software is built.

I lead PwC’s Cloud, Engineering, Data, and AI platform, focused on helping organizations turn
technology investment into real, lasting business outcomes. I’m part of PwC’s Consulting and
Technology leadership teams, where industry expertise and engineering capability come
together to solve complex, enterprise-scale challenges.
Additionally, I serve on PwC’s global Cloud, Engineering, Data, and AI leadership team, helping
shape a consistent client experience worldwide. I also act as an executive sponsor for PwC’s
strategic Cloud and AI alliance relationships, working closely with partners to bring
differentiated solutions to market.
I’ve spent more than 20 years at PwC, most recently leading the creation of the firm’s Microsoft
business after leading the Digital Transformation and Innovation Practice for the Technology,
Media, and Telecommunications Sector. My approach is practical and execution-oriented, with
a focus on growth, technology, and change that actually delivers.
Outside of work, I enjoy experimenting with emerging technologies with my two sons and wake
surfing with my wife.
speakers.company_position: US and Global Head of Cloud, Engineering, Data, and AI

speakers.bio: Matt Wyman is the CEO and co-founder of Okareo, the platform for testing, evaluating, and monitoring Voice AI agents — using synthetic user simulation to find the edges of agent behavior before customers do. A career-long builder of developer and testing tools, Matt was previously Chief Product Officer and Chief Customer Officer at Sauce Labs, the leader in continuous web and mobile app testing, and VP of Product at CircleCI, where he helped define modern CI/CD practices. His earlier roles include product leadership at Xtime and CoreLogic, and he founded two startups, RealiD and ConnectingVoices. That blend of shipping developer platforms and obsessing over quality at scale led him to co-found Okareo in 2023, tackling the hardest reliability problem in AI today: real-time voice agents facing real human behavior. Matt holds degrees in Computer Science and Cultural Anthropology from UC Berkeley — a pairing that turns out to be exactly right for teaching machines to talk to people.

Meghna Shah is a Principal in PwC’s Engineering and AI practice and a technology leader with over 18 years of experience designing, building, and scaling enterprise and customer-facing products.
She advises senior technology and business leaders on translating strategy into execution, leading cross-functional teams of engineers, architects, product managers, and designers to deliver modern platforms and solutions. Her experience spans product and platform strategy, architecture, and agile delivery, with a focus on applying emerging technologies, including AI, to solve complex business and customer challenges.
Meghna works with organizations to modernize technology foundations, evolve operating
models, and drive measurable outcomes through disciplined engineering. She is particularly
focused on how enterprises can scale AI responsibly, with strong governance and human
oversight. She holds a Master’s degree in Information Systems Management from Carnegie Mellon University and a Bachelor’s degree.

Meredith Eisen is a product management leader with expertise in software security, AI-driven automation, and DevSecOps. As Sr. Director of Product Management at Sonatype, she drives innovation in software supply chain security, helping organizations build secure, high-quality applications at scale. With a background in FinTech, digital transformation and enterprise product strategy, she is passionate about enabling developers with proactive security solutions.

Michael Angelo Rivera (Yes, like the ninja turtle) currently leads a team on GitLab Orbit (aka the GitLab Knowledge Graph) to bring better context to agents.
He is a self-starter at heart and is passionate about creating effective workspaces, improving the status quo, and being a good team player. He is interested in all things related to software engineering, building new products, coffee, and pizza.

Michael Irwin has worked with containers since 2016, as a meetup organizer, platform architect, and Docker Captain, and joined Docker in 2022, where he works in developer relations. He builds the labs, workshops, and demos behind Docker's tooling, and teaches university courses on containers.

Co-founder at Second State. Author of 5 books on software development. PhD in astrophysics. Docker Captain.

Agentic engineer by day, vibe coder by night. Open-source AI & Rust. Maker of the vibe keyboard: https://vibekeys.dev

Most cloud engineers don't begin with a PhD in history. Michal did. In 2009, he traded archives for networking and spent the next decade designing and operating enterprise networks, working with routers, switches, firewalls, and load balancers - up to 2021 when he decided he had spent enough time with packets and moved into AWS cloud engineering, where he works mostly on cloud security, containers and AI topics.
Since 2023 Michal is an AWS Community Builder (Containers) and in same year he founded the AWS User Group Košice, Slovakia. He also holds the AWS Golden Jacket and is a frequent speaker at technology conferences.
https://michalsalanci.com

Mike Chambers is a Senior AI specialist DA at AWS. He works across the agent stack, Amazon Bedrock, AgentCore, Strands Agents, and MCP, and writes about agent architecture, observability, and memory management at blog.mikegchambers.com. He builds agent systems in the open. His mcp-lambda-handler is pip installed 35k+ per month. Based in Brisbane Australia, Mike travels the world to connect with the AI community.

Milin Desai currently serves as the CEO of Sentry. Used by more than 4 million developers and 150,000 organizations worldwide, Sentry helps every developer detect, understand, and fix broken code, fast. Milin joined Sentry from VMware where he helped build out multiple lines of business from networking (0->1b+) to multi cloud (0->100M+ SAAS). Earlier in his career, he held engineering and product roles at Veritas and Riverbed.

Mirela Viersa is a Customer Innovation professional at SAP with 10+ years of experience in innovation, technology, and customer transformation. She focuses on AI, human-centered innovation, and helping organizations turn emerging technologies into impactful solutions.

Mitesh Patel is a developer advocate manager at NVIDIA. His team is responsible for creating workflows to showcase how developers can harness GPU acceleration in their workflows using tools and frameworks popular in the developer community. Before NVIDIA, he was a senior research scientist at Fuji Xerox Palo Alto Laboratory Inc. (a research subsidiary of Fuji Xerox), where he worked on developing indoor localization technologies for applications such as asset tracking in hospitals and delivery cart tracking in manufacturing facilities. Mitesh received his Ph.D. in Robotics from the Center of Autonomous Systems (CAS) at the University of Technology Sydney, Australia in 2014.

Monica Sarbu is the founder and CEO of Xata, an agent-native Postgres platform built for the AI era. As AI agents become first-class users of data infrastructure, Xata enables teams to safely branch production databases in seconds, give every workflow its own isolated Postgres environment, and scale without multiplying cost or risk.

Xata is backed by Index Ventures and prominent technology founders including the creators of Elastic, Confluent, Vercel, and Netlify.

Before Xata, Monica founded Packetbeat, an open-source monitoring solution acquired by Elastic in 2015. It evolved into Elastic Beats, one of the most widely adopted observability ecosystems in the world.

She also founded [Tupu.io](http://tupu.io/), a nonprofit providing free mentorship for underrepresented people entering tech. When not rethinking databases, she enjoys traveling and exploring the world with her daughter.

Morgan Helton is a software engineer at Flox, working on cloud infrastructure and systems reliability. With prior experience in industrial controls and instrumentation and two decades of Linux and open-source use, Morgan blends practical engineering discipline with modern cloud-native practices.

Moritz Plassnig is the Chief Executive Officer of CloudBees. Moritz is an entrepreneur, technologist, and product leader with deep expertise in developer tools, software delivery, and data governance. He co-founded Codeship, a cloud-based CI/CD platform that was acquired by CloudBees in 2018. Following the acquisition, he held several senior roles at CloudBees, including SVP of Operations & Corporate Development and GM of the company’s cloud/SaaS business.

Most recently, Moritz served as Chief Product Officer at Immuta, where he scaled the company’s data security and governance business, overseeing product and go-to-market strategy across engineering, product management, customer success, and marketing. He is also an angel investor in developer, data, and security startups, including Ona, an AI-native developer environment platform, and DX, a developer intelligence platforms, and served on the board of CloudSkiff prior to its acquisition by Snyk.

Moritz is based in Boulder, Colorado with his family.

With over 15 years in technology spanning software engineering, data engineering, and cybersecurity leadership, I bring a unique cross-functional perspective to building secure, scalable systems that actually work in enterprise environments. Over the past five years in cybersecurity, I've focused on application security posture management and helping organizations scale security practices without slowing down development velocity.

Neel Sundaresan is General Manager of AI Products and Productivity Tools at IBM. Before joining IBM, he served as Vice President of Data & AI at Microsoft, where he led several data and cloud productivity initiatives and played a key role in integrating AI into these tools. He is the creator of Bob, IBM’s AI software development partner. He pioneered the concepts of “Code as Data” and “Teaching Machines to Code,” land created Microsoft’s first AI code assistant, Intellicode which evolved into GitHub Copilot.He was instrumental in bringing key AI techniques and innovations into the product. Earlier in his career, Neel headed eBay Research and Data Labs, driving advancements in search, recommender systems, computer vision, economics, human-computer interaction, and distributed computing. He began his career at IBM’s Almaden Research Center, where he developed IBM’s first search engine and contributed to foundational work in web mining and XML systems. A frequent speaker at international conferences, Neel holds over 320 patents and has published more than 150 research papers. He earned his Ph.D. in Computer Science from Indiana University Bloomington and is an alumnus of the Indian Institute of Technology, Bombay.

Nemanja was born in Serbia in 1994 and moved to Canada in 2021, although he still likes European environment much more than the North American. He's been a mobile developer his whole career. His first job was in 2014 as a native Android app developer. In summer of 2016 he was given a chance to learn Swift and native iOS app development that he excitedly accepted. Finally, in December 2018, only a couple of weeks after v1.0 was launched he embarked on a Flutter journey and is still sailing fearlessly.

Nicholas Muy is the VP Engineering - Platform and Security and CISO at Scrut.io, where he leads securing agentic infra, and tackling crazy problems. In his free-time, he's a Venture Partner at Tidal Ventures and Syndicate Co-Lead at Venture in Security, he loves working with friends/founders building and solving problems. Previously a security engineering at Expedia Group and cybersecurity strategy at the U.S. Department of Homeland Security.

Nikhil Gandhi is the Senior Vice President of Engineering for Yahoo Mail, where he oversees global engineering, product, and design for one of the world’s largest consumer communication platforms. He oversees a global team, leading technical strategy and execution across core messaging infrastructure, AI-driven experiences, spam and safety systems, and platform modernization, while driving user growth, engagement, and monetization. His organization also supports critical priorities including privacy, data governance, security, and global infrastructure at scale.

Prior to Yahoo, Nikhil was Head of Engineering for Ads Platform at TikTok, responsible for monetization systems powering a significant share of revenue, including creator tools and in-app commerce. He previously held leadership roles at Meta, scaling the Ads Experience organization globally, and spent a decade at Apple helping grow the Apple Online Store into a multi–tens of billions business while leading global engineering for Apple.com. A deeply technical leader, he combines strong product and platform instincts with a track record of building high-performing global teams and delivering complex systems at scale.

I am a software engineer and technical leader specializing in large-scale mobile infrastructure, iOS architecture, performance optimization, and privacy-sensitive client-side systems. Over the past decade, I have worked across global technology companies and major financial institutions, building systems that support products used by millions — and in some cases billions — of people.

At Meta, I work on Instagram’s iOS infrastructure, focusing on application responsiveness, startup performance, rendering efficiency, network data handling, and scalable experimentation. My work involves leading complex cross-functional initiatives across engineering, product, machine learning, analytics, legal, and privacy teams, turning ambiguous business and technical challenges into reliable systems shipped at global scale.

Earlier, at Meta Audience Network, I worked on monetization infrastructure for video and playable ads and helped design privacy-compliant architectures in response to major platform and regulatory shifts, including GDPR and Apple’s tracking changes. Before that, I led mobile architecture initiatives at T-Bank, including the Faster Payments System integration, server-driven UI platforms, media delivery infrastructure, and modernization of core mobile architecture. I also led the iOS department at Vivid Money, where I managed an organization of about 20 engineers and introduced engineering practices adopted across the company.

In my talks, I focus on practical engineering lessons from building, scaling, and optimizing mobile systems in high-impact environments.

Nitin Eusebius is a Principal Solutions Architect and Generative AI Tech Lead at Amazon Web Services (AWS) with over 20 years of experience in enterprise technology, cloud architecture, and large-scale digital platforms. He specializes in AI Engineering, Generative and Agentic AI, helping organizations design secure, resilient, and production-ready systems. He designs production-scale AI systems and helps organizations move AI initiatives from experimentation to scalable, real-world deployment, aligning AI capabilities with modern engineering and delivery practices. Nitin has led complex modernization and transformation programs, advised executive stakeholders, and driven architectural strategies across cloud-native, hybrid, and distributed environments. He actively leads field initiatives, contributes to thought leadership and blogs, and publishes on AWS official channels and community platforms. Nitin holds all AWS Certifications and 4 NVIDIA Generative AI certifications and is a frequent speaker at AWS re:Invent, re:Inforce, NVIDIA GTC, AI Dev Summit, and global AWS Summits.

Oleg Šelajev is a developer advocate at Docker working on AI,developer productivity, Testcontainers. Developer. Author. Speaker. Java Champion, Microsoft MVP, Docker captain. 

Loves all languages.

Olivier Lacombe is a Director of Product Management at Google DeepMind. He specializes in Gemini Serving, Pre-training, Edge Computing and Open Models. He led the launch of Gemma 4 under an Apache 2.0 license. Lacombe has held leadership roles at X (the moonshot factory) and Android Intelligence during his tenure at Google. He focuses on scaling machine learning technologies server-side and at the edge and has full-cycle experience with model development.

Oren is a seasoned IT executive with over 20 years of leadership across enterprise and financial sectors, now serving as Global Field CTO in the Tanzu division. A long-time platform advocate, he’s helped organizations navigate the evolution from Cloud Foundry to Kubernetes and now toward AI-native platforms. Oren is a recognised expert, author, and frequent speaker at VMware events, sharing insights drawn from real-world platform transformations at scale.

Paige Bailey is a Member of the Technical Staff for the Developer Experience team at Google DeepMind, specializing in the AI for software development domain. Prior to returning to Alphabet, Paige spent just over a year working on machine learning and MLOps at GitHub, and in the Microsoft Developer Tools Division (DevDiv). As a former applied machine learning engineer, she is passionate about using machine learning to improve developer productivity and accelerate the creative process.

Pamela Fox is a developer advocate at Microsoft, where she helps developers use Python with Azure, Microsoft Foundry, VS Code, and GitHub. Before Microsoft, she was one of the first engineers at Coursera, early DevRel at Google, lecturer at UC Berkeley of the largest CS class, and the creator of the Khan Academy programming courses.

Paul Anthony Claxton is a Marine veteran, entrepreneur, and venture capital allocator. He built companies without institutional backing before transitioning into venture investing, bringing an operator’s perspective to capital allocation. He developed the Reloadable Note™, a proprietary financing instrument, and focuses on backing founders building structurally durable, long-term companies. Paul also publishes a Weekly newsletter sharing his ideas, insights & experiences as an AI Venture Capitalist to empower & inspire his followers.

Paul Zimmerman is a Developer Advocate at Uber, working on the open-source Michelangelo machine learning platform. Before joining Uber, Paul led developer advocacy, community engagement, technical content, and open-source collaboration programs at Cisco. His work focuses on making complex platforms more approachable and helping technical audiences implement their ideas.

Paweł Matynia has over 10 years of experience in Quality Assurance and Test Automation. Currently, he works as a Senior Advanced Software Engineer at Honeywell Aerospace, where he focuses on delivering business value through efficient, reliable, and scalable automation solutions. Passionate about continuous improvement, Paweł strives to bridge the gap between technology and people, sharing best practices and insights on quality, automation, and process excellence.

Peter Farkas is a seasoned open source leader with over 15 years of experience building sustainable open source projects and businesses. He currently serves as the CEO of Percona, a global leader in open source database software and services.
Before joining Percona, Peter was the Co-Founder and CEO of FerretDB, the truly open source MongoDB alternative that enables developers to use MongoDB drivers seamlessly with PostgreSQL as the backend.

Peter is a strong advocate for open source solutions, believing that they can drive innovation and sustainable growth on par with-or beyond-proprietary software.

I’m a Principal Software Engineer at Mastercard with 18 years of experience across software engineering, data analytics, distributed and large-scale systems. I’ve built and optimized software architectures globally in payments, banking, telecom and manufacturing, worked across multiple countries, and mentored engineers and organizations. I explore AI, Payments, HPC, and emerging technologies to create systems that are scalable, high-performance, efficient, reliable and importantly secure systems.

Phil Conway is a Dev Advocate at SandboxAQ, a Google-originated startup focused on solving problems through the application of Quantum & AI-based technologies. 

He has nearly two decades of experience covering networking, security, cloud computing and solutions architecture for global organizations, financial institutions and government departments.

Philip Kiely is the author of Inference Engineering and is an early employee at Baseten. Outside of work, you'll find Philip practicing martial arts, reading a new book, or cheering for his adopted SF sports teams.

Phoebe Wang is a software engineer working on ML infrastructure at OpenAI. Her work focuses on the systems layer behind production AI, including reliability, evaluation, and infrastructure for machine learning workflows.

Her research background spans human-centered machine learning, fairness in predictive systems, explainable AI, and semantic anomaly detection. Her published work includes CHI research on stakeholder fairness notions in predictive systems, and her Google Scholar profile has 100+ citations.

Ex-Google, Colossus TL - multi-purpose storage foundations, got to work on most of its different parts.
Ebpf-based live cloud debugger for compiled languages, first at startup, then at Datadog.
Now storage lead at Blacksmith.
Doing data-driven optimizations whenever I find opportunity.

Prasanna Balaprakash is co-founder and CEO of PrimaLabs, where he leads the development of workload-aware AI inference systems that improve performance, reliability, energy efficiency, and cost for production AI applications. Previously, he was Director of AI Programs and a Distinguished R&D Scientist at Oak Ridge National Laboratory, where he co-led an AI initiative focused on secure, trustworthy, and efficient AI for scientific discovery, experimental facilities, and national security. He also served as the AI lead for several U.S. Department of Energy projects. Before joining Oak Ridge, Prasanna held multiple research and leadership positions at Argonne National Laboratory, progressing from postdoctoral researcher to R&D Group Leader in the Mathematics and Computer Science Division, with a joint appointment at the Argonne Leadership Computing Facility. Earlier in his career, he served as Chief Technology Officer at Mentis SA in Brussels.
His work spans artificial intelligence, machine learning, optimization, GPU systems, benchmarking, and high-performance computing. He received the DOE Early Career Award in 2018 and earned his PhD from the CoDE-IRIDIA AI Lab at Université Libre de Bruxelles, supported by Marie Skłodowska-Curie and F.R.S.-FNRS fellowships.

Prashanth Chandrasekar is Chief Executive Officer of Stack Overflow and is responsible for driving Stack Overflow’s overall strategic direction and results.

Prashanth is a proven technology executive with extensive experience leading and scaling high-growth global organizations. Previously, he served as Senior Vice President & General Manager of Rackspace’s Cloud & Infrastructure Services portfolio of businesses, including the Managed Public Clouds, Private Clouds, Colocation and Managed Security businesses.

Before that, Prashanth held a range of senior leadership roles at Rackspace including Senior Vice President & General Manager of Rackspace’s high growth, global business focused on the world’s leading Public Clouds including Amazon Web Services (AWS), Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud Platform (GCP) and Alibaba Cloud, which became the fastest growing business in Rackspace’s history.

Prior to joining Rackspace, Prashanth was a Vice President at Barclays Investment Bank, focused on providing Strategic and Mergers & Acquisitions (M&A) advice for clients in the Technology, Media and Telecom (TMT) industries. Prashanth was also a Manager at Capgemini Consulting where he managed Operations transformation engagements and consulting teams across the US. He holds an MBA from Harvard Business School, an M.Eng in Engineering Management from Cornell University and a B.S. in Computer Engineering (summa cum laude) from the University of Maine.

Prashanth is married and has two children.

With over 12 years of experience in the software industry, I specialize in architecting secure and high-performance systems for the Smart TV ecosystem. Currently, I focus on the development of on-device subscription and payment infrastructures, managing the delicate balance between seamless UI performance and rigorous security standards. My work centers on building robust SDK APIs that power global consumer platforms, ensuring that every transaction is not only performant but also compliant with evolving global privacy and security regulations. I am passionate about solving the engineering constraints unique to embedded consumer devices while maintaining a world-class developer experience.

Preetam Dwivedi is a Staff Engineer on Uber’s Developer Platform team, where he leads the core systems that power code collaboration, including code hosting, code review, merge queues, and artifact management. With a background in distributed systems, he focuses on scaling developer workflows and improving the reliability and productivity of large engineering organizations.

Prince Kohli is a distinguished technology executive and visionary leader with three
decades of experience in building, scaling, and transforming solutions across critical
sectors, including enterprise software, cloud computing, telecoms, and security.

As the current Chief Executive Officer of Sauce Labs, he spearheads an AI-driven end-
to-end continuous quality platform trusted by a distinguished list of large enterprise clients. For the past decade, Mr. Kohli's focus has been at the forefront of Artificial Intelligence platforms, including the development of one of the industry's first agentic platforms.

Throughout his career, he has cultivated a strong reputation for operational excellence
and for building high-performing, globally distributed teams within companies of all sizes, from startups to large enterprises. His entrepreneurial background includes co-founding a successful, VC-backed company. 

Committed to responsible innovation, he is also a valued member of the Ethical AI Governance Group, collaborating with practitioners who share similar values.

Mr. Kohli holds a Ph.D. in Computer Science from the Georgia Institute of Technology and
a Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science and Engineering from the Indian Institute of
Technology (IIT), New Delhi, India.

Founder of  Cloud Girl, former executive at Microsoft. As
Sr. Director at Microsoft leading GitHub Copilot & AI-SDLC strategy across Fortune 100 enterprises. Former Head of North America Developer Advocacy at Google Cloud launched Gemini Code Assist at Cloud Next '23 alongside the CEO, and ran the global hackathon program across 60+ countries. Author of two O'Reilly bestsellers. Faculty at UPenn. TED speaker. 350K+ community across platforms.

Radostina (Ina) Tsvetkova was recognized as one of Norway’s top 50 women in Tech in 2026. Ina is a Senior Advisor in Digital Accessibility and Inclusive Design at the Norwegian Directorate of Labour and Welfare (NAV). She is an Invited Expert in the W3C Accessibility Guidelines Working Group, a PhD candidate in Computer Science, a Certified Professional in Web Accessibility (CPWA), a DHS Trusted Tester, and an ISTQB Advanced Level Test Manager and Test Analyst.

Ina provides guidance on digital accessibility throughout the product development lifecycle, from early planning and design through development, testing, and procurement. She has also participated in the development of Norwegian and European accessibility standards.

Ina is a passionate advocate for an accessible and inclusive world for all, regardless of ability. 

She enjoys sharing knowledge and engaging others and has presented at conferences including CSUN 2026, Agile Testing Days 2025, a11yCamp 2025, a11yTO 2025, M-Enabling 2025, BdKCSE 2025, Social Media Days 2025, Web4All 2025, EuroSTAR 2024, Odin 2023, and Mangfold i Mai (Diversity in May) 2023 and 2025.

Rahul Deshpande is the executive vice president and global head of Research and Development and the Services Enablement and Transformation (SET) team at Mastercard. Global R&D pioneers’ new products and services, tackles complex challenges, and unlocks opportunities through emerging technologies bringing transformative value to consumers, businesses and governments worldwide. The SET organization strengthens Mastercard’s delivery excellence by modernizing cross-functional
operating models and enabling scalable, repeatable ways of working across Services and R&D, ensuring that innovation moves from concept to customer value with clarity, quality and measurable impact.

Previously, Rahul served as the chief technology officer at Ethoca, a Mastercard company. He was instrumental in developing solutions capable of preventing chargebacks, combating friendly fraud, and enhancing digital customer experiences through real-time, data-based collaboration. Rahul first joined Mastercard in 2014 and held several positions, including senior vice president of Digital Strategy and vice president of Engineering and R&D.

Prior to Mastercard, Rahul held leadership positions across Fortune 500 logistics, supply chain, consulting and technology firms. His contributions in these roles include the development of award- winning applications, intelligent pricing engines and efficient supply-chain networks.

As an engineer with a background in industrial electronics, Rahul holds a Master of Business Administration from Washington University in St. Louis, as well as a master’s degree in Computer
Science with a specialization in artificial intelligence and genetic programming. Rahul is based in St. Louis and serves on the board of directors for the St. Louis Children’s Museum. In 2022, he was named Executive of the Year by the Asian American Chamber of Commerce.

speakers.bio: Rahul Pandita is a researcher on the Code|AI team at Microsoft, where he works on the intelligence behind GitHub Copilot. He has led research and engineering across AI-assisted development(from Copilot Voice and Copilot Workspace to agentic compute environments). His work sits at the intersection of program analysis, HCI, cognitive science, and applied ML, all in service of making AI coding tools that work for developers. Rahul holds a PhD in Computer Science from NC State, focused on automated software engineering and developer productivity. He occasionally blogs at https://rahulpandita.me/

I am a Senior Vice President of Software Engineering at JPMorgan Chase, specializing in enterprise-scale cloud platforms, distributed systems, and AI-enabled infrastructure. I lead and contribute to the design of secure, scalable, and highly resilient cloud-native architectures supporting mission-critical financial systems.

My expertise spans AWS, Kubernetes, platform engineering, DevOps, and Site Reliability Engineering, with a strong focus on building self-service infrastructure platforms and enabling large engineering organizations to operate at scale. I work extensively on multi-account cloud architectures, infrastructure automation, reliability engineering, and integrating AI and machine learning workloads into modern cloud environments.

Over the past decade, I have focused on designing high-performance systems that improve scalability, operational efficiency, and platform reliability in complex enterprise environments. I am passionate about advancing cloud architecture standards, mentoring engineers, evaluating innovative technology solutions, and contributing to the broader technology community through speaking, technical publications, and industry judging initiatives.

Rajat is a Staff Software Engineer at Netflix, leading the technical architecture for the global ML Model Serving Infrastructure. With nearly a decade at Netflix and Amazon, he has specialized in building highly available distributed systems and stable, usable ML platforms that power personalization, search, and commerce at scale. A recipient of Amazon’s prestigious "Just Do It" Award from Jeff Bezos for his bias for action, Rajat excels at abstracting the complexities of distributed computing to drive developer velocity and platform reliability. He holds a Master's in Computer Science from North Carolina State University, and has spent his career applying that foundation to massive-scale infrastructure challenges.

Rajesh Agadi is a Principal Architect at Google Cloud leading Strategic AI customers. Serving as a Strategic Advisor to executive teams, he guides global organizations to design, build, and modernize their cloud infrastructure with AI-driven innovation at planet-scale.

Raju Dandigam is an accomplished Engineering Manager and Staff Engineer with over 15 years of experience, evolving from a front-end developer to a strategic technology leader. He drives business growth through innovative front-end architecture, full-stack team leadership, and results-oriented project execution. With deep expertise in JavaScript frameworks—including React, Angular, and Node.js—Raju has successfully led large-scale, cross-functional initiatives such as AI-powered trip planners, rewards platforms, and automation frameworks that significantly improved platform stability and reduced manual QA efforts.

Beyond his technical leadership, Raju is a passionate advocate for knowledge sharing. He has authored numerous technical articles on JavaScript, React, Angular, Node.js, and Cypress, featured on platforms like SitePoint, HackerNoon, Tutorialspoint, Medium, DZone, and Dev.to. He is also an active contributor to the tech community, having served as a judge for prestigious industry recognitions, including the Globee Awards, Business Intelligence Group, IAA Committee, SWE Awards, and Dev.to innovation challenges.

In 2025, Raju was invited to speak at the International JavaScript Conference (iJS) and CypressConf, where he presented deep dives on front-end scalability and modern testing architectures.

Ranjan Parthasarathy is CEO and co-founder of Axiomstudio.ai, where he is building enterprise-grade AI platforms for governed software development, agent orchestration, and AI adoption at scale. He previously served as Chief Product and Technology Officer at Apica and was founder and CEO of LOGIQ.AI, his second technology company to be acquired. Ranjan’s work spans AI, DevOps, ITOps, observability, data platforms, and enterprise automation, with a focus on helping engineering and operations teams build faster without compromising governance, security, or reliability. He holds an  MS degree from Stanford University and is based in the San Francisco Bay Area.

Raphael Manke is a full-stack developer many years of experience in developing serverless applications in the AWS cloud. At Dash0 he is responsible for integrating AWS telemtry data into the platform.

Ratul Ghosh is the Tech Lead and Architect for the Intuit Accountant Suite, an AI-native platform powered by Intuit Intelligence. Previously, he designed and led the development of GenOrchestrator, the core engine of Intuit’s GenOS platform, and successfully launched Intuit's Prompt Management and Agentic Starter Kit. Prior to GenOS, Ratul architected CoreAI and built the Feature Management Platform from the ground up. He brings extensive end-to-end experience across data engineering, MLE, platform engineering, and product engineering.

speakers.bio:
Ravi Belani is the Chairman and Founder of the Alchemist Accelerator, a venture-backed accelerator for enterprise startups. Ravi is also a Lecturer of Entrepreneurship at Stanford University, where he is a board advisor to Stanford's Entrepreneurship Center in the Engineering School and co-chairs the Education & Curriculum Subcommittee.


Ravi has been the first institutional investor in 7 unicorns (including LaunchDarkly, Rigetti, Onebrief, PubMatic) and the second institutional investor in one decacorn (Twitch).


Ravi formerly spent six years as part of the investment team at Draper Fisher Jurvetson's Menlo Park global headquarters.


Ravi formerly worked in product management at two Kleiner Perkins enterprise startups and as a consultant in McKinsey and Company's San Francisco office. Ravi is a Phi Beta Kappa and Tau Beta Pi graduate of Stanford University, holding a BS with Distinction and MS in Industrial Engineering. Ravi also holds an MBA from Harvard Business School.

Ravi Sastry Kadali is an Engineering Leader with two decades of progressive engineering leadership spanning defense, enterprise, and hyperscale systems. He built platform integrity systems at Meta protecting 3B+ users, engineered Windows platform releases at Microsoft, designed intrusion detection systems at India's Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO), hardened API security infrastructure at Neustar Security Services, and delivered edge-security and networking solutions at Volterra (acquired by F5) and X Corp.

A passionate Go ecosystem contributor, Ravi has accepted patches in the Go project (golang/go), Kubernetes, etcd, gosec, gocloak, semgrep, gqlgen, OWASP ZAP, and Aqua Security's Trivy. He is the creator of go-safeinput  - a unified injection defense library addressing MITRE CWE Top 25 - and SecurePrompt, a pre-flight AI prompt security scanner. He is a co-editor of security engineering technical papers and a recurring invited panelist at cybersecurity events.

At WeAreDevelopers, Ravi Sastry brings a rare blend of hands-on open-source craft and battle-tested security expertise earned protecting billions of users at the world's largest platforms.

Richard Rizk is Co-Founder and CTO of BLACKBOX AI — and the pioneer behind the only end-to-end encrypted inference technology available today.

He built Encrypted Model: client-sealed AI inference where prompts are encrypted on the user’s device and decrypted only inside an attested GPU enclave. The proxy, the host, and the operator never hold the key. AES-256-GCM. ECDH P-384. Hardware attestation before secrets move. True end-to-end encryption for AI inference and agentic workloads — the Signal standard, applied to the model hop.

Where others stop at TLS or trust the gateway, Richard’s stack answers a harder question: can anything except you and the attested enclave read the prompt at all?

At WeAreDevelopers World Congress North America, he joins leaders from Sentry, Render, and Cognition on the mainstage to discuss what it takes to run AI-written software in production — at speed, and without surrendering the prompts that built it.

Richard is Chief Evangelist at Unqork, where he leads the development of solutions that showcase the full power of the Unqork platform. Previously, he led Financial Services and Insurance Solutions at Conga. Before that, Richard held senior roles in solution delivery, including Head of Integrated Solutions at S&P Global Market Intelligence, where he drove transformational initiatives for strategic accounts.

Rishab is a Staff Developer Evangelist at Twilio, part-time cloud professor at St. Lawrence College, co-author of Learn to Cloud, AWS Community Builder, and a Microsoft MVP. He is passionate about helping people get into cloud and sharing his learnings from his time in cloud, DevOps and now DevRel.

Rocky Warren is a Senior Staff Software Engineer at Clipboard, where he leads AI strategy and software delivery for marketplace products across healthcare, education, and hospitality staffing. He works on developer productivity, testing reliability, and AI-enabled engineering workflows. His current focus is making coding agents useful in real production systems by improving the verification, observability, and review loops around agent-authored code.

Ron Veen is a seasoned software engineer with extensive experience ranging from Microservices to mainframes. His passion for software engineering and architecture has been his guiding force throughout his career. With over 20 years of expertise in the JVM and the Java ecosystem, Ron is an Oracle Certified Java Programmer (OCP) and a certified Sun Business Component Developer (SCBCD/OCPBCD). 

A dedicated Java enthusiast, Ron also has a keen interest in alternative JVM languages, particularly Kotlin. At Team Rockstars IT, he serves as a Special Agent and lead developer, frequently speaking at international conferences. Ron is the author of books on Java Cloud-native migrations with Jakarta EE and on Virtual Threads, Structured Concurrency, and Scoped Values. He has also co-written a book on Kotlin.

Rukmini Reddy is the Senior Vice President of Engineering, responsible for managing product and platform delivery, infrastructure and data science. Reddy joined PagerDuty from Slack where she guided the vision, strategy and execution of a comprehensive re-architecture, transforming the messaging software into an automation platform that empowered users to streamline their work.

Additionally, Rukmini spent over a decade in senior executive roles at various enterprise companies, where she built a strong track record for driving engineering and product strategy during periods of hyper-growth and product transformation across SaaS, B2B and B2C businesses.

Rukmini has a master of science degree in computer engineering from the University of Arkansas and earned a bachelor’s degree from Osmania University in computer science and engineering.

Experienced Software Engineer | Architect | Keynote & Public Speaker | Java Champion | Google Developer Expert for Cloud | Docker Captain | Oracle ACE Pro | Community Leader | Mentor | Ex-leader of JavaZone and Norwegian JUG – javaBin.

Dr. Ryan Ries is a renowned AI and data scientist with more than 15 years of leadership experience in data and engineering at fast-scaling technology companies. Dr. Ries holds over 20 years of experience working with AI and 7+ years helping customers build their AWS data infrastructure and AI models.

After earning his Ph.D. in Biophysical Chemistry at UCLA and Caltech, Dr. Ries has helped develop cutting-edge data solutions for the U.S. Department of Defense and a myriad of Fortune 500 companies. As Chief AI and Data Scientist for Mission, a CDW company, Ryan has built out a successful team of Data Engineers, Data Architects, ML Engineers and Data Scientists to solve some of the hardest problems in the world utilizing AWS infrastructure.

I am a Senior Java Developer with over 14 years of hands-on experience in the trenches of enterprise software. Currently a full-time engineer at eBay, I spend my days solving scalability and reliability challenges for financial systems that serve millions of users.

My technical journey has focused on high-stakes environments, including migrating 192M+ sellers to next-generation billing platforms and designing APIs that handle 80M+ daily requests. I specialize in the intersection of Java, Spring Boot, and Azure.

After more than a decade of focusing on execution and architecture, I am now dedicated to sharing my "war stories" and technical insights with the broader developer community. My goal is to help other engineers navigate the complexities of modernizing legacy systems and building at scale.

Sachin Kaura is Vice President and Chief Architect for AI Research, Experimentation and Evaluation at SAP Business AI. He leads the architecture and evaluation of agentic AI systems, translating emerging research into secure and reliable enterprise products and SAP Ecosystem. As the founder of SAP Joule for Consultants, he has brought generative AI grounded in trusted enterprise knowledge to SAP's consulting ecosystem. His work focuses on making enterprise software ready for AI agents by addressing identity, permissions, APIs, business context, orchestration, observability and governance. This enables AI agents to safely complete complex tasks across business systems and deliver measurable business value.

Previously he did ML infra at Etsy and helped build the next-gen DNS at Microsoft. He's been writing technical deep-dives for freeCodeCamp and HackerNoon since before it was a growth hack, holds an MS from USC, and is @edorado93 everywhere. Ask him about fixing prod from a bar.

Sagi Rodin is a seasoned technology leader dedicated to helping SaaS companies scale faster. Saloni Garg is a Senior Machine Learning Engineer at Adobe, where she specializes in AI and machine learning. She is also a recognized author in the field, with a forthcoming book on Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to be published by De Gruyter later this year.
